issues.title: decoder should wait on transpose
Master-replica partial synchronization doesn't work when mutating queries start with parameter
issues.body:
In our setup we have master and replica. When we mutate the data on the master node with a parametreless query, such as:

```
GRAPH.QUERY "default:diagrams" "CREATE (:TestNode {id: 'test-node-static-11223', type: 'static'})"
```

We see how this query is repeated on replica as-is (I use `monitor` command in redis-cli to observe this).

However, if the query starts with `CYPHER ` contains a parameter, such as:

```
GRAPH.QUERY "default:diagrams" "CYPHER id='test-node-987161' name='Initial Name 2' value=101 CREATE (n:TestNode {id: $id, name: $name, value: $value})"
```

it executes properly on the master node, but in the replicas monitor I only see:

```
"GRAPH.QUERY" "default:diagrams" "CYPHER id"
```

and therefore the change does not propagate to replica.

The issue first appears on v4.10.2. The previous v4.10.1 and earlier properly replay the whole query on the replica.

Multiple connections - crash with signal: 11
issues.body:
Hello,

Under some conditions we experience crash of FalkorDB with signal 11 error. This is not a new issue, we experienced it since at least v.4.8.3. (but could be present in earlier versions as well, we didn't check). This crash seems to be different from the one described https://github.com/FalkorDB/FalkorDB/issues/1231 , also the crash I'm describing now reproduces on the latest 4.12.4 version, where the one from #1231 is fixed (I can confirm that). Good thing that on 4.12.4 we get much more detailed log - on 4.8.3 we get just a couple of lines that there was signal 11 error.

I have developed a stress test that helps me consistently reproduce the issue. Unfortunately I can't share it, as it runs on a production snapshot for the data and on our backend codebase, I couldn't create  a consistent synthetic load that reproduces the crash.

The exact conditions when it happens are:

* Running queries on multiple connections. We have .NET backend that uses connection pool via StackExchange.Redis.MultiplexerPool, but I observed the same behaviour when connected to the same database from two different backends, each of which doesn't use a connection pool. At the same time when I set pool size to 1 (so, we still use the library, but with just one connection) we don't get the crash. In fact we started to see the issue when the connection pool was introduced.
* It seems like the size of the pool doesn't matter. I get crash on 2 connections and 100 connections in the same time.
* Happens with and without active replica instance.
* Dataset size doesn't matter much - I can reproduce the crash on the dataset that is around 40 Mb.
* Write queries cause the problem - if we only do reads, it doesn't happen.

I attach the crash log below. I redacted the dumped queries a bit to not leak the proprietary data, but the structure of the queries is preserved, just the names changed.

issues.title: Issue with Alias Access in ORDER BY Clause in Falkordb
issues.body:
When executing the following query in Falkordb:
MATCH (n {id: 22}) 
WITH n AS alias 
ORDER BY alias.k1 
RETURN alias.k1
I encounter the following error:
_AR_EXP_UpdateEntityIdx: Unable to locate a value with alias alias3 within the record.
However, the following queries execute successfully without issues:
MATCH (n {id: 22}) 
WITH n AS alias 
ORDER BY alias 
RETURN alias.k1

MATCH (n {id: 22}) 
WITH n AS alias 
ORDER BY n.k1 
RETURN alias.k1

MATCH (n {id: 22}) 
WITH n AS alias  
RETURN alias.k1
Expected Behavior:
The query should return the correct value for alias.k1 when ordering by alias.k1.
Additional Information:
The alias is accessible and its properties are accessible in other parts of the query, which indicates that the issue is specific to the ORDER BY clause when using the alias.
The problem only occurs when the alias is used in the ORDER BY clause.

issues.body:
Environment
architecture: x86
os: Ubuntu 20.04
docker：falkordb/falkordb:edge

Q1:`MATCH (n0 :L1)-[r0 :T0]->(n1 :L0 :L4)<-[r1 :T0]-(n2 :L1 :L0), (n3)<-[r2 :T3]-(n2 :L1)<-[r3 :T0]-(n4 :L3), (n4 :L3)<-[r4 :T1]-(n5 :L4)-[r5 :T4]->(n6), (n7 :L1 :L2)<-[r6 :T1]-(n8 :L0)-[r7 :T3]->(n5), (n5)-[r8 :T2]->(n9 :L1 :L4), (n6 :L3)<-[r9 :T2]-(n4), (n10 :L3)-[r10 :T3]->(n11 :L2 :L3 :L0)-[r11 :T0]->(n4), (n8 :L2)-[r12 :T2]->(n12) return count(*)`
result：[[2]]

Q2:`MATCH (n6 :L3)<-[r5 :T4]-(n5 :L4), (n2 :L1 :L0)-[r1 :T0]->(n1 :L4 :L0), (n2 :L1 :L0)-[r2 :T3]->(n3), (n12)<-[r12 :T2]-(n8 :L2 :L0)-[r6 :T1]->(n7 :L2 :L1), (n2 :L1 :L0)<-[r3 :T0]-(n4 :L3)-[r9 :T2]->(n6 :L3), (n10 :L3)-[r10 :T3]->(n11 :L2 :L3 :L0), (n4 :L3)<-[r4 :T1]-(n5 :L4)<-[r7 :T3]-(n8 :L2 :L0), (n4 :L3)<-[r11 :T0]-(n11 :L2 :L3 :L0), (n5 :L4)-[r8 :T2]->(n9 :L4 :L1), (n0 :L1)-[r0 :T0]->(n1 :L4 :L0) return count(*)`

Q2 and Q1 are equivalent. Q2 performs an equivalent rewrite of the MATCH clause, altering the structural composition of the corresponding pattern. In theory, their results should be identical; however, the counts differ — one returns 2 while the other returns 3 — indicating the presence of a bug. We will later search for similar bugs in simpler MATCH clauses.

issues.title: A logic bug is caused by the combination of two MATCH clauses.
issues.body:
Environment
architecture: x86
os: Ubuntu 20.04
docker：falkordb/falkordb:edge

Q1:`MATCH (n0 :L0 :L2)-[r0 :T1]->(n1 :L0 :L3)-[r1 :T1]->(n2 :L3), (n3 :L2)<-[r2 :T4]-(n1), (n3 :L2)-[r3 :T3]->(n3), (n4 :L3)-[r4 :T2]->(n2 :L3)<-[r5 :T3]-(n5 :L6 :L2 :L3), (n5)-[r6 :T3]->(n6)  MATCH (n2 :L3)<-[]-(n5)-[]->(n6) return count(*)`
return [[1]]
Q2:`MATCH (n6)<-[r6 :T3]-(n5 :L3 :L6 :L2), (n1 :L3 :L0)-[r1 :T1]->(n2 :L3), (n1 :L3 :L0)<-[r0 :T1]-(n0 :L2 :L0), (n4 :L3), (n4 :L3)-[r4 :T2]->(n2 :L3)<-[r5 :T3]-(n5 :L3 :L6 :L2), (n3 :L2)<-[r3 :T3]-(n3 :L2)<-[r2 :T4]-(n1 :L3 :L0)  MATCH (n2 :L3)<-[]-(n5)-[]->(n6) return count(*)`
return [[2]]
Q2 performs an equivalent rewrite of the first MATCH clause of Q1, so the results of Q1 and Q2 should be the same. However, one returns 1 while the other returns 2. When we execute the first part of Q1 and Q2 separately, the results are consistent, but adding the second, identical MATCH clause causes the results to diverge. This indicates that the bug is likely caused by the combination of the two MATCH clauses.

issues.title: exists(pattern) function differ from the documentation's description.
issues.body:
### Issue Description:
I am encountering a limitation with the exists(pattern) function in FalkorDB, which seems to differ from the documentation's description.

### Documentation vs. Behavior:
In the FalkorDB documentation, the exists(pattern) function is described as:
exists(pattern) returns true when at least one match for the pattern exists.
However, when I attempt to use exists() with a graph pattern like exists((n)-[]-()) (where n is a node with an edge to any other node), I encounter the error:
Unable to resolve filtered alias '(n)-[]-()'
This suggests that FalkorDB only supports the existence check for a single node rather than a complete graph pattern, as implied by the documentation.

### Steps to Reproduce:
Run the following query in FalkorDB:
GRAPH.QUERY a "MATCH (n) WHERE exists((n)-[]-()) RETURN *"
The following error is returned:
(error) Unable to resolve filtered alias '(n)-[]-()'

issues.title: Unexpected behavior when reusing variable from an unbound previous MATCH in CALL subquery
issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce:
Start falkordb with an empty database.
Execute the following query:
CALL {
    OPTIONAL MATCH (n0 {k1: false})
    WITH * 
    WHERE false
    RETURN n0  
} 
CALL {
    OPTIONAL MATCH () <-[:rt0]-(n0) 
    MERGE p0 = (n0) -[:rt1]->()
    WITH p0 
    RETURN p0 AS alias0
}
RETURN alias0

### Expected behavior:
The query should fail in the second CALL subquery with an error: Failed to create relationship; endpoint was not found.
This is because in the second CALL, n0 should be treated as a new variable due to the fact that it was not imported from the first CALL, and it is effectively unbound.

However, if you modify the query to use WHERE true or WHERE n0.k2 instead of WHERE false in the first CALL, the query fails as expected, throwing an error: Failed to create relationship; endpoint was not found.

### Actual behavior
The query executes successfully without any error

issues.title: FalkorDB allows invalid MERGE query where path variable is incorrectly treated as node variable
issues.body:
### Description:

Executing the following query in FalkorDB unexpectedly succeeds, even though it should fail due to conflicting use of the path variable (p) as both a path and a node. According to Cypher specifications, a path variable (like p) cannot be used as a node variable in a MERGE operation, but FalkorDB allows this and creates two paths instead of returning an error.
Query:

```
MERGE p = (n0:l0)-[r0:rt0]->(n1:l1)
MERGE (n2:l2)-[r1:rt1]->(p)
RETURN p
```

### Observed Behavior:

FalkorDB successfully executes the query without returning an error, even though p is a path variable and should not be used as a node variable in the second MERGE clause.
Two paths are created, and the variable p is incorrectly recognized as a node variable in the second MERGE, leading to logical inconsistencies in the graph.
This behavior contradicts the expected behavior as per Cypher's rules, which state that paths cannot be merged as node variables.

### Expected Behavior:

The query should fail with an error similar to:
p defined with conflicting type Path (expected Node),
as the variable p is a path and cannot be treated as a node in the second MERGE.
The error should prevent the creation of paths and ensure that path variables are used correctly as paths, not nodes.

issues.title: Divide by zero in GRAPH.MEMORY USAGE

issues.title: Deleted node is still accessible within the same transaction after DELETE in RETURN clause
issues.body:
## Description: When executing a query that deletes a node and then returns one of its properties in the same transaction, FalkorDB incorrectly returns the property value instead of raising an error. This behavior is inconsistent with other Cypher-compliant databases such as Neo4j and Memgraph, which correctly report that the node has been deleted and cannot be accessed anymore. ## Steps to Reproduce: Start FalkorDB with an empty database. Execute the following commands sequentially: CREATE (n:l1 {k1:1}); MATCH (n:l1) DELETE n RETURN n.k1; ## Observed Behavior: FalkorDB successfully executes the query and returns 1, meaning it can still access the deleted node’s property (n.k1). This implies that the deleted node object remains accessible within the same execution context even after deletion. Example Output: 1 ## Expected Behavior: The query should fail, as the node n has already been deleted before the RETURN clause is evaluated. Cypher engines such as Neo4j and Memgraph handle this correctly by producing an error like: Node with id 0 has been deleted in this transaction This ensures proper transactional consistency and prevents returning data from entities that no longer exist.

issues.title: SET incorrectly allows assigning properties to a Path variable (SET p.k1 = ... should fail)
issues.body:
## Description: When executing a Cypher query that attempts to set a property on a path variable, FalkorDB incorrectly accepts the query and executes it successfully. According to Cypher semantics, paths are not entities and therefore cannot have properties. Only nodes and relationships can store properties. Other Cypher databases (Neo4j) correctly reject such operations. FalkorDB should throw a type error, but instead allows the operation to proceed. ## Steps to Reproduce: Start FalkorDB with an empty database. Execute: OPTIONAL MATCH p = (n) SET p.k1 = 1 RETURN n; ##Observed Behavior: The query executes successfully. FalkorDB applies SET p.k1 = 1 without reporting any error. This indicates that FalkorDB is erroneously treating the path variable p as a node or an entity capable of holding properties. ## Expected Behavior: Cypher engines must reject such queries. A path is a composite structure, not a graph entity, so setting properties on it is invalid. Expected error (based on Cypher semantics): Type error: Cannot set properties on a path. Expected Node or Relationship. Other implementations (Neo4j) correctly return an error and do not execute the query.

issues.title: Crash via Uncontrolled Memory Allocation in Cypher range() Function
issues.body:
FalkorDB V4.14.8

Environment:
Ubuntu 24.04 LTS

Summary:
FalkorDB contains an input validation flaw within the Cypher query language's range() function implementation. By crafting a query with extreme integer values (e.g., range(1, INT64_MAX)), an attacker can force the database engine to attempt an impossible memory allocation (exceeding physical RAM and virtual address space limits). This results in immediate resource exhaustion, causing the server process to hang, crash (Segmentation Fault), or be terminated by the OS OOM (Out of Memory) Killer, leading to a complete Denial of Service.


POC:
Prerequisites
A running instance of Redis with the FalkorDB module loaded (ulimit -v 1048576 for rapid crash.

Reproduction Steps
Connect to the server using redis-cli or any standard Redis client.

Execute the following command:
GRAPH.QUERY grammar_fuzz "RETURN range(1, 9223372036854775807)"

Unexpected Behavior:
1、The server becomes unresponsive immediately.
2、System memory usage spikes to 100%.
3、The client connection drops with an error similar to: Error: Server closed the connection

Root Cause Analysis:
The vulnerability stems from missing Upper Bound Checks in the implementation of the range(start, end) function.When the query engine processes range(1, 9223372036854775807):It calculates the required list size: size = end - start + 1.It attempts to allocate memory to store these integers. Assuming 8 bytes per integer, the request is for approximately 73 Exabytes of RAM.The memory allocator attempts to fulfill this request, causing extreme memory pressure, swap thrashing, or an immediate crash due to allocation failure handling (or lack thereof).

-------

~test-FalkorDB$ ./redis-7.2.4/src/redis-server --loadmodule ./FalkorDB/bin/linux-x64-release/src/falkordb.so

terminal 2:

issues.title: Security Constraint Bypass via Null Byte Injection in FalkorDB v4.14.8
issues.body:
1. Executive Summary
FalkorDB contains a vulnerability in its Cypher query parser where the null byte (\x00) is incorrectly interpreted as a string terminator. This behavior allows an attacker to truncate the query string at an arbitrary position. By injecting a null byte, an attacker can effectively discard any subsequent Cypher clauses (such as mandatory WHERE clauses for authorization, status checks, or audit logging) that are appended by the application layer. This leads to Authorization Bypass and Logic Manipulation.

2. Vulnerability Details
Environment: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS
Component: Query Parser / Lexer module
Attack Vector: Remote (via Redis Protocol).

3. Root Cause Analysis
The Redis protocol is binary-safe and provides the explicit length of the payload. However, FalkorDB's internal query parser appears to handle the query string using C-style string semantics (stopping at the first null terminator \0), ignoring the actual length provided by the Redis module API.

When the parser encounters \x00 inside the query buffer, it treats it as the End-Of-String (EOS), ignoring all subsequent characters.

4. Proof of Concept (PoC)
Scenario: An application enforces a security policy where users can only query "active" accounts. The application implements this by appending AND n.active = true to the end of every user-supplied query.

Reproduction Script (Python):

The following script demonstrates how to bypass this check to retrieve data for a disabled (inactive) user.

issues.title: GRAPH.slowlog reply should set the query arguments as the last in the array
issues.body:
GRAPH.slowlog reply should set the query parameters as the last in the array. The changes in the reply is causing a breaking change. The original command used to return 4 arguments: ``` GRAPH.SLOWLOG graph_id 1) 1) "1581932396" 2) "GRAPH.QUERY" 3) "MATCH (a:Person)-[:FRIEND]->(e) RETURN e.name" 4) "0.831" 2) 1) "1581932396" 2) "GRAPH.QUERY" 3) "MATCH (me:Person)-[:FRIEND]->(:Person)-[:FRIEND]->(fof:Person) RETURN fof.name" 4) "0.288" ``` Currently it returns 5 arguments where the 4th argument is the query arguments if there are any, which is a breaking change for clients that are expecting the get the time on the 4th argument ``` GRAPH.SLOWLOG graph_id 1) 1) "1581932396" 2) "GRAPH.QUERY" 3) "MATCH (a:Person)-[:FRIEND]->(e) RETURN e.name" 4) (nil) 5) "0.831" ``` To avoid the breaking change, the arguments should be returned as the 5th ``` GRAPH.SLOWLOG graph_id 1) 1) "1581932396" 2) "GRAPH.QUERY" 3) "MATCH (a:Person)-[:FRIEND]->(e) RETURN e.name" 4) "0.831" 5) (nil) ```

issues.title: SET allows labeling of path variables (openCypher violation)
issues.body:
### Configuration FalkorDB Version: `falkordb/falkordb:latest` (pulled 2025-12-15) Operating System: WSL2 – Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS Installation Method: Docker --- ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start falkorDB via Docker ``` docker run --rm -p 6379:6379 falkordb/falkordb:latest ``` 2. Connect with redis-cli ``` redis-cli -h 127.0.0.1 -p 6379 ``` 3. Run the following queries ``` GRAPH.DELETE g ``` ``` GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (:X {k:10})-[:S {k:10}]->(:Y {k:10})" ``` ``` GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH p=(a:X {k:10})-[r:S {k:10}]->(b:Y {k:10}) SET p:L RETURN r" ``` --- ### Expected behaviour The query should fail with a semantic/type error. In [Cypher Query Language Reference, Version 9](https://s3.amazonaws.com/artifacts.opencypher.org/openCypher9.pdf) - A label is a token that is assigned to nodes only. (See page 5) - The `SET` clause is used to update labels on nodes and properties on nodes and relationships. (See page 107) `p` is a named path, so `SET p:L` is invalid and should be rejected during semantic analysis (e.g. “expected Node but was Path”). ### Actual behaviour The query executes successfully with no error and returns the relationship `r`. The invalid `SET p:L` clause is silently accepted.

issues.body:

issues.title: Massive atomic write operations within CALL {} subqueries exhaust transaction memory buffers
issues.body:
Details The CALL { ... } subquery clause executes its contents as a single atomic transaction unit. FalkorDB does not enforce a limit on the number of operations (e.g., CREATE, DELETE) pending in the transaction log/buffer. A query that queues millions of node creations/deletions inside a subquery causes the transaction buffer to grow unboundedly until the server runs out of memory. PoC Prerequisites: A running instance of Redis with the FalkorDB(v4.14.10, Lasted) module loaded. Reproduction Steps: Connect to the server using redis-cli or any standard Redis client. Execute cypher: GRAPH.QUERY exploit "CALL {UNWIND range(0, 2147483647) AS v1 CREATE (n:Node) DETACH DELETE n} RETURN count(*)" Crash Evidence ``` Terminal1: ~/test-FalkorDB$ ulimit -v 1048576 ~/test-FalkorDB$ ./redis-7.2.4/src/redis-server --loadmodule ./FalkorDB/bin/linux-x64-debug/src/falkordb.so Terminal2: 127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY grammar_fuzz "CALL {UNWIND range(0, 2147483647) AS v1 CREATE (n:Node) DETACH DELETE n} RETURN count(*)" Error: Server closed the connection not connected> ``` [crash-log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25065752/crash-log.txt)

issues.title: Dos via Lack of cardinality checks in UNWIND chains allows exponential node creation (Cartesian Explosion)
issues.body:
Details FalkorDB allows chaining multiple UNWIND clauses without estimating the resulting cardinality before execution. A query utilizing three or more UNWIND clauses on a relatively small list (e.g., size 1000) creates a Cartesian product of $1000^3$ (1 billion) operations. The execution engine attempts to process this massive write load without batching or limits, leading to an OOM crash. issues.title: Dos via Creating dense relationships between all nodes triggers rapid memory exhaustion in the edge store
issues.body:
Details When a query attempts to create relationships between every pair of nodes in a set (A fully connected graph), the complexity is O(N^2). For a dataset of 1,000 nodes, this results in 10^6 potential edges. FalkorDB's adjacency storage mechanism attempts to allocate space for these pointers rapidly, causing the process to hit memory limits and crash before the operation can be rejected or timed out. PoC ``` Terminal1: ~/test-FalkorDB$ ulimit -v 1048576 ~/test-FalkorDB$ ./redis-7.2.4/src/redis-server --loadmodule ./FalkorDB/bin/linux-x64-debug/src/falkordb.so Terminal2: 127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY grammar_fuzz "UNWIND range(1, 1000) AS i CREATE (:Victim {id: i})" 1) 1) "Labels added: 1" 2) "Nodes created: 1000" 3) "Properties set: 1000" 4) "Cached execution: 0" 5) "Query internal execution time: 2.393162 milliseconds" 127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY grammar_fuzz "MATCH (a:Victim), (b:Victim) CREATE (a)-[:AA {data: 'padding'}]->(b)" Error: Server closed the connection (121.55s) not connected> ``` [crash-log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25066258/crash-log.txt)

issues.title: Dos via the collect(p) function consumes excessive memory when aggregating variable-length paths in dense graphs
issues.body:
Details When performing a variable-length path match (e.g., -[*1..10]->) in a dense graph and aggregating the results using collect(p), the DFS/BFS traversal algorithm materializes all found path objects in RAM. Due to the combinatorial nature of graph paths, the number of paths grows exponentially with depth. The aggregation function lacks a memory circuit breaker, leading to OOM. PoC Prerequisites: A running instance of Redis with the FalkorDB(v4.14.10, Latest) module loaded. Reproduction Steps: Connect to the server using redis-cli or any standard Redis client. Execute the following cyphers: ``` Terminal1: ~/test-FalkorDB$ ulimit -v 1048576 ~/test-FalkorDB$ ./redis-7.2.4/src/redis-server --loadmodule ./FalkorDB/bin/linux-x64-debug/src/falkordb.so Terminal2: 127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY grammar_fuzz "UNWIND range(1, 50) AS i CREATE (:VLP {id: i})" 1) 1) "Labels added: 1" 2) "Nodes created: 50" 3) "Properties set: 50" 4) "Cached execution: 0" 5) "Query internal execution time: 0.474050 milliseconds" 127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY grammar_fuzz "MATCH (a:VLP), (b:VLP) WHERE a.id <> b.id CREATE (a)-[:NEXT]->(b)" 1) 1) "Relationships created: 2450" 2) "Cached execution: 0" 3) "Query internal execution time: 5.819055 milliseconds" 127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY grammar_fuzz "MATCH p=(:VLP)-[*1..10]->(:VLP) RETURN collect(p)" Error: Server closed the connection (1.09s) not connected> ```

issues.title: Dos via nested list comprehensions allocate multi-dimensional arrays without total size limits
issues.body:
Details Cypher allows nested List Comprehensions (lists within lists). When used with large input ranges, the projection engine allocates memory for the resulting matrix immediately. A query defining a [100,000 x 100,000] matrix attempts to allocate billions of elements. issues.body:
## Summary
FalkorDB should emit Redis keyspace notifications when graph data is modified. This would enable other Redis modules and applications to react to graph changes in real-time without polling.

## Motivation
Currently, there's no way for external modules or applications to be notified when FalkorDB graphs are modified. This makes it difficult to:
- Build reactive systems that respond to graph changes
- Implement caching layers that invalidate on updates
- Create audit logs or change tracking systems
- Trigger downstream processing when graphs are modified
- Coordinate between multiple Redis modules

Redis provides a standard mechanism for this through keyspace notifications, which FalkorDB should leverage.

## Proposed Solution
FalkorDB should call `RedisModule_NotifyKeyspaceEvent()` when graph data changes. This should be implemented in the relevant command handlers.

### Recommended Events

**Essential events:**
- `graph.query` - When a write query is executed (queries containing CREATE, MERGE, SET, DELETE, REMOVE)
- `graph.delete` - When a graph is deleted/dropped
- `graph.node.create` - When nodes are created
- `graph.node.update` - When node properties are modified
- `graph.node.delete` - When nodes are deleted
- `graph.edge.create` - When edges/relationships are created
- `graph.edge.update` - When edge properties are modified
- `graph.edge.delete` - When edges are deleted
- `graph.create` - When a new graph is created
- `graph.index.create` - When an index is created
- `graph.index.drop` - When an index is dropped
- `graph.constraint.create` - When constraints are added
- `graph.constraint.drop` - When constraints are removed

* Build reactive systems that respond to graph changes
* Implement caching layers that invalidate on updates
* Create audit logs or change tracking systems

Redis provides a standard mechanism for this through keyspace notifications, which FalkorDB should leverage.

## Proposed Solution

FalkorDB should call `RedisModule_NotifyKeyspaceEvent()` when graph data changes. This simplified approach sends a single generic notification for any graph modification.

### Event

**Single generic event:**

* `graph.modified` - When any write operation modifies the graph (CREATE, MERGE, SET, DELETE, REMOVE operations)

This simplified approach avoids the complexity of tracking specific node/edge operations and provides a straightforward notification mechanism.

### Implementation Example

```c

        "graph.modified",

}

issues.title: Release 4.16.2
Use-After-Free Crash via Reference to Deleted Relationship
issues.body:
#Summary
The database service crashes if a query deletes a node and then attempts to use a relationship connected to that node. Deleting a node automatically destroys its connections. However, the system fails to realize the relationship is gone. When the query tries to access this dead relationship later, it tries to read invalid memory (a uaf error), causing the entire system to crash.

#Affected Version
FalkorDB v4.16.1(Latest)

#PoC
Prerequisites:
A running instance of Redis with the FalkorDB(v4.16.1, Latest) module loaded.

Reproduction Steps:
Connect to the server using redis-cli or any standard Redis client.

Execute the following cyphers:
GRAPH.QUERY fuzz_graph "CREATE (a)-[r:R]->(a) WITH r, a DETACH DELETE a RETURN startNode(r)"

#Expected Behavior:
The database should handle the invalid reference gracefully.
It should return a semantic error 
(e.g., Error: Variable 'r' refers to a deleted entity) or return NULL.

#Actual Behavior:
The database server process terminates immediately.
The client receives a "Error: Server closed the connection" error.
System logs indicate a Segmentation Fault (SIGSEGV).

#Crash evidence
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY fuzz_graph "CREATE (a)-[r:R]->(a) WITH r, a DETACH DELETE a RETURN startNode(r)"
Error: Server closed the connection
not connected>

issues.title: Heap Use-After-Free via Dangling List Reference
issues.body:
#Summary
FalkorDB fails to properly invalidate references within list containers when a node is deleted, resulting in a Heap Use-After-Free vulnerability. When a graph node is collected into a list variable (e.g., WITH [n] AS list) and subsequently deleted using DETACH DELETE via a reference outside the list (e.g., DELETE list[0]), the list container fails to sanitize or invalidate its internal reference. This leaves a dangling pointer in the list variable pointing to freed memory.

#Affected Version
FalkorDB v4.16.3(Latest)

#PoC
Prerequisites:
A running instance of Redis with the FalkorDB(v4.16.3, Latest) module loaded.

Reproduction Steps:
Connect to the server using redis-cli or any standard Redis client.

Execute the following cyphers:
```
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY test "CREATE (n {payload: 123}) WITH [n] AS list DETACH DELETE list[0] WITH list UNWIND range(1, 100) AS i CREATE (:Filler {val: 0xDEADBEEF}) RETURN list[0].val"
1) 1) "list[0].val"
2)   1) 1) (integer) 3735928559
     2) 1) (integer) 3735928559
     3) 1) (integer) 3735928559
... ...
    99) 1) (integer) 3735928559
   100) 1) (integer) 3735928559
3) 1) "Labels added: 1"
   2) "Nodes created: 101"
   3) "Properties set: 101"
   4) "Nodes deleted: 1"
   5) "Cached execution: 0"
   6) "Query internal execution time: 0.920428 milliseconds"
```
#Observed Behavior
The query returns the integer 3735928559 (which is 0xDEADBEEF in decimal) instead of the original payload 123 or an error.
```
1) 1) "list[0].val"
2) 1) 1) (integer) 3735928559  <-- PROOF OF UAF & REALLOCATION
   ...
   100) 1) (integer) 3735928559
```
#Expected Behavior: 
The query should properly handle the access to a deleted node. Ideally, it should return NULL when accessing properties of a deleted node, or return an error indicating the entity no longer exists.

issues.title: Feature Request: Add LIMIT parameter to fulltext query procedures
issues.body:
## Summary

`db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes()` and `db.idx.fulltext.queryRelationships()` don't support a LIMIT parameter, causing performance issues when fulltext results are combined with WHERE filters in Cypher.

## Current Behavior

```cypher
-- FalkorDB: No LIMIT parameter, returns ALL matches
CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryRelationships('RELATES_TO', 'search term')
YIELD relationship AS rel, score
```

Returns all matching relationships from the fulltext index. Cypher-level LIMIT can only be applied after subsequent MATCH/WHERE processing.

## Comparison with Other Providers

```cypher
-- Neo4j: Supports LIMIT in the procedure call
CALL db.index.fulltext.queryRelationships("index_name", "search term", {limit: 10})

-- Kuzu: Supports TOP parameter
CALL QUERY_FTS_INDEX('label', 'index', 'search term', TOP := 10)
```

## Problem

When combining fulltext search with WHERE filters:

```cypher
CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryRelationships('RELATES_TO', 'search term')
YIELD relationship AS rel, score
MATCH (n:Entity)-[e:RELATES_TO {uuid: rel.uuid}]->(m:Entity)
WHERE e.created_at >= '2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00'
RETURN e, score
ORDER BY score DESC
LIMIT 10
```

If the WHERE filter eliminates all results, the Cypher LIMIT never short-circuits. The query must process ALL fulltext matches through the MATCH pattern before determining there are no results.

**GRAPH.PROFILE evidence:**

| Scenario | Fulltext results | Node scans | Time |
|----------|-----------------|------------|------|
| No WHERE filter, LIMIT 10 | 21 | 137K | 2.1s (LIMIT stops early) |
| WHERE filter, 0 matches | 144 | 981K | 6.5s (exhausts all) |
| Broad query + WHERE filter | 11,837 | ALL | >60s TIMEOUT |

## Underlying Support

RediSearch already supports LIMIT via `FT.SEARCH ... LIMIT offset count`. This feature request is about exposing that through FalkorDB's Cypher procedure interface.

## Proposed API

```cypher
-- Option A: Additional parameters
CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryRelationships('RELATES_TO', 'search term'

issues.title: Using optionally matched edge in `WHERE` clause erroneously causes a `Type mismatch` error
issues.body:
## Description
There appears to be some erroneous behavior when using optional edge matches (`-[:E *0..1]->`) in FalkorDB.

As far as I can tell, the issue appears when:
- An optional edge match is combined with a single edge (non-optional) traversal
- The `WHERE` clause references multiple such edges
- Filtering is performed on one or more nodes on the path

## Steps to Reproduce

For example, with the following setup:
```
CREATE (:A {x: 1})-[:E {id: 1}]->(:B)-[:F {id: 3}]->(:C)
```

The following query errors out:
```
MATCH (:A {x: 1})-[e:E*0..1]->()-[f:F]->(:C) WHERE e.id + f.id > 0 RETURN 1

(error) Type mismatch: expected Map, Node, Edge, Datetime, Date, Time, Duration, Null, or Point but was Path
```

If we remove the `{x: 1}` filter on the starting node, the error goes away:
```
MATCH (:A)-[e:E*0..1]->()-[f:F]->(:C) WHERE e.id + f.id > 0 RETURN 1

1) 1) "1"
2) 1) 1) (integer) 1
3) 1) "Cached execution: 0"
   2) "Query internal execution time: 0.545379 milliseconds"
```

Similarly, changing the `WHERE` clause to `e.id > 0` or `f.id > 0` (i.e., without combining them) also circumvents the error:
```
MATCH (:A {x: 1})-[e:E*0..1]->()-[f:F]->(:C) WHERE f.id > 0 RETURN 1

1) 1) "1"
2) 1) 1) (integer) 1
3) 1) "Cached execution: 0"
   2) "Query internal execution time: 0.687402 milliseconds"
```

## Additional Information

I'm seeing this error in the latest release (`4.16.3`) with Redis `8.2.0`.

issues.title: Redis 8.x dict ABI incompatibility causes SEGFAULT in UNIQUE constraint enforcement
issues.body:
## Summary

FalkorDB's internal RediSearch dict implementation (`dictCreate`, `dictAdd`, `dictFind`, etc.) shares symbol names with Redis's own dict API. On Redis 8.x, Redis's `dictType` struct has 12+ fields while RediSearch's has 6 fields. Without symbol isolation, FalkorDB's dict calls resolve to Redis's implementations via dynamic symbol interposition, causing null pointer dereferences.

## Reproduction

1. Build FalkorDB v4.16.5 from source
2. Load as a Redis 8.x module (tested with Redis 8.6.1)
3. Create a graph with some nodes
4. Create an exact-match index on a property
5. Create a UNIQUE constraint on the same property:
   ```
   GRAPH.CONSTRAINT CREATE mygraph UNIQUE NODE MyLabel PROPERTIES 1 myProp
   ```
6. **Result**: Redis crashes with `signal 11` (SEGFAULT) in `EnforceUniqueEntity+0x1ea`

## Root Cause

`nm -D falkordb.so | grep dictCreate` shows that `dictCreate` (and other `dict*` symbols) are exported from the shared object. When loaded into Redis 8.x, the dynamic linker may resolve RediSearch's internal calls to `dictCreate`/`dictAdd`/`dictFind` to Redis's versions instead. Since the `dictType` struct layout differs between RediSearch and Redis 8.x, this causes field misalignment and null pointer access.

## Notes on `-Bsymbolic`

The CMakeLists.txt already includes `-Wl,-Bsymbolic,-Bsymbolic-functions` in the linker flags, which should prevent this. However, in our builds (Clang 19, Ubuntu 24.04, AMD EPYC), `readelf -d falkordb.so` does **not** show the `DF_SYMBOLIC` flag in the dynamic section, and the symbols remain globally visible. We verified the flag is present in the actual link command but it doesn't take effect in the final binary.

issues.title: FalkorDB CI Runtime Optimization
issues.body:
# FalkorDB CI Runtime Optimization Plan

## Context

The CI pipeline currently takes **~40 minutes per PR** (bottlenecked by CodeQL at 38-42min, with Build at 35-36min). Every PR triggers **16 build jobs** (8 platforms × 2 build types), **24 test jobs** (6 platforms × 4 test types), **6 security scans**, plus separate sanitizer, coverage, and CodeQL workflows. GitHub Actions cache budget exhaustion errors are appearing ("Cache reservation failed: You have reached your configured budget"), meaning dependency caches are being evicted and builds frequently fall back to building everything from scratch.

**Goal:** Reduce PR CI wall-clock time from ~40 min to ~15-20 min, and reduce cache pressure to prevent budget exhaustion.

---

## Recommendations (ordered by impact/effort ratio)

### 1. Remove CodeQL from PR triggers — move to master-only + weekly schedule
**File:** `.github/workflows/codeql-analysis.yml` (lines 14-25)

CodeQL C++ analysis takes **36 minutes** on a dedicated GCE VM and is the single longest workflow. Most large C++ projects run CodeQL on merge to master + a weekly schedule, not on every PR.

**Change:** Remove the `pull_request` trigger. Keep `push` to master/version branches and the weekly `schedule` cron.

- **Savings:** Eliminates the 42-min critical path from PRs
- **Effort:** Low (2 lines removed)
- **Risk:** Low — security issues caught on merge to master instead of PR review; weekly schedule provides safety net

### 2. Skip debug builds on PRs — only build debug on master/tag pushes
**File:** `.github/workflows/build.yml` (line 123)

Currently `build_type: [release, debug]` runs for every event, producing 16 build jobs. Debug artifacts are only consumed by the release-image workflow (which runs on master/tags). Sanitizer and coverage have their own separate debug-like builds.

**Change:** Make `build_type` conditional:
```yaml
build_type: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && fromJSON('["release"]') || fromJSON('["release", "debug"]') }}

issues.title: Use proper double and unsigned int comparison
issues.body:
## Weighted shortest path returns wrong results for fractional edge **weights**

proc_sp_paths.c:529-531, proc_ss_paths.c:519-521 — path_cmp returns double as int: The comparison function returns da->weight - db->weight and da->cost - db->cost as int, but these are double values. 

For values between -1.0 and 1.0, the result truncates to 0, making all such paths appear equal. 

This is a correctness bug that also causes the heap to do unnecessary work. 

Use proper double comparison: return (da->weight > db->weight) - (da->weight < db->weight);



## Integer Overflow in Comparators (qsort corruption)
**Files:** `src/graph/graph_delete_edges.c:37`, `src/value.c:861,876,891`, `src/graph/tensor/tensor.c:506`, `src/procedures/proc_sp_paths.c:529`
**Category:** Data Corruption / Undefined Behavior
**Severity:** CRITICAL

Multiple `qsort` comparator functions subtract 64-bit values and return the result as `int`:
- `_edge_cmp`: `return as - bs;` where `as`, `bs` are `uint64_t` NodeIDs → truncation to `int`
- `SIValue_Compare`: `a.longval - b.longval` for `int64_t` → signed overflow is UB
- `SIValue_Compare`: entity ID subtraction (`uint64_t` → `int`)
- `path_cmp`: `double` subtraction → `int` truncation (values between -1 and 1 become 0)

Broken comparators violate the total ordering requirement of `qsort`, causing incorrect sort results, infinite loops, or out-of-bounds memory access in the sort implementation.

**Trigger:** Sorting data with IDs > INT_MAX, large time differences, or fractional path weights.
**Fix:** Use three-way comparison: `return (a > b) - (a < b);

release 4.16.7
Multiple bugs in Bolt protocol implementation
issues.body:
## Summary

A code review of the Bolt protocol implementation (`src/bolt/`) uncovered **13 bugs** ranging from critical data corruption and security vulnerabilities to protocol violations and minor issues.

---

## Critical Bugs

### 1. Wrong byte-order function in `bolt_read_map_size` (`bolt.c:558`)

`ntohs` (16-bit) is used instead of `ntohl` (32-bit) when reading MAP32 size, silently truncating any map size > 65535.

```c
// BUG:
return ntohs(buffer_read_uint32(data));
// FIX:
return ntohl(buffer_read_uint32(data));
```

### 2. `bolt_reply_int` never emits tiny ints (`bolt.c:140`)

`TINY_INT8_MIN` is `0xF0` (=240 unsigned), but the comparison is against `int64_t data`. The condition `data >= 240 && data <= 127` is **always false**, so the tiny int encoding path is never taken. Every small integer wastes 1 extra byte.

### 3. Stack buffer overflow in `is_authenticated` (`bolt_api.c:77-87`)

A 64-byte stack buffer `s` is used for `bolt_read_string` without checking the incoming string length. A malicious client can overflow the stack by sending oversized key strings.

---

## High Severity Bugs

### 4. Fixed-size buffer overflow in `get_query` (`bolt_api.c:284`)

A 4096-byte stack buffer is used for parameterized queries with recursive `sprintf` and no bounds checking.

### 5. Null pointer arithmetic in `validate_headers` (`ws.c:81`)

`strchr(i, ',') + 2` computes `NULL + 2` when no comma is found — undefined behavior leading to crash.

### 6. Point2D writes 4 fields but declares 3 (`resultset_replybolt.c:85-89`)

An extra `bolt_reply_null` after the 3 declared structure fields corrupts the bolt message framing.

---

## Medium Severity Bugs

### 7. WebSocket frame header broken for payloads > 65535 (`ws.c:218-219`)

The 16-bit extended length overflows; the 64-bit extended length case (RFC 6455 payload len = 127) is never handled.

### 8. `ws_write_empty_header` missing return value (`ws.c:200-207`)

Declared as `uint64_t` return type but has no return statement.

issues.title: HNSW vector index silently returns empty/wrong results during concurrent ingestion
issues.body:
## Summary

FalkorDB's HNSW vector index (`db.idx.vector.queryNodes` / `db.idx.vector.queryRelationships`) silently returns 0 results or incorrect results as the graph grows during ingestion. In our testing, **83% of HNSW queries failed** after ~5 episodes of data ingestion, with the failure rate increasing over time.

This is likely related to #716, but with significantly more reproduction detail.

## Reproduction

**Setup:**
- FalkorDBLite (embedded, single process)
- ~42 episodes ingested sequentially via `add_episode()` (no concurrent writes)
- Each episode extracts 3-49 entity nodes with 768-dim embeddings (BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5)
- HNSW index created with: `CREATE VECTOR INDEX FOR (n:Entity) ON (n.name_embedding)`
- Queries via: `CALL db.idx.vector.queryNodes('Entity', 'name_embedding', $limit, vecf32($search_vector))`

**Observed behavior:**

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Total HNSW queries | 472 |
| Queries returning results | 81 (17%) |
| Queries returning 0 results | 391 (83%) |
| Identical string that should return cosine=1.0 | Not found |

**Timeline of degradation:**
- Episodes 1-5 (small graph): HNSW works — 26 successes, 11 zero results
- Episodes 6+ (growing graph): HNSW mostly broken — 47 successes, 364 zero results

**Specific example:** An entity "And Put Away Childish Things" exists in the graph with a valid `name_embedding`. Searching for the exact same embedding via HNSW returns 0 results, while a Cypher `MATCH` query confirms the entity exists with a non-null embedding.

## Diagnosis

The HNSW index appears to structurally degrade as nodes are inserted. The failure pattern is:
- Works fine initially with a small graph
- Progressively returns fewer results as nodes accumulate  
- Eventually returns 0 results for the vast majority of queries
- Occasionally returns results (non-deterministic — some traversal paths still work)
- **Exporting to a fresh graph restores correct results** (as reported in #716)

issues.title: Unknown relation type in read after write
issues.body:
A merge operation which introduces a new relationship-type is expected to find it when performing its directives.

Starting with an empty graph
```cypher
CREATE (a);

CYPHER relationships=[{v: 1}, {v: -2}]
UNWIND $relationships as relData
MATCH (src), (dest)
WITH relData, src, dest
MERGE (src)-[rel:R]->(dest)
ON CREATE SET rel.v = -12
ON MATCH SET rel.v = 34;
```

Above query would create a single edge `rel:R` although the MERGE clause would try to create it twice due to the UNWIND loop, that second creation would be detected and treated as a match. The MERGE clause must be able to locate its created entities and be aware of its schema changes.

issues.title: ci: Pin GitHub Actions dependencies to commit SHAs for supply-chain security
issues.body:
## Summary

All third-party GitHub Actions in this repository's workflows are currently referenced by **mutable version tags** (e.g., `actions/checkout@v4`). This is a supply-chain security risk — tags can be force-pushed to point to malicious code.

## Recommendation

Pin all third-party GitHub Actions to their **full commit SHA** while preserving the version in a comment for readability:

```yaml
# Before (insecure)
uses: actions/checkout@v4

# After (secure)
uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4
```

## Affected Files

- `.github/workflows/batch-backport.yml`
- `.github/workflows/benchmark.yml`
- `.github/workflows/browser-tests-trigger.yml`
- `.github/workflows/build.yml`
- `.github/workflows/codeql-analysis.yml`
- `.github/workflows/coverage.yml`
- `.github/workflows/release-drafter.yml`
- `.github/workflows/release-image.yml`
- `.github/workflows/release-ramp.yml`
- `.github/workflows/sanitize.yml`

37 action references across 11 workflow file(s).

Three code quality issues were identified by [AI findings](https://github.com/FalkorDB/FalkorDB/security/quality/ai-findings) in `tests/flow/test_path_algorithms.py`:

3. **Hardcoded expected count in `test07_ss_k_minimal_paths`**: Similarly hardcodes `5` as the expected result count instead of adapting to the actual number of available paths with `min(len(self.ss_paths), 5)`.

issues.body:
## Summary
Three code quality issues were identified by [AI findings](https://github.com/FalkorDB/FalkorDB/security/quality/ai-findings) in `src/cron/cron.c`:

1. **Unsafe timespec comparator (`cmp_timespec`)**: Uses `a.tv_sec - b.tv_sec` / `a.tv_nsec - b.tv_nsec` subtraction pattern which can overflow for large `time_t` / `long` values, producing wrong sort order in the cron task heap. Should use the safe three-way comparison pattern (`< → -1`, `> → 1`, `== → 0`).
2. **Typo in comment**: `miliseconds` → `milliseconds` in `Cron_AddTask` parameter doc.
3. **Typo in comment**: `wan't` → `wasn't` in `Cron_AbortTask`.

The comparator bug is the most significant — it could cause incorrect task scheduling order under certain timestamp values.

## Problem

The Trivy SBOM scan of `falkordb/falkordb-server:latest` (Debian 12.13, `redis:8.2.3` base) reports **285 vulnerabilities** (3 CRITICAL, 34 HIGH, 106 MEDIUM, 140 LOW). None have upstream Debian package fixes available.

However, **~157 of these CVEs (~56%)** come from packages that are not needed at runtime and can be removed from the Docker images.

## Unnecessary packages in Docker images

| Package group | # CVEs | Max Severity | Why unnecessary |
|--------------|--------|--------------|-----------------|
| **Node.js 24** (via nodesource) | 8 | CRITICAL | Installed in `Dockerfile.server` but server-only image has no browser |
| **Python 3.11** (from redis base) | 80 | HIGH | Ships with `redis:8.2.3` but FalkorDB never uses Python at runtime |
| **gnupg** (11 packages) | 33 | MEDIUM | Installed as nodesource setup script dependencies, left behind |
| **curl / libcurl4** | 24 | MEDIUM | Only used to download nodesource setup script — not used at runtime |
| **libldap** | 12 | HIGH | Transitive dependency of curl/gnupg — not needed at runtime |

### Debian images (`Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.server`)

## Description

`LOAD CSV FROM 'https://...'` returns empty results in the `edge` tag Docker image built from current master, while it works correctly in the v4.16.7 release.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Pull the edge Docker image
2. Run:
```
redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY a "LOAD CSV FROM 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FalkorDB/FalkorDB/refs/heads/master/demo/social/resources/person.csv' AS row RETURN row"
```
3. Observe empty array result instead of CSV data

## Expected Behavior

The query should return the CSV rows from the remote file.

## Actual Behavior

```
1) 1) "row"
2) (empty array)
3) 1) "Cached execution: 0"
   2) "Query internal execution time: 268.278282 milliseconds"
```

## Root Cause

Commit 1ed48e9f (#1761) removed the `curl` package from Docker images to reduce CVE surface. However, `curl` was the package that pulled in `ca-certificates` as a dependency. Without CA certificates at `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` (the path compiled into the statically-linked libcurl), HTTPS certificate verification silently fails, causing LOAD CSV to return empty results.

## Affected Images

All four Docker variants (Debian browser, Debian server, Alpine browser, Alpine server).

## Regression

Introduced in #1761

issues.title: Add smoke tests for production Docker images before publishing
issues.body:
## Problem

Current CI runs all tests (unit, flow, TCK, fuzz) exclusively against **test Docker images** (`tests/Dockerfile.*`), which include extra packages like curl, Python, build tools, and ca-certificates. The **production Docker images** (`build/docker/Dockerfile*`) are built, uploaded, and eventually published to Docker Hub without any validation.

This gap allowed #1774 to happen — `ca-certificates` was removed from production images (via #1761), silently breaking `LOAD CSV FROM 'https://...'`, while all tests passed because test images still had the package.

## Proposal

Add a `smoke-test` job to `build.yml` that runs against the actual production Docker images after they are built, catching runtime-breaking regressions before images reach Docker Hub.

The smoke test should validate:
- Redis starts and becomes ready
- FalkorDB module loads successfully
- Basic graph CRUD operations work
- **LOAD CSV from HTTPS** works (validates CA certificates + libcurl)
- GRAPH.LIST and GRAPH.DELETE work

Test logic should live in a standalone script (`tests/docker/smoke-test.sh`), not embedded in the workflow YAML, making it easy to run locally and extend over time.

issues.title: SIGSEGV due to data race in Cache_GetValue LRU update (concurrent readers cause cache corruption)
issues.body:
### Summary

SIGSEGV (segfault) crash in `ExecutionPlan_Free` due to a data race in the LRU cache implementation (`Cache_GetValue` in `src/util/cache/cache.c`). The root cause is two concurrent readers updating `cache->counter` and `entry->LRU` under a read lock, leading to corrupted LRU values, wrong evictions, and ultimately use-after-free and segfaults.

### Details
- Race condition on `cache->counter` and `entry->LRU` in `Cache_GetValue` (both incremented/assigned under only a read lock, allows concurrent writes)
- Incorrect LRU state can cause a cached value to be evicted and freed while still in use, resulting in heap corruption and a crash.
- The crash signature points to invalid/corrupted pointers (e.g., 0x65756c61ee == ASCII "value") being dereferenced in `ExecutionPlan_Free` during cache eviction.

### Example backtrace
```
_query → ExecutionCtx_FromQuery → Cache_SetGetValue → CacheArray_CleanEntry → ExecutionCtx_Free → ExecutionPlan_Free ← CRASH
```

### Fix
- The PR uses C11 atomics (`atomic_llong` + `atomic_fetch_add` and `atomic_store`) for both `counter` and cache entry LRU fields.
- This allows all readers to safely increment the counter and update LRU state concurrently, while preserving cache performance.

### References
- See PR: https://github.com/copilot/tasks/pull/PR_kwDOJ9smgc7PO8aD?session_id=24bfcb2e-1d89-4340-8000-3d830c99d581

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Run heavy parallel queries through the module
2. Exercise cache churn (query mix larger than cache size)
3. Eventually segfaults can be triggered due to mishandled cache evictions

### Impact
- Severe: Can corrupt heap/state and kill the server process

---
**Suggested labels**: `bug`, `category/bug`

issues.title: SIGSEGV: Data race when accessing schema arrays in plan construction can crash _GraphContext_GetLabelID
issues.body:
### Bug: SIGSEGV crash in `_GraphContext_GetLabelID` due to schema array data race

#### Summary
Under high concurrency, FalkorDB may crash with a segmentation fault in `_GraphContext_GetLabelID`. This happens because schema array access (`gc->node_schemas`, `gc->relation_schemas`) is not protected during execution plan construction, allowing a data race between reader and writer threads:

- **Reader thread (plan building):** Calls `_GraphContext_GetLabelID` to resolve labels by iterating the schema array, with no lock held.
- **Writer thread:** Adds a new schema using `arr_append`, which may reallocate the schema array, invalidating the pointer the reader is iterating over.

#### Steps to Reproduce
1. Run a workload with many concurrent `GRAPH.RO_QUERY` and `GRAPH.QUERY`/`MERGE` operations, where write queries frequently introduce new labels (e.g. via `MERGE (n:SomeNewLabel)` or `SET n:SomeNewLabel`).
2. Observe rare, intermittent SIGSEGV crashes in `_GraphContext_GetLabelID`. Redis bug reports will point to a fault in this symbol within `falkordb.so`.

#### Root Cause
- Execution plan building does **not** hold any lock on the schema arrays. The code explicitly documents this in `graph_hub.c`.
- When a write query adds a new schema, `arr_append` can reallocate the array. Any reader thread concurrently iterating the old array is left with a dangling pointer, triggering a crash.

#### Expected Behavior
Concurrent `GRAPH.RO_QUERY` and write queries with new labels should not cause segmentation faults.

#### Fix
- Add a `pthread_rwlock_t _schema_rwlock` to `GraphContext`, using a read lock for plan-building functions that iterate the schema arrays, and a write lock for functions that can reallocate the arrays (`GraphContext_AddSchema`, `GraphContext_RemoveSchema`).
- See WIP PR: https://github.com/FalkorDB/FalkorDB/pull/PR_kwDOJ9smgc7PQrb4 (generated by Copilot Coding Agent)

issues.title: fix(query): Memory leak and wrong free in OpSort SortReset
fix: integer overflow in qsort comparators (uint64_t subtraction truncated to int)
issues.body:
## Summary

Multiple `qsort` comparator functions subtract `uint64_t` values and return the result as `int`, causing integer overflow and incorrect sort ordering.

This was partially covered by #1688 (now closed), but only the `path_cmp` double-to-int truncation was fixed. The uint64_t comparator bugs remain on `master`.

## Affected Locations

| File | Line | Expression |
|------|------|------------|
| `src/graph/graph_delete_edges.c` | 37 | `return as - bs;` (NodeID = uint64_t) |
| `src/graph/graph_delete_edges.c` | 42 | `return at - bt;` (NodeID = uint64_t) |
| `src/graph/tensor/tensor.c` | 508 | `return a_id - b_id;` (uint64_t) |
| `src/value.c` | 879 | `return ENTITY_GET_ID(...) - ENTITY_GET_ID(...)` (uint64_t) |

## Root Cause

When `a = 0` and `b = 0x100000000`, the uint64_t subtraction yields `0xFFFFFFFF00000000`, which truncates to `0` as an `int` — incorrectly indicating equality instead of `a < b`.

## Impact

- **`graph_delete_edges.c`**: Incorrect edge deletion order can corrupt adjacency matrices
- **`tensor.c`**: Incorrect tensor operations produce wrong query results
- **`value.c`**: Incorrect SIValue comparisons for nodes/edges with large IDs

## Fix

Use the safe three-way comparison pattern:
```c
return (a > b) - (a < b);
```

## References
- Partially covered by #1688 (closed, only `path_cmp` fixed)

issues.title: Fix memory corruption in plan cache: QGNode now owns its alias/labels (prevents use-after-free on eviction)
issues.body:
## Summary
This PR fixes a critical cache ownership and memory corruption bug in the execution plan cache, which frequently results in use-after-free and hard-to-reproduce crashes (SIGSEGV, corrupted pointers, server aborts) under concurrent load or heavy plan cache churn.

### Root Cause
- `QGNode` and `QGEdge` structs store `const char *alias` and `const char **labels` that point directly into the `AST` parse tree memory.
- When plans are cached, clones retain only shallow copies of the AST, but the cache/free logic can release the shared AST memory (via LRU eviction) while cached `QueryGraph` instances still contain pointers into freed memory.
- This leads to spurious segfaults and memory corruption: QGNode_Free() attempts to free/deallocate invalid pointers, and heap corruption follows.

### The Fix
- Update `QGNode_Clone` (and related QGEdge logic, if affected) to **deep-copy** the alias string and all label strings, so every cached or cloned plan becomes self-contained and does not reference shared or freed memory.
- Update `QGNode_Free` to free these strings when QGNode is destroyed.
- Related logic for QGEdge should receive a similar update if affected.
- This ensures that even if the AST is freed, cached plans remain valid and safe.

### Test
- Adds a new flow test where the execution plan cache is cycled rapidly under concurrent load, mixing repeated and unique queries. (Includes script logic based on prior analysis. See below for minimal Python repro.)
- Test asserts that under high concurrency, no server crash or segfault occurs once fix is present.
- **Script (minimal):**
```python
# See previous message for full script
# ...
```

### Related Issues
- Fixes: _new issue (detailed)_
- Connects: #152 ("Changing cache logic causes test failures")

---
- [x] All memory (alias, label strings) in QGNode is now properly owned and freed.
- [x] Cache churn and concurrent reuse correctly managed.
- [x] Flow test included to ensure regression is detected.

issues.title: Default TIMEOUT=1000ms silently kills long-running queries (e.g. Graphiti episode ingestion)
issues.body:
## Summary

The default `TIMEOUT` config on recent `falkordb/falkordb:latest` images is **1000ms**. Any query that runs longer than 1 second — for example, a Graphiti episode ingestion that triggers entity extraction + vector index updates — is killed with `Query timed out`. The failure mode is particularly nasty because async clients like [Graphiti MCP](https://github.com/getzep/graphiti)'s queue worker catch the error internally and the caller sees `add_memory` succeed, while nothing is ever actually written to the graph.

## Repro

```bash
# Pull current latest and check the default
docker run --rm -d --name fdb-test -p 6379:6379 falkordb/falkordb:latest
sleep 2
docker exec fdb-test redis-cli GRAPH.CONFIG GET TIMEOUT
# → TIMEOUT / 1000
```

Compare with an older digest (e.g. `sha256:ba4951f913391b777d17e43436860ebfeca44401490ef7c684eddae1c2a9adfa`, pulled a few months earlier) where the same command returns `30000`.

## Impact

Discovered while debugging why Mac Mini's Graphiti graph stopped growing. Timeline:

- 2026-04-01: Container recreated, pulled `falkordb/falkordb:latest` (new digest).
- 2026-04-01 → 2026-04-07: Graphiti kept accepting `add_memory` HTTP calls and returning success, but the async queue worker failed every episode with `graphiti_core.driver.falkordb_driver - ERROR - Error executing FalkorDB query: Query timed out`. Episode count froze. No user-facing signal.
- 2026-04-07: Noticed the silent failure by comparing node counts between two machines. `GRAPH.CONFIG GET TIMEOUT` returned `1000` on the broken side and `30000` on the working side. Both were running the same Graphiti version against the same data.

The offending query was:

issues.title: Bolt protocol: Support arbitrary usernames (not only 'falkordb') for authentication
issues.body:
## Problem

Currently, the Bolt protocol implementation for FalkorDB only accepts 'falkordb' as the username (the 'principal') during authentication (see `src/bolt/bolt_api.c`). Any other username is rejected due to a hardcoded check:

```c
// check if the principal is falkordb
if(principal_len != 8 || memcmp(s, "falkordb", 8) != 0) {
    return false;
}
```

This creates unnecessary limitations for Neo4j-compatible drivers and tools, which expect to use user-defined usernames for multi-user and ACL scenarios. FalkorDB should allow the Bolt 'principal' field to be any username that is valid per the Redis (ACL or requirepass) authentication, rather than always requiring 'falkordb'.

## Requested Change

- Allow the Bolt LOGON/HELLO authentication to accept any username in the 'principal' field and pass it through to the Redis AUTH call.
- Ensure compatibility with Redis ACL and multi-user authentication environments.
- Maintain backward compatibility so that the 'falkordb' username continues to work.
- Update documentation and error messages to reflect the new behavior.

## Context
- Required for better compatibility with standard Neo4j drivers and security best practices.
- Critical for deployments with multiple users or custom ACLs.

## References
- See `is_authenticated()` in `src/bolt/bolt_api.c`
- [Original implementation discussion](https://github.com/FalkorDB/FalkorDB/pull/1703)

---
Please consider implementing this enhancement to improve Bolt protocol usability and align with common database authentication patterns.

issues.title: Use-after-free in AttributeSet batch removal causes heap corruption
issues.body:
## Description

`AttributeSet_RemoveIdx` has a use-after-free bug when batch-removing 2+ attributes. The swap-with-last loop processes indices in ascending order (smallest first). When a value is copied from a higher position into a lower one, and that higher position is later freed, the copy is left with a dangling heap pointer.

## Root Cause

The indices array is sorted descending via `qsort(cmp_desc)`, but the loop `for (int16_t i = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` iterates them in ascending order. The swap-with-last pattern `vals[idx] = vals[l-1]` copies the struct (including heap pointers). When `l-1` is itself a removal target processed in a later iteration, freeing it invalidates the earlier copy.

**Concrete example** — removing indices [1, 3] from `[v0, v1, v2, v3]` where v1, v3 are strings:
1. idx=1: Free v1, copy vals[3]→vals[1] (vals[1] now points to v3's string)
2. idx=3: Free vals[3] → frees the same string vals[1] points to → **dangling pointer**

## Impact

- **Heap corruption**: dangling pointers lead to use-after-free and double-free
- **Production crashes**: SIGSEGV in `EP_Free`, `HashTableRelease`, and jemalloc internals
- **Trigger condition**: any Cypher query that sets 2+ existing attributes to NULL in a single operation (e.g., `SET n.a = NULL, n.b = NULL`), or MERGE/UPDATE patterns that remove multiple attributes via `AttributeSet_Update`

## Introduced In

Commit `0ddddf039` — "Reduce attribute-set memory consumption" (PR #1379, Dec 8 2025). The old code removed one attribute at a time; the compact format rewrite added batch removal with the incorrect loop direction.

## Affected Versions

v4.18.0 and later (any version containing commit 0ddddf039).

issues.title: Active defrag race condition: writer threads access entity data without graph lock
issues.body:
## Description

Active defragmentation can move `AttributeSet` memory while writer threads are reading entity data without holding the graph lock, causing use-after-free crashes.

## Root Cause

Writer threads executing MERGE queries hold **no graph lock** during the match phase. The lock is only acquired lazily via `QueryCtx_LockForCommit` inside `op_merge.c` at commit time. Meanwhile, the defrag callback runs on the main Redis thread, acquires the **WRITE lock**, and calls `RedisModule_DefragAlloc` to relocate `AttributeSet` memory. The writer thread is left with stale pointers to freed memory.

**Timeline:**
1. Worker thread starts MERGE query — `ExecutionPlan_Execute` at `cmd_query.c:234` (no lock)
2. Match phase in `op_merge.c:295-371` scans entity attributes (no lock)
3. Main thread runs defrag callback — acquires WRITE lock, moves `AttributeSet` via `RedisModule_DefragAlloc` (`graphcontext_defrag.c:75-92`)
4. Worker thread accesses the old (now freed) `AttributeSet` memory → **SIGSEGV**

## Reproduction

A reproduction script (`repro_defrag_race.py`) reliably crashes the server in ~10-20 seconds by:
1. Enabling aggressive defrag settings: `activedefrag yes`, `active-defrag-threshold-lower 1`, `active-defrag-threshold-upper 1`, `active-defrag-ignore-bytes 1`
2. Running 8 concurrent writer threads executing parameterized MERGE+SET queries

Control tests confirm: defrag-only = safe, writers-only = safe, both together = crash.

## Impact

- **Production crashes**: SIGSEGV in `EP_Free`, `HashTableRelease`, and jemalloc internals
- **Affects any deployment with `activedefrag yes`** (Redis default varies by configuration)
- Observed in 10+ production crash reports on FalkorDB v4.18.0

## Affected Versions

All versions with active defrag support. The fundamental issue is the lockless match phase window in `cmd_query.c`.

## Related

The same lockless match phase window also allows `GRAPH.EFFECT` (replication) commands to modify graph data while a worker thread reads

issues.title: feat(deps): replace Dependabot gitsubmodule tracking with tag-only update workflow
issues.body:
## Problem

Dependabot's `gitsubmodule` ecosystem opens PRs on **every upstream commit** to tracked submodules under `deps/`. This creates excessive noise — most commits are not releases, and updating to arbitrary mid-development SHAs can introduce instability.

## Expected Behavior

Submodule update PRs should only be created when a **new tag/release** is published upstream, not on every commit. Each submodule update should produce its own PR for easier reviewability.

## Submodules Affected

| Submodule path | Upstream repo |
|---|---|
| `deps/LAGraph` | `GraphBLAS/LAGraph` |
| `deps/RediSearch` | `FalkorDB/RediSearch` |
| `deps/libcsv` | `rgamble/libcsv` |
| `deps/libcurl` | `curl/curl` |
| `deps/oniguruma` | `kkos/oniguruma` |
| `deps/quickjs` | `bellard/quickjs` |
| `deps/rax` | `antirez/rax` |
| `deps/utf8proc` | `JuliaStrings/utf8proc` |
| `deps/xxHash` | `Cyan4973/xxHash` |

## Proposed Solution

1. Create a new GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/submodule-update.yml`) that runs weekly (+ manual trigger) and checks each submodule for new tags/releases, opening per-submodule PRs only when updates are available.
2. Disable the Dependabot `gitsubmodule` entry by setting `open-pull-requests-limit: 0`.

issues.title: Missing return after rm_free in RDB deleted-entity decoders causes use-after-free
issues.body:
## Description

When decoding deleted nodes/edges from an RDB stream, `RdbLoadDeletedNodes` and `RdbLoadDeletedEdges` (v18, v19) validate that the buffer length is a multiple of `sizeof(NodeID)` / `sizeof(EdgeID)`. If the check fails, the buffer is freed via `rm_free()`, followed by `ASSERT(false)`.

In release builds, `ASSERT` compiles to a no-op, so execution falls through past the free:
1. The loop dereferences the already-freed pointer (use-after-free read)
2. `rm_free()` is called again at the end of the function (double-free)

## Affected Functions

- `RdbLoadDeletedNodes_v19` — `current/v19/decode_graph_entities.c`
- `RdbLoadDeletedEdges_v19` — `current/v19/decode_graph_entities.c`
- `RdbLoadDeletedNodes_v18` — `prev/v18/decode_graph_entities.c`
- `RdbLoadDeletedEdges_v18` — `prev/v18/decode_graph_entities.c`

## Expected Behavior

The function should return immediately after freeing the buffer on a corrupted/misaligned input, regardless of build configuration.

issues.title: `count(variable)` may double-count matches in a simple converging-relationship pattern
issues.body:
**FalkorDB version**
FalkorDB `4.16.8`

Docker image used locally:
- `falkordb/falkordb-server:latest`

**Environment**
- Host OS: Windows
- Architecture: x86_64
- Deployment: Docker
- Connection method: RESP / `GRAPH.QUERY`
- Client used for direct reproduction: project FalkorDB executor
- Differential comparison target: Neo4j Community `2026.03.1`
**Describe the bug**
FalkorDB appears to over-count rows for a simple converging relationship pattern when using `count(variable)`.

With the minimal graph:

```cypher
CREATE (:Person {name: 'Alice'})-[:FRIEND]->(:Person {name: 'Bob'})<-[:FRIEND]-(:Person {name: 'Charlie'});
```

the query:

```cypher
MATCH (p1:Person)-[:FRIEND]->(p2:Person)<-[:FRIEND]-(p3:Person)
RETURN p2.name AS person, count(p1) AS friendsCount
```

returns:

- Neo4j: `Bob, 2`
- FalkorDB: `Bob, 4`

This looks like duplicated aggregation rather than a simple ordering or formatting difference.

**To Reproduce**
1. Start a FalkorDB Docker container.
2. Run:

```cypher
MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n;
CREATE (:Person {name: 'Alice'})-[:FRIEND]->(:Person {name: 'Bob'})<-[:FRIEND]-(:Person {name: 'Charlie'});

MATCH (p1:Person)-[:FRIEND]->(p2:Person)<-[:FRIEND]-(p3:Person)
RETURN p2.name AS person, count(p1) AS friendsCount
```

**Expected behavior**
The result should be:

```text
person = Bob
friendsCount = 2
```

This is the result returned by Neo4j `2026.03.1`.

**Actual behavior**
FalkorDB returns:

```text
person = Bob
friendsCount = 4
```

issues.title: High RSS / resident-memory retention after repeated temporary graph create/delete cycles
issues.body:
## Summary

I observed a memory behavior in FalkorDB that I would like to better understand.

When I repeatedly create short-lived graphs, insert a batch of nodes, and then immediately delete those graphs, the logical memory footprint returns close to baseline, but the process RSS does not return to a stable band quickly. In particular, `used_memory` stays nearly flat after the workload, while `used_memory_rss` and `allocator_resident` remain elevated and drift upward across batches.

Running `MEMORY PURGE` reduces RSS noticeably, so this currently looks more like resident-memory retention than a classic "objects are never freed" leak. I would like to understand whether this is expected behavior under FalkorDB's current design, or whether maintainers would consider it a bug or an area for improvement.

## Environment

- FalkorDB Docker image: `falkordb/falkordb:latest`
- Redis allocator reported by `INFO memory`: `jemalloc`

## Reduced reproduction

This is a reduced workload intended to represent repeated temporary-graph churn. It is not meant to stress unusual Cypher semantics.

Start FalkorDB:

```bash
docker run --rm -d --name falkordb-rss -p 6379:6379 falkordb/falkordb:latest
```

Run several batches of create/delete churn:

```bash
for batch in $(seq 1 5); do
  start=$(( (batch - 1) * 24 + 1 ))
  end=$(( batch * 24 ))
  for i in $(seq "$start" "$end"); do
    redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY "g$i" "UNWIND range(1,5000) AS x CREATE (:N {v:x})"
    redis-cli GRAPH.DELETE "g$i"
  done
  echo "=== batch $batch ==="

issues.title: Queries with trailing semicolons followed by whitespace are rejected as multi-statement
issues.body:
## Bug

When a query ends with a trailing `;` followed by whitespace (e.g. newline, space), the `parse_query` function in `src/ast/ast.c` incorrectly rejects it with:

```
Error: query with more than one statement is not supported.
```

## Reproduction

Send any valid single-statement Cypher query that ends with `;\n`, `; `, or `;\t`. For example, a long `CREATE` query ending with `RETURN count(*) AS created;` followed by a trailing newline.

```
RETURN 1;
```
(note the trailing newline after the semicolon)

## Expected Behavior

The query should execute successfully, since it is a single valid statement. Trailing whitespace after a semicolon should be ignored.

## Root Cause

`parse_query` in `src/ast/ast.c` only strips trailing `';'` characters:

```c
int len = strlen(query);
while(len > 0 && query[len - 1] == ';') {
    len--;
}
```

If any whitespace follows the semicolon, the semicolon is never reached by the loop. `cypher_fparse` then receives the `;` as a statement terminator, leaving unconsumed input and causing `cypher_parse_result_eof()` to return `false`.

## Environment

- FalkorDB master branch
- Affects any client sending queries with trailing whitespace after semicolons

issues.title: AndMultiplexer_Consume silently truncates query results on branch failure
Double-free heap corruption when SET clause references the same property twice
issues.body:
## Description

`AttributeSet_Update` produces a double-free / heap-use-after-free when a single Cypher `SET` operation contains the same property name more than once, e.g.:

```cypher
SET n.x = NULL, n.x = NULL
```

This corrupts the heap in release builds (silent wrong results / crash) and triggers an immediate `SIGABRT` in debug builds.

## Root Cause

The categorization loop in `AttributeSet_Update` calls `AttributeSet_Contains(_set, attr_id, &idx)` to locate the existing slot for each incoming entry. Because removals are deferred, both occurrences of the same `attr_id` resolve to the **same slot index**, so that index is appended to `remove_idx[]` twice.

`AttributeSet_RemoveIdx` then:
1. Frees the value at `slots[idx]` and swap-copies the last live attribute into that position.
2. Processes the duplicate entry — frees `slots[idx]` again, which is now the swapped-in neighbour → **double-free of a live attribute**.

The bug affects:
- The normal (mixed update) path — duplicate `NULL` entries for an existing property
- The `only_additions` fast-path — duplicate non-NULL entries for a property when the set is initially empty (creates two entries for the same id)

## Reproduction

```cypher
CREATE (n {a: 'alpha', b: 'bravo', x: 'original'})
WITH n SET n.x = NULL, n.x = NULL
RETURN n
```

In a debug build (`ASSERT`/glibc heap checks active):
```
malloc: *** error for object 0x…: pointer being freed was not allocated
Abort trap: 6 (SIGABRT)
```

Also reproducible via the unit test added in PR #1882:
```c
test_attributeset_duplicate_id_remove   // → SIGABRT before fix
```

## Impact

- **Heap corruption** on the hottest write path
- Remotely triggerable by any client that issues a Cypher SET with a repeated property name
- Replicated to replicas via the effects stream, so corruption propagates

## Affected Versions

Any version containing commit `0ddddf039` (PR #1379, "Reduce attribute-set memory consumption") — v4.18.0 and later.

## Fix

PR #1882 — adds last-write-w

issues.title: Nested pattern comprehensions return NULL for inner scope variables
issues.body:
## Description

When using a nested pattern comprehension inside a map projection within an outer pattern comprehension, the inner comprehension returns `NULL` instead of resolving the outer scope variable.

## Steps to Reproduce

```
GRAPH.QUERY test "CREATE (:Issue {id:1})-[:RAISED_BY]->(:Person {name:'Alice'})-[:WORKS_FOR]->(:Organization {name:'Acme'})"

GRAPH.QUERY test "MATCH (i:Issue) RETURN [(i)-[:RAISED_BY]->(p:Person) | p { .name, worksFor: [(p)-[:WORKS_FOR]->(o:Organization) | o { .name }] }][0] AS raisedBy"
```

## Expected Result

```
raisedBy
{name: Alice, worksFor: [{name: Acme}]}
```

## Actual Result

```
raisedBy
{name: Alice, worksFor: NULL}
```

## Additional Context

The inner pattern comprehension `[(p)-[:WORKS_FOR]->(o:Organization) | o { .name }]` does not resolve `p` from the outer comprehension scope. The same query works correctly on Neo4j 5.x.

This pattern is commonly used by graph ORM libraries to project nested relationships (e.g., loading a view with `Issue → Person → Organization` in a single query).

**Workaround**: Restructure the query to use `CALL { }` subqueries instead of nested pattern comprehensions:

```
MATCH (i:Issue)
CALL {
    WITH i
    OPTIONAL MATCH (i)-[:RAISED_BY]->(p:Person)
    OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:WORKS_FOR]->(o:Organization)
    RETURN p { .name, worksFor: collect(o { .name }) } AS raisedBy
}
RETURN raisedBy
```

**Environment**: FalkorDB latest (Docker `falkordb/falkordb:latest`), tested April 2026.

issues.title: collect() on null node from OPTIONAL MATCH produces map with null values instead of being skipped
issues.body:
## Description

When `OPTIONAL MATCH` finds no matching node and the result is `null`, `collect()` with a map projection on that null node produces `[{key: NULL, ...}]` instead of skipping the null entirely (as Neo4j does).

## Steps to Reproduce

```
GRAPH.QUERY test "CREATE (:Issue {id:1})-[:RAISED_BY]->(:Person {name:'Alice'})"

GRAPH.QUERY test "MATCH (i:Issue) CALL { WITH i OPTIONAL MATCH (i)-[:RAISED_BY]->(p:Person) OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:WORKS_FOR]->(o:Organization) WITH p, collect(DISTINCT o { .name, .uuid }) AS orgs RETURN { person: { name: p.name }, worksFor: orgs } AS raisedBy } RETURN raisedBy"
```

Note: There is no `:Organization` node or `:WORKS_FOR` relationship in the graph.

## Expected Result (Neo4j behavior)

```
{person: {name: Alice}, worksFor: []}
```

`collect()` skips `null` values, producing an empty list.

## Actual Result (FalkorDB)

```
{person: {name: Alice}, worksFor: [{name: NULL, uuid: NULL}]}
```

The null node is projected into a map with all-null values and included in the collected list.

## Impact

This causes downstream deserialization failures when ORMs/mappers encounter unexpected null values in what should be an empty collection. The workaround is to explicitly filter nulls:

```cypher
collect(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o IS NOT NULL THEN o { .name, .uuid } END) AS orgs
```

But this shouldn't be necessary — `collect()` should skip nulls by default, matching Neo4j's behavior.

**Environment**: FalkorDB latest (Docker `falkordb/falkordb:latest`), tested April 2026.

issues.title: DELETE not visible to subsequent WHERE pattern predicate in same query
issues.body:
## Description

When a relationship is deleted with `DELETE r`, a subsequent `WHERE NOT (target)<-[]-()` in the same query does not reflect the deletion. The pattern predicate still sees the deleted relationship, causing the WHERE to incorrectly filter out the node.

## Steps to Reproduce

```
GRAPH.QUERY test "CREATE (:A {id:1})-[:R]->(:B {id:2})"

GRAPH.QUERY test "MATCH (a:A)-[r:R]->(b:B) DELETE r WITH b WHERE NOT (b)<-[]-() DELETE b RETURN 'orphan deleted'"
```

Then check:
```
GRAPH.QUERY test "MATCH (b:B) RETURN b.id"
```

## Expected Result

B should be deleted — after `DELETE r`, B has no incoming relationships, so `NOT (b)<-[]-()` should be true.

```
GRAPH.QUERY: (empty result, B deleted)
```

## Actual Result

B still exists:
```
b.id
2
```

The query returns `'orphan deleted'` (the WHERE passes), but `DELETE b` silently fails to persist.

## Additional Context

- Without the WHERE clause, `DELETE r WITH b DELETE b` works correctly — both are deleted.
- Splitting into two separate queries works correctly.
- This pattern is used by ORMs for CASCADE DELETE_ORPHAN — delete a relationship, then delete the target if it has no remaining relationships.

Neo4j handles this correctly — deletions are visible to subsequent clauses within the same query.

**Environment**: FalkorDB latest (Docker `falkordb/falkordb:latest`), tested April 2026.

issues.body:
`tests/flow/test_slowlog.py` fails intermittently, and has been "fixed" twice by enlarging the query that is supposed to displace a slowlog entry. The size was never the problem.

## What fails

Under coverage instrumentation it reproduces every time; a release build shows nothing:

```
run 1: Total Tests Run: 6, Total Tests Failed: 1   test_slowlog.py:89  (assertNotEqual)
run 2: Total Tests Run: 6, Total Tests Failed: 1   test_slowlog.py:89
run 3: Total Tests Run: 6, Total Tests Failed: 1   test_slowlog.py:89
```

`test06_force_replace` fails alongside it on `assertContains(q1, queries)` — same cause.

## Cause: contention, not query size

`populate_slowlog` runs 19 queries **concurrently** through an async pool. A slowlog entry records the query's own latency, so queries competing for the same cores record times far above the work they actually do:

| | |
|---|---|
| work each populate query actually does | ~105 ms |
| what the ten retained entries recorded | **5,600 – 8,771 ms** |
| inflation | **~37×** |

Every later test then has to out-rank those entries while running **alone**. So the bar is set by an inflation factor that depends on the runner's core count and on whether instrumentation is enabled — and it cannot be met by sizing the query:

| candidate displacing query | solo | vs the entry it must evict |
|---|---:|---:|
| current nested UNWIND | 404 ms | **0.07×** |
| same shape, 10× populate's rows | 1,524 ms | 0.27× |
| same shape, 25× rows | 3,701 ms | 0.66× |
| same shape, 50× rows (125 M rows) | 7,516 ms | 1.34× |

Only a 125-million-row query clears it, at a margin of 1.34×. That is the shape of a test chasing a moving target.

Run serially, an entry's latency is its own work — **98.9–154.5 ms** under the same instrumentation — and the bar becomes something a query can be sized against. The *existing* displacing query already clears it at 3.81×.
