issues.title: CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX ... OPTIONS {stopwords} is accepted but not applied when the label already has a range index
issues.body:
**Versions:** FalkorDB 6.0.0 (`falkordb/falkordb:6.0.0`, amd64, graph module ver 60000) and 6.0.1 (amd64 and arm64, ver 60001).

If a label already has a range index, `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX ... OPTIONS {stopwords: [...]}` reports `Indices created: 1` with no warning, but the stopwords are not applied.

**Repro (redis-cli):**

```
GRAPH.QUERY g1 "CREATE INDEX FOR (n:L) ON (n.uuid)"
GRAPH.QUERY g1 "CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX FOR (n:L) ON (n.t) OPTIONS {stopwords: ['router']}"
GRAPH.QUERY g1 "CREATE (:L {uuid:'u1', t:'router restarted'})"
GRAPH.QUERY g1 "CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes('L','router') YIELD node RETURN count(node)"
GRAPH.QUERY g1 "CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes('L','restarted') YIELD node RETURN count(node)"
```

| order | `'router'` (the stopword) | `'restarted'` (control) |
|---|---|---|
| range index first, then fulltext (above) | **1** | 1 |
| fulltext first, then range | 0 | 1 |

I reproduced it twice on each of 6.0.0 amd64, 6.0.1 arm64 and 6.0.1 amd64. `CALL db.indexes()` reported `OPERATIONAL` before each query.

In both orders, a later `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX FOR (n:L) ON (n.t2) OPTIONS {stopwords: ['router']}` fails with `Can not override index configuration: Stopwords are already set for label 'L'`. In the range-first case that error says the stopwords are set, even though they are not being applied.

**Expected:** either apply the stopwords whatever index already exists on the label, or reject the `OPTIONS` with an error.

Related: #2540 (`createNodeIndex` on the Rust engine), #1209 (stopwords and queries), getzep/graphiti#1947. Graphiti creates its range indices before its fulltext indices, so a DDL migration that keeps its stopwords runs into this.

issues.title: GRAPH.RESTORE crashes the server on an empty or truncated payload
issues.body:
## Description

`GRAPH.RESTORE` crashes the server if the payload is empty or ends early. It should return an error.

## Steps to reproduce

```
GRAPH.RESTORE x ""
```

Any payload that is cut off at a value boundary does the same thing.

## Cause

`graph_restore` decodes with `BufferedReader::from_slice`, which leaves `rdb` as a null pointer. When the reader runs out of bytes, `ensure_available` calls `load_chunk`, which calls `raw::load_string_buffer(self.rdb)`. That ends up in `RedisModule_LoadStringBuffer` with a null IO handle and Redis dereferences it.

The `TYPE_BLOB` branch of `read_buffer` already checks `self.rdb.is_null()`, but `load_chunk` does not.

Related problem in the same path: the header, schema and payload directory decoders call `Vec::with_capacity(count as usize)` with counts taken from the payload, so a short payload with a very large count aborts the process on the allocation.

## Expected

An error reply, server keeps running, no key created.

## Notes

Found by reading the code in `src/serializers/buffered_io.rs` and `src/serializers/decoder/mod.rs` on `main`. Fix is in #3167.

issues.title: macOS build fails with Homebrew LLVM 23: VectorSimilarity's vec_utils.cpp doesn't include <string>
issues.body:
On macOS with Homebrew LLVM 23 (`llvm 23.1.2`), the RediSearch dep fails to build in VectorSimilarity:

```
deps/RediSearch/deps/VectorSimilarity/src/VecSim/utils/vec_utils.cpp:157:17: error: implicit instantiation of undefined template 'std::basic_string<char>'
  157 |     std::string value(rawParam.value, rawParam.valLen);
      |                 ^
/opt/homebrew/Cellar/llvm/23.1.2/bin/../include/c++/v1/__fwd/string.h:43:7: note: template is declared here
```

**Cause:** `vec_utils.cpp` uses `std::string` but includes only `<cmath>`, `<cerrno>`, `<climits>`, `<float.h>` and `<algorithm>`. It got `<string>` indirectly through one of those, and libc++ 23 no longer provides it that way. On macOS, RediSearch's `build.sh` forces `clang`/`clang++` from `PATH` (`build.sh:424`), so Homebrew LLVM 23 compiles it against its own libc++.

- **This is the only failure.** With `MAKEFLAGS=-k`, 403 of the 404 RediSearch object files compile.
- **Linux is unaffected.** CI has built with clang-23 since #3163 and `main` is green, because that build uses libstdc++.
- **Upstream has the same code.** RedisAI/VectorSimilarity master still has these includes (the last change to the file is `ca937dbf8`, 2026-06-04), so bumping the submodule doesn't fix it.

**Repro** (macOS, Homebrew `llvm` 23.x):

```bash
CC=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/clang CXX=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/clang++ \
  FALKORDB_NATIVE_DEPS_FORCE=1 cargo build
```

issues.body:
### Summary

Add machine-checked Lean 4 proofs for the Rust engine to the repository, and a Claude Code skill that helps contributors keep them working.

Over the last two weeks the engine was modelled in Lean 4, function by function, and properties were proved about those models. Where a property turned out to be false, the Lean counterexample was reproduced against the real Rust and compared with the C module. That process found roughly 200 confirmed bugs. Most are now fixed on main through the PRs linked from the ledger. The proofs currently live outside version control, so nobody else can run, extend or review them.

issues.title: [Rust] Non-boolean WHERE on a variable-length relationship silently matches nothing instead of a type error
issues.body:
### Summary

A non-boolean `WHERE` predicate on a variable-length relationship silently matches nothing. It should raise the same type error it raises anywhere else, which is what C does.

### Reproduction

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (:A)-[:R {w: 5}]->(:B)"
```

| query | Rust (`main` @ da6f808c3) | C (`falkordb-server:edge-c`) |
|---|---|---|
| `MATCH (a:A)-[r:R*1..2]->(b) WHERE r.w RETURN count(a)` | **0** | `Type mismatch: expected Boolean but was Integer` |
| `MATCH (a:A)-[r:R*1..2]->(b) WHERE r.missing RETURN count(a)` (null) | 0 | 0 |
| `MATCH (a:A)-[r:R]->(b) WHERE r.w RETURN count(a)` (fixed length) | type error | type error |
| `WITH 5 AS x WHERE x RETURN count(x)` | type error | type error |

Only the var-length row diverges; null is a rejection on both engines.

### Mechanism

`absorb_edge_filters_into_vlt` moves a `WHERE` conjunct that reads only the edge alias into `CondVarLenTraverse`'s `edge_filter` (`graph/src/planner/optimizer/absorb_edge_filters_into_vlt.rs:130`), where it is evaluated per edge during the walk. That evaluation treats every result other than `true` as a rejection (`graph/src/runtime/ops/cond_var_len_traverse.rs:293-294`):

```rust
Ok(Value::Bool(true)) => {}
Ok(_) => continue,
```

A `FilterOp` evaluating the same predicate raises a type error for a non-boolean, non-null result. Moving the predicate into the walk is an optimization, so it must not change what the query means.

### Expected

Match `FilterOp` and C: `true` keeps the edge, `false` or `null` rejects it, anything else is `Type mismatch: expected Boolean but was <type>`.

issues.title: RESTORE ... REPLACE onto an existing graph crashes the server
issues.body:
Running RESTORE <key> 0 <payload> REPLACE on a key that already holds a graph crashes FalkorDB (SIGSEGV). This is the root cause behind both #259 (bioProcessBackgroundJobs crash on the BIO thread, seen in production) and #2506 (Index_SetLanguage crash on self dump/restore of an indexed graph).

Root cause: Redis decodes the RESTORE payload before evicting the old value, so the old graph is still registered under its name. The v20 decoder looks the graph up by name and merges the payload into the live GraphContext instead of building a fresh one. This (a) re-adds the already-indexed schema → Schema_AddIndex returns a NULL index that's passed to Index_SetLanguage → NULL deref, and (b) hands the still-referenced context back to Redis as the "new" value → the old value's lazy free double-frees the live graph on the BIO thread.

Steps to reproduce:
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (:Person {name:'alice', bio:'hello world'})"
GRAPH.QUERY g "CALL db.idx.fulltext.createNodeIndex({label:'Person', language:'english'}, 'name', 'bio')"
EVAL "local d = redis.call('DUMP', KEYS[1]); return redis.call('RESTORE', KEYS[1], 0, d, 'REPLACE')" 1 g
→ server crashes with SIGSEGV.

Run redis-server as a non-root falkordb user in the Docker image
issues.body:
The runtime image runs `redis-server` as root. Run it as a dedicated, unprivileged `falkordb` user instead, the way the official redis image runs it as `redis`.

### What it does

- `run.sh` starts as root, hands the data directory and the certificates `gen-certs.sh` generates to `falkordb`, and execs `redis-server` through `gosu`.
- It stays root when the container is started with `--user`, when it lacks `CAP_SETUID`/`CAP_SETGID`, or when `SKIP_DROP_PRIVS=1` is set. `SKIP_FIX_PERMS=1` skips the ownership step. Both names match the official image's.
- The image creates a `falkordb` account (uid/gid 999) in place of the `redis` account it creates today, and owns the data and TLS directories as `root:falkordb` with mode 0775.

issues.title: Parenthesized `id(n) = x` predicate disables NodeByIdSeek (falls back to All Node Scan)
issues.body:
### Summary

When an `id()` equality predicate in a `WHERE` clause is wrapped in parentheses, the planner no longer uses `NodeByIdSeek`. It falls back to `All Node Scan` followed by `Filter`. The parentheses do not change what the query means, but the lookup becomes O(N) instead of O(1).

Fully parenthesized predicates are common in Cypher written by query builders, so this is easy to run into. In our case, a query builder rendered `MATCH (a), (b) WHERE ((id(a) = 1) AND (id(b) = 2)) ...` to create a relationship between two known nodes. FalkorDB planned it as `Filter <- Cartesian Product <- All Node Scan x2` (O(N^2)). At 100,000 nodes it hits the default 1000 ms timeout, while the unparenthesized form runs in under 0.1 ms.

Neo4j plans all the parenthesized queries below with `NodeByIdSeek`.

```
redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY repro "UNWIND range(1, 100000) AS i CREATE (:N {i: i})"

issues.title: release 6.0.2
batch-backport only backports the first 30 matching PRs
issues.body:
The batch-backport workflow finds the PRs to backport with a single call to the search API (`.github/workflows/batch-backport.yml`). The call sets no page size and doesn't page. The search API returns 30 results per page by default, so a run backports at most 30 PRs and drops the rest without listing them.

The 6.0 run on 2026-10-08 matched 44 PRs and opened #3189 with 30. These were PRs merged into `main`, labelled `6.0`, and merged after `v6.0.1`. Results were sorted by last update, so the dropped PRs weren't only the newest ones. The other 14 were cherry-picked into #3189 by hand.

The search also filters by the tag's date rather than its time (`merged:>YYYY-MM-DD`). This leaves out PRs merged later on the day the tag was made.

issues.title: Implicit deduplication causes multiplicity loss in multigraphs when edge variables are unreferenced
issues.body:
**Version**
FalkorDB 6.0.2 Latest

**Environment**
Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS x86_64

**Bug Description**
In standard openCypher, a MATCH clause must return a row for every distinct matched path in the graph. In a multigraph where multiple parallel edges exist between two nodes, matching those edges should yield a cardinality equal to the number of parallel edges, even if the edge variable is not explicitly returned.

However, FalkorDB incorrectly collapses/deduplicates multiple parallel edges into a single row if the edge variable (e.g., [e]) is not explicitly referenced in the RETURN or WHERE clause. This leads to a severe loss of cardinality and invalidates logical equivalence when unfolding variable-length paths.

**To Reproduce**

```
# 1. Create a multigraph with 5 parallel edges:

GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n"
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (n30:V {id: 30}), (n31:V {id: 31}), (n30)-[:R0]->(n31), (n30)-[:R0]->(n31), (n30)-[:R0]->(n31), (n30)-[:R0]->(n31), (n30)-[:R0]->(n31)"

# 2. Baseline Query (Using variable-length path - Works Correctly):

GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH p = (a:V)<-[:R0*1..1]-(c:V) RETURN a.id, c.id"
# Expected & Actual: 5 rows. (Cardinality is correctly maintained).

# 3. Metamorphic Candidate Query (Standard explicit match - Fails):

GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (a:V)<-[e:R0]-(c:V) RETURN a.id, c.id"
# Expected Output: 5 rows.
```

**Expected Behavior**
According to standard openCypher semantics, a MATCH clause operates on paths and must return one row for every distinct path found in the graph. Because there are 5 parallel physical edges between node 30 and node 31, matching the relationship between them must yield 5 distinct paths.

**Environment**

# Output: path_count = 1. (Incorrect).
```

issues.title: Incorrect Three-Valued Logic (3VL) evaluation for missing properties (NULL) in list comprehensions and NONE() predicates
issues.body:
**Version**
FalkorDB 6.0.2 Latest

**Environment**
Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS x86_64

**Bug Description**
In the openCypher specification, comparing a missing property (NULL) to a string (e.g., NULL = 'string') must evaluate to NULL (unknown), not FALSE. Furthermore, aggregating functions like NONE(p) follow strict Three-Valued Logic (3VL). NONE(p) is equivalent to NOT ANY(p). If the predicate evaluates to NULL, ANY([NULL]) evaluates to NULL, and NOT(NULL) remains NULL. Finally, a WHERE NULL clause must filter out the row (acting as falsy).

FalkorDB violates this 3VL standard. When a missing property is evaluated inside a list comprehension with a NONE() predicate, FalkorDB incorrectly evaluates NULL = 'string' as FALSE instead of NULL. This causes NONE() to return TRUE, incorrectly allowing the row to pass the filter. Neo4j strictly follows the standard and filters the row out.

**To Reproduce**

```
# 1. Create a graph where one entity is missing a property:

issues.body:
**Version**
FalkorDB 6.0.2 Latest

**Environment**
Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS x86_64

**Bug Description**
A fundamental rule of the openCypher specification is Relationship Isomorphism (also known as relationship uniqueness). Within a single MATCH clause (including comma-separated patterns), the same physical relationship cannot be traversed or bound more than once.

However, FalkorDB fails to enforce this uniqueness constraint. When a query contains comma-separated patterns, FalkorDB allows the same relationship to be matched and bound to multiple path variables simultaneously. This leads to invalid Cartesian products and violates standard Cypher pattern-matching semantics.

**To Reproduce**

```
# 1. Create a graph with exactly ONE edge between two nodes:

GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n"
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (c1:C {id: 1}), (c2:C {id: 2}), (c1)-[:E {w: 5}]->(c2)"
 
# 2. Execute a single MATCH clause with comma-separated path patterns:

GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH p1=(:C {id:1})-[:E]->(:C {id:2}), p2=(:C {id:1})-[:E]->(:C {id:2}) RETURN p1 = p2 AS is_eq"
# (Note: A secondary metamorphic query RETURN nodes(p1) = nodes(p2) AND relationships(p1) = relationships(p2) yields the exact same faulty result).
```

**Expected Behavior (Neo4j Standard)**
The query should return 0 rows (Empty set).
Because there is only one :E edge between node 1 and node 2, the first pattern p1 consumes that edge. The second pattern p2 cannot reuse the same edge due to the relationship isomorphism rule. Therefore, the overall MATCH fails to find a valid subgraph, returning 0 rows.

**Actual Behavior (FalkorDB)**
The query incorrectly returns 1 row with is_eq = true.
FalkorDB ignores the isomorphism constraint, binding the exact same physical edge to both p1 and p2 simultaneously in the same MATCH scope. The engine then evaluates p1 = p2 as true, openly demonstrating that the edge uniqueness rule was violated.

issues.title: Type inconsistency: sum() implicitly casts integers to floats (returned as strings), differing from reduce()
issues.body:
**Version**
FalkorDB 6.0.2 Latest

**Environment**
Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS x86_64

**Bug Description**
When calculating the sum of integer properties, openCypher expects type consistency unless an explicit cast or overflow occurs. However, FalkorDB exhibits inconsistent type coercion depending on the operator used.
When calculating a path weight using reduce(acc=0...), the engine correctly preserves the Integer type. But when performing the exact same mathematical calculation using the sum() aggregate function, the engine implicitly casts the result to a Double/Float (which is serialized and returned as a String over the Redis RESP protocol).

While the numerical values are mathematically equivalent, this unexpected type shifting breaks strongly-typed database clients (e.g., Java, Go, Rust drivers) that expect consistent return types (e.g., integers) for equivalent logical queries, leading to unexpected deserialization crashes (ClassCastException).

**To Reproduce**

```
# 1. Create a graph with integer weights:

GRAPH.QUERY type_graph "MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n"
GRAPH.QUERY type_graph "CREATE (a:Node {id: 1}), (b:Node {id: 2}), (a)-[:LINK {w: 1}]->(b)"

# 2. Query using reduce (Maintains Integer):

GRAPH.QUERY type_graph "MATCH p=(a:Node)-[:LINK]->(b:Node) RETURN reduce(acc = 0, r IN relationships(p) | acc + coalesce(r.w, 0)) AS path_weight"
# Actual Output: (integer) 1

# Actual Output: "1" (Serialized as a string representation of a float)
```

**Expected Behavior**
Both queries should return the exact same data type. If the inputs to sum() are purely integers and do not exceed the 64-bit integer limit, sum() should return an Integer type, identical to the behavior of reduce() and consistent with Neo4j's type handling.

**Version**
FalkorDB 6.0.2 Latest

**Environment**

Multigraph Cardinality Loss: It drastically miscalculates the Cartesian product of parallel edges across multi-hop paths compared to Neo4j.

issues.title: Write with an open index scan aborts or stalls the server; BGSAVE child can block on the pending-slots mutex
issues.body:
## Summary

On `main` at `ec2448f`, two lock hazards in the indexes that RediSearch backs can stop the server.

- A write query that still has an index scan open when it commits aborts the server. With a `RESTORE` running beside it, the server stops answering instead.
- A BGSAVE child can block forever on the pending-slots mutex of an index.

## 1. A write commits while its index scan is open

Two common query shapes keep a scan open at commit time: an index scan below `LIMIT`, and an index scan that feeds a `CALL {}` subquery.

Repro on a stock `main` server. The last command aborts the server:

```
redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(1, 2000) AS i CREATE (:W {v: i})"
redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE INDEX FOR (n:W) ON (n.v)"
# wait until this prints OPERATIONAL
redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g "CALL db.indexes() YIELD status RETURN status"
redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (n:W) WHERE n.v > 0 WITH n LIMIT 10 SET n.v = n.v + 100000 RETURN count(n)"
```

- Expected: the query returns 10.
- Actual: the server aborts, and the log shows `attempted to upgrade a spec read lock to a write lock`.

The stall needs two clients. Client A loops `MATCH (n:D) WHERE n.id > 0 WITH n LIMIT 5 SET n.x = n.x + 1` over 20,000 nodes with a range index on `:D(id)`. Client B loops `GRAPH.DELETE r` and `RESTORE r` of a 2,000-node graph with one range index.

- Expected: both loops make progress, and PING answers.
- Actual: PING gets no reply after 0.2 s, and neither loop completes another command. The writer holds the RediSearch read locks and waits for the GIL. The `RESTORE` holds the GIL and waits for the RediSearch write lock.

## 2. A BGSAVE child blocks on the pending-slots mutex

The RDB encoder runs in the BGSAVE child. It calls `Indexer::index_info`, which reads `Index::pending_count` of every index. `pending_count` locks the `pending_slots` mutex (`graph/src/index/mod.rs:2164`). issues.body:
# Repeated traversal after swapping independent OPTIONAL MATCH clauses

### Describe the situation

Hi, FalkorDB developers,

Please consider these two queries:

```cypher
// q1
MATCH (u:GspAnchor)
OPTIONAL MATCH (u)-[:GSP_LOW]->(v:GspLow)
OPTIONAL MATCH (u)-[:GSP_HIGH]->(w:GspHigh)
WHERE (w.keep = true)
RETURN u.uid, v.uid, w.uid;

// q2
MATCH (u:GspAnchor)
OPTIONAL MATCH (u)-[:GSP_HIGH]->(w:GspHigh)
WHERE (w.keep = true)
OPTIONAL MATCH (u)-[:GSP_LOW]->(v:GspLow)
RETURN u.uid, v.uid, w.uid;
```

I swap two `OPTIONAL MATCH` clauses that share only `u`; the condition uses only `w`. Both queries return the same ten rows, including the rows with a missing low or high neighbor. For q1, FalkorDB repeats the high traversal for each low neighbor, and I measure about eight times the runtime of q2.

### Which FalkorDB versions are affected?

I ran this case on FalkorDB 4.18.8, which reports module version `41808`, using Cypher in the FalkorDB Docker image on macOS ARM64.

Create this data in an empty graph, then run q1 and q2 above:

```cypher

issues.body:
# Cartesian product scans millions of targets before an empty index lookup

### Describe the situation

Hi, FalkorDB developers,

Please consider these two queries:

```cypher
// q1
MATCH (a:GspLow)
WHERE (a.id = 1)
MATCH (b:GspHigh)-[:GSP_LINK]->(c:GspTarget)
WHERE (c.keep = true)
RETURN a.uid, b.uid, c.uid;

// q2
MATCH (b:GspHigh)-[:GSP_LINK]->(c:GspTarget)
WHERE (c.keep = true)
MATCH (a:GspLow)
WHERE (a.id = 1)
RETURN a.uid, b.uid, c.uid;
```

I swap two independent `MATCH` clauses and get no rows from either query, because no `GspLow` node has `id=1`. In q1, FalkorDB stops after the empty index lookup. In q2, it scans 3,000,001 targets before checking the same index, and I measure about 236 times the runtime of q1.

### Which FalkorDB versions are affected?

I ran this case on FalkorDB 4.18.8, which reports module version `41808`, using Cypher in the FalkorDB Docker image on macOS ARM64.

### How to reproduce

Create this data in an empty graph, then run q1 and q2 above:

```cypher

CREATE (:GspLow {uid: 1, id: 0}),

issues.title: [Rust] Slow log panics and kills the server when a multi-byte character straddles byte 2048 of a slow query
issues.body:
### Summary

The slow log cuts the query text (and the parameter text) at byte 2048 without regard to UTF-8 character boundaries. A query longer than 2048 bytes that runs past the 10 ms slow-log threshold, with a multi-byte character straddling byte 2048, panics the worker and takes the server down. C answers normally and logs the query.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

Query: `UNWIND range(1, 2000000) AS x WITH x WHERE x < 0 RETURN count(x) AS c, '<a × 1975>é'` — 2050 bytes, `é` occupies bytes 2047..2049.

```python
prefix = "UNWIND range(1, 2000000) AS x WITH x WHERE x < 0 RETURN count(x) AS c, '"
q = prefix + "a" * (2047 - len(prefix.encode())) + "é" + "'"
r.execute_command("GRAPH.QUERY", "g", q)
r.execute_command("GRAPH.SLOWLOG", "g")
```

Rust: the connection drops and redis-server exits:

```
<module> FalkorDB panic: panicked at src/slow_log.rs:49:10:
end byte index 2048 is not a char boundary; it is inside 'é' (bytes 2047..2049 of string)
```

C (`master` module): the query returns, and `GRAPH.SLOWLOG g` holds one entry whose query is the first 2048 bytes followed by `...` (2051 bytes, ending `aaaa\xc3...` — the `é` cut in half, so the stored text is not valid UTF-8).

The same happens with a long parameter string (`CYPHER p='...é...'`), through `truncate` on the params text.

### Mechanism

`src/slow_log.rs`:
- `entry_hash` (:48-49) hashes `query[..min(len, 2048)]`; this is the first slice that panics.
- `truncate` (:30-32) stores `s[..2048]` + `"..."` for both the query and the params.

Both are byte slices of a `&str`, which panic when the index falls inside a character.

Other byte-limit slices in `src/` were checked: `telemetry.rs` truncates by `char_indices`, `divergence_guard.rs::clip` walks to a char boundary, and the `graph_core.rs` slices are at NUL / params offsets that are always boundaries. Only the slow log is affected.

### Expected

The query answers and the slow log records it, as in C.

### Suggested fix

Cut at the nea

issues.title: [Rust] ORDER BY aggregate is matched to a projection whose constants differ in type (max(x % 4.0) taken for max(x % 3))
issues.body:
### Summary

An aggregate in `ORDER BY` is matched to a projected aggregate whose constants differ in type. `max(n.v % 4.0)` is taken to be the projected `max(n.v % 3)`, so the query sorts by the wrong expression instead of being rejected. C rejects the query.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(1,6) AS i CREATE (:N {g: i % 2, v: i})"
GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (n:N) RETURN n.g AS g, max(n.v % 3) AS m ORDER BY max(n.v % 4.0)"
```

Rust: returns rows `[0, 2], [1, 2]`, ordered by `m`.

C:

```
failed to map aggregation expression within ORDER BY clause, please use alias
```

With `% 4` (an Int, so Int is compared with Int) Rust already rejects it (`failed to map aggregation expression`). Only a difference across constant types slips through.

### Mechanism

`replace_agg_subtrees` (`graph/src/planner/binder.rs:2608`) replaces an ORDER BY aggregate with a projection alias when `raw_exprs_structurally_equal` says the trees match. Its node comparison `expr_ir_eq` (`graph/src/planner/binder.rs:2665-2680`) compares values only for same-type constant pairs (Int/Int, Float/Float, String/String, Bool/Bool). Every other pair falls back to `std::mem::discriminant(a) == std::mem::discriminant(b)`. Every constant is `ExprIR::Constant`, so `Constant(Int(3))` equals `Constant(Float(4.0))`, `Constant(Null)` equals `Constant(Int(7))`, and so on. The same fallback ignores the payload of `Quantifier`, `ListComprehension`, `Reduce`, `Case`, `ShortestPath`, `Pattern`/`PatternComprehension` and `CompiledRegex`.

Open PR #3011 reuses `raw_exprs_structurally_equal` for non-aggregate ORDER BY expressions too, so there `ORDER BY n.v % 4.0` would be bound to a projected `n.v % 3`.

### Expected

Constants match only when they are equal values. C's `AR_EXP_Equals` compares them with `SIValue_Compare`, so `3` matches `3.0`, while `4.0` does not match `3`, `'3'` does not match `3`, and `null` does not match `7`. In those cases the query fails as it does

issues.title: [Rust] CowBTree: remove_batch leaves a one-child non-root branch; a later insert_batch panics in Node::min
issues.body:
### Summary

`CowBTree::remove_batch` (`graph/src/index/falkordb/data_structures/cow_btree/`) can leave a **non-root branch with a single child** at any `BRANCH_MAX >= 4`. The tree's contents stay right, but the shape is broken: one later single-key `remove` that drains that branch's lone leaf leaves an **empty non-root leaf**, and the next `insert_batch` panics in `Node::min`.

Reachability: since #2350 the native numeric index calls `CowBTree::remove_batch` on every commit that removes entries (`FalkorIndex::merge`, `index/falkordb/falkordb_index.rs:335` → `numeric.rs:121`). At the production fan-out (`LEAF_MAX = BRANCH_MAX = 256`) the shape needs a tree of height >= 3 (more than 65,536 leaves, i.e. millions of entries in one `(label, attribute)` column) and a single commit that drains all but one leaf of a level-1 subtree, so it was **not reproduced through a live query**; the repro below is a Rust unit test at small fan-out. No C comparison applies (C has no equivalent structure). Found while proving #2278's CowBTree in Lean (`proofs/cow_btree/FalkorCowBTree/BugsBatch.lean` on `proofs/lean4-verification`). Different from the two CowBTree bugs in #2893 / #2897.

### Reproduction (`main` @ b033aecc6, `cargo test -p graph --lib`; debug and `--release` behave the same)

```rust
let pairs: Vec<(u64, u64)> = (0..96u64).map(|d| (d, 0)).collect();
let mut t = CowBTree::<2, 4>::from_sorted(&pairs);              // root -> 3 subtrees of 32
t.remove_batch(&(33..64u64).map(|d| (d, 0)).collect::<Vec<_>>());
check_invariants(&t, false);   // panics: "branch must have >= 2 children (a 1-child root should collapse): 1"
assert!(t.remove(32, 0));      // leaves an empty non-root leaf
t.insert_batch(&[(0, 1), (95, 1)]);
```
```
panicked at cow_btree/mod.rs:83:25:
range end index 8 out of range for slice of length 0
```
(without the `check_invariants` line; same message in a release test build).

### Mechanism

- `Node::remove_batch` (`node.rs:483-541`) repairs under-full children

issues.title: [Rust] CowBTree: DOC_BYTES 3/5/6/7 pass the const assert but the second insert panics (latent)
issues.body:
### Summary

`CowBTree<LEAF_MAX, BRANCH_MAX, DOC_BYTES>` (`graph/src/index/falkordb/data_structures/cow_btree/mod.rs`) accepts `DOC_BYTES ∈ 1..=8` in its const assert, but the doc field is read back with `read_width`, which handles only widths `1 / 2 / 4 / 8`. With `DOC_BYTES ∈ {3, 5, 6, 7}` the tree compiles and the **second insert panics**.

Latent: the only production instantiation (`index/falkordb/numeric.rs`) uses a supported width, so no query is affected; the repro is a Rust unit test. No C comparison applies. Found in the Lean model (`LeafAosD.docBytes3_*` on `proofs/lean4-verification`). Different from the two CowBTree bugs in #2893 / #2897.

### Reproduction (`main` @ b033aecc6, `cargo test -p graph --lib`)

```rust
let mut t = CowBTree::<256, 256, 3>::new();   // compiles: assert is DOC_BYTES >= 1 && DOC_BYTES <= 8
assert!(t.insert(1, 1));
assert!(t.insert(2, 2));                      // panics
```
```
debug:   panicked at cow_btree/mod.rs:98:13: assertion `left == right` failed   (debug_assert_eq!(width, 8))
release: panicked at cow_btree/mod.rs:99:33: range end index 16 out of range for slice of length 11
```

### Mechanism

`AosLeaf::doc` (`leaf/aos.rs:35`) calls `read_width(.., DOC_BYTES)`; `read_width` (`mod.rs:88-102`) matches `1 | 2 | 4` and treats every other width as 8. The const asserts in `Default::default` / `new` / `from_sorted` (`mod.rs:140, 162, 180`) only check `1 <= DOC_BYTES <= 8`.

### Expected

Either every `DOC_BYTES` the const assert accepts works, or the unsupported widths fail to compile.

### Suggested fix

Smaller change: tighten the const assert to `DOC_BYTES ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8}` (the widths `read_width` was designed for — "widths are powers of two so every read is a single fixed-size load"). Supporting 3/5/6/7 would need a variable-length read in a hot path for no current user.

issues.title: [Rust] Index on an attribute named `range:x` / `vector:x` reloads from RDB as an index on `x`
issues.body:
### Summary

A range or vector index on an attribute whose name starts with `range:` or `vector:` comes back after an RDB round-trip as an index on the attribute without that prefix. `CREATE INDEX FOR (n:L) ON (n.`range:x`)` reloads as an index on `x`, so the index silently stops covering the attribute it was built for. C keeps `[range:x]`.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

```
redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (:L {x:1})"
redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g 'CREATE INDEX FOR (n:L) ON (n.`range:x`)'
redis-cli DEBUG RELOAD
redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g "CALL db.indexes() YIELD label, properties RETURN label, properties"
```

Rust:
```
L
[x]
```

C (`bin/macos-arm64v8-release/falkordb.so`):
```
L
[range:x]
```

### Mechanism

`decode_index_field` (`src/serializers/mod.rs:641-646`) strips a `range:` / `vector:` prefix from the field name it reads. Since #2459 the encoder (`src/serializers/mod.rs:363-382`) writes the bare attribute name, as C does, so on load the name never carries a RediSearch prefix. The strip only alters user attribute names that happen to start with those strings. It dates from the migration (#2279), before #2459 changed the encoder; every released Rust version (6.0.0+) contains #2459.

### Expected

The attribute name is read back verbatim, as C does.

### Suggested fix

Drop the prefix strip in `decode_index_field` and use the name as read.

issues.title: [Rust] graph.traverse([a]) leaves a out when a has a self-loop
issues.body:
### Summary

`graph.traverse([a])` leaves `a` out of its own result when `a` has a self-loop. C returns it.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

```
GRAPH.UDF LOAD t "falkor.register('ids', function(n){ return graph.traverse([n])[0].map(x => x.id); });"
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (a {id:0})-[:R]->(a), (a)-[:R]->(:B {id:1})"
GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (a {id:0}) RETURN t.ids(a)"
```

| | `t.ids(a)` |
|---|---|
| Rust | `[1]` |
| C | `[0, 1]` |

`node.getNeighbors()` already returns `[0, 1]` on Rust; only `graph.traverse` drops it.

### Mechanism

`js_traverse_impl` (`graph/src/udf/js_classes.rs:743-744`) seeds the BFS `visited` set with the start node, so the self-loop's target (the start node) fails `visited.insert(neighbor_id)` and is never emitted.

### Expected

`[0, 1]`, as C and `getNeighbors()`.

### Suggested fix

Do not pre-mark the start node as visited: it is emitted (once) when an edge reaches it. With the default depth of 1 this only affects self-loops. With `maxDepth > 1` a start node on a cycle is reported once, at the depth it is reached, which is what reachability means everywhere else.

Related, not the same: #3083 / PR #3084 (a self-loop *edge* reported twice).

issues.title: [Rust] NOT over a pattern predicate keeps rows where the inner predicate is null
issues.body:
### Summary

When `NOT` wraps a predicate that mixes a scalar test with a pattern, rows where the inner predicate is `null` pass the filter. `NOT null` is `null`, so these rows should be dropped. C drops them.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (:N {v: 0}), (:N), (:N {v: 5}), (:N)-[:R]->(:M)"
GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (a:N) WHERE NOT (a.v > 1 OR (a)-->()) RETURN count(a)"
GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (a:N) WHERE NOT (a.v > 1 AND (a)-->()) RETURN count(a)"
```

| query | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| `NOT (a.v > 1 OR (a)-->())` | 2 | 1 |
| `NOT (a.v > 1 AND (a)-->())` | 4 | 3 |

In the `OR` case, the node with no `v` and no edge gives `NOT (null OR false)` = `null`, yet Rust counts it. The same happens in the `AND` case for the node with no `v` that has an edge: `NOT (null AND true)` = `null`.

### Mechanism

`Planner::expr_to_plan` (`graph/src/planner/mod.rs:1542-1549`) plans `NOT(complex)` as `AntiSemiApply(input, plan(inner))`. The inner plan passes a row only when the inner expression is `true`, so `AntiSemiApply` passes every row where it is not `true`, which includes `null`. That is two-valued negation, not Cypher's three-valued one.

### Expected

Rows where the negated predicate is `null` are filtered out (Rust 1 and 3 above, as in C).

### Suggested fix

Push the `NOT` down with De Morgan before planning: `NOT (A OR B)` becomes `NOT A AND NOT B`, `NOT (A AND B)` becomes `NOT A OR NOT B`, and `NOT NOT A` becomes `A`. These identities hold in three-valued logic. The leaves are then either `NOT pattern`, where `AntiSemiApply` is correct because a pattern is never `null`, or `NOT scalar`, which becomes an ordinary `Filter` that handles `null` correctly.

### Found by

Lean 4 model of the planner (`proofs/`, ledger entry W4-plan-1).

issues.title: [Rust] Decision: integer division is exact in Rust but goes through double in C (9007199254740993 / 1, 4611686018427387903 / 4611686018427387904 = 1 on C)
issues.body:
### Decision needed: should `Integer / Integer` be exact (Rust) or go through `double` (C)?

C computes `Integer / Integer` by converting both operands to `double`, dividing, and truncating the result back to `int64`. Rust divides the two `i64` values directly. For operands up to 2^53 the answers agree. Above that they differ: C loses the low bits of the dividend, and can even round the quotient up to the next integer. Nothing crashes. This issue is for the decision: **keep exact division in Rust and document the C difference, or copy C.** No PR is attached.

Results: Rust = release build of `main` @ b033aecc6. C = local `master` build of the C module (`bin/macos-arm64v8-release/falkordb.so`, arm64).

| # | Query | Rust | C | Exact truncated quotient |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `RETURN 9007199254740993 / 1` | `9007199254740993` | `9007199254740992` | `9007199254740993` |
| 2 | `RETURN 9007199254740993 / 3` | `3002399751580331` | `3002399751580330` | `3002399751580331` |
| 3 | `RETURN 123456789012345678 / 10` | `12345678901234567` | `12345678901234568` (rounded **up**) | `12345678901234567` |
| 4 | `RETURN 1000000000000000001 / 7` | `142857142857142857` | `142857142857142864` | `142857142857142857` |
| 5 | `RETURN 9223372036854775807 / 2` | `4611686018427387903` | `4611686018427387904` | `4611686018427387903` |

issues.title: [Rust] Decision: UNIQUE constraint key for true vs 1 — C treats them as one value (RediSearch numeric), Cypher equality keeps them distinct
issues.body:
### Decision needed: should a UNIQUE constraint treat `true` and `1` (and `false` and `0`) as the same key?

C enforces UNIQUE through the RediSearch numeric field, and it indexes a Boolean as the number `1.0` / `0.0`. So under a UNIQUE constraint on C, `true`, `1` and `1.0` are one key, and `false` and `0` are another. openCypher says `true = 1` is `false`, and both engines agree on that. Rust's constraint key distinguishes all three today. The planned fix for #2774 will merge `1` and `1.0`, and it has to decide whether to merge Booleans too. **This issue is for that decision: copy C, or follow Cypher equality.** No PR is attached.

Results: Rust = release build of `main` @ b033aecc6. C = local `master` build of the C module (`bin/macos-arm64v8-release/falkordb.so`).

Setup (both engines): `GRAPH.QUERY u "CREATE INDEX FOR (n:P) ON (n.k)"`, then `GRAPH.CONSTRAINT CREATE u UNIQUE NODE P PROPERTIES 1 k` (status `OPERATIONAL` on both). Then the queries below run in order:

| # | Query | Rust | C | Cypher equality |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `CREATE (:P {k: true})` | created | created | — |
| 2 | `CREATE (:P {k: 1})` | created | `unique constraint violation on node of type P` | `true = 1` is `false` → distinct, accept |
| 3 | `CREATE (:P {k: 1.0})` | created (#2774) | violation | `1.0 = 1` is `true` → duplicate of #2, but distinct from `true` |
| 4 | `CREATE (:P {k: false})` | created | created | — |
| 5 | `CREATE (:P {k: 0})` | created | violation | `false = 0` is `false` → accept |
| 6 | `MATCH (n:P) RETURN n.k, typeOf(n.k) ORDER BY id(n)` | `true`/Boolean, `1`/Integer, `1`/Float, `false`/Boolean, `0`/Integer | `true`/Boolean, `false`/Boolean | — |
| 7 | `RETURN true = 1` | `false` | `false` | `false` |

Constraint creation over existing data behaves the same way (fresh graph):

| Steps | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| `CREATE (:P {k: 1}), (:P {k: true})`, then index + `GRAPH.CONSTRAINT CREATE … UNIQUE … k` | `OPERATIONAL` | `FAILED` |

### The same conflation leaks int

issues.title: [Rust] A deleted edge keeps its type after a type is registered by a constraint, so a reused id reports the old type
issues.body:
### Summary

When a relationship type is registered by anything other than an edge write — `GRAPH.CONSTRAINT CREATE ... RELATIONSHIP <new type>`, or `ADD_SCHEMA` on a replica — `relationship_type_matrix` is not widened to the new type count. From then on, deleting an edge does not remove it from that matrix (in a release build; a debug build trips a `debug_assert`). The deleted edge keeps its old type, so when the next edge reuses the id it has two types, and `type(r)` reports the stale one.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (:N)-[:A]->(:N)"
GRAPH.CONSTRAINT CREATE g MANDATORY RELATIONSHIP B PROPERTIES 1 x
GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH ()-[r]->() DELETE r"
GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (a), (b) WHERE id(a) = 0 AND id(b) = 1 CREATE (a)-[r:C]->(b)"
GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH ()-[r]->() RETURN id(r), type(r)"
GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH ()-[r:A]->() RETURN count(r)"
```

| | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| `id(r), type(r)` | `0, A` | `0, C` |
| `count` of `:A` edges | `0` | `0` |

Rust's edge 0 sits in the `C` tensor but has both `A` and `C` in `relationship_type_matrix`; `type(r)` takes the first.

### Mechanism

- `Graph::get_type_id_mut` (`graph/src/graph/graph.rs:1250-1266`) pushes the type and its tensor but does not call `resize()`. `get_relationship_matrix_mut` (`graph.rs:1364-1380`) and `get_label_id_mut` (`graph.rs:1188`) both do, for this reason.
- `delete_relationships` (`graph.rs:2916-2921`) and `delete_implicit_edges` (`graph.rs:3023-3055`) build the removal mask as `relationship_cap x relationship_types.len()`. With the matrix still one column narrower, `remove_mask` → `tombstone_masked` gets `GrB_DIMENSION_MISMATCH`, which is only checked by `debug_assert_eq!` (`graphblas/matrix.rs:990`). In release the removal is skipped.
- Callers of `get_type_id_mut`: `src/commands/constraint.rs:74` (primary) and `graph/src/effects/v3/apply.rs:546` (`ADD_SCHEMA` on a replica), so replicas get the same bug. Bulk insert also calls it, but it resizes before wr

issues.title: [Rust] A deleted node loses labels set or removed earlier in the same query
issues.body:
### Summary

A node deleted by a query is meant to keep all of its details for the rest of that query (the project rule for Rust: a deleted entity keeps everything). Labels the same query added or removed before the `DELETE` are lost: the snapshot is taken from the committed label matrix, not from the query's own view of the node.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

```
GRAPH.QUERY h "CREATE (:A {v: 1})"
GRAPH.QUERY h "MATCH (n:A) SET n:C DELETE n RETURN labels(n), n:C"

GRAPH.QUERY h2 "CREATE (:A {v: 1})"
GRAPH.QUERY h2 "MATCH (n:A) REMOVE n:A DELETE n RETURN labels(n), n:A"
```

| Query | Rust | Expected (Rust rule) | C |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SET n:C DELETE n RETURN labels(n), n:C` | `[A], false` | `[A, C], true` | `[], false` |
| `REMOVE n:A DELETE n RETURN labels(n), n:A` | `[A], true` | `[], false` | `[], false` |

C returns no labels at all for a deleted node. The expected values here follow the agreed Rust behaviour (a deleted entity keeps all its details), so they are the labels the node had in this query just before the `DELETE`, not C's.

### Mechanism

`DeleteOp` snapshots a committed node's labels with `g.get_node_label_ids(id)` — the committed label matrix — in both places:

- `delete_nodes_bulk`, `graph/src/runtime/ops/delete.rs:284`
- `delete_entity`, `graph/src/runtime/ops/delete.rs:464`

The attributes next to them are taken from the pending view (`update_node_attrs` / `get_node_attrs`), but the labels skip `Pending::update_node_labels`. `Runtime::get_node_labels` and `node_has_label_id` then answer from that snapshot.

### Expected

`labels(n)` and `n:L` on a deleted node give the labels as of the `DELETE`, including labels set or removed earlier in the same query.

### Suggested fix

Take the snapshot the same way `Runtime::get_node_labels` builds the live view: committed label ids with `pending.update_node_labels(id, ..)` applied, in both places.

issues.title: [Rust] Tensor::resize shrinking keeps the multi-edge ids of pairs it cuts off (latent)
issues.body:
### Summary

Latent, not reachable from Cypher today. `Tensor::resize` to smaller dimensions drops the forward entries of pairs outside the new bounds but leaves their multi-edge ids in `me`. Those ids then show up as edges with no forward entry: `iter_edges` returns them and `edge_count` counts them.

### Reproduction (`main` @ b033aecc6)

Unit test, added in the linked PR:

```rust
let mut t = Tensor::new(8, 8);
// (0, 1) and (5, 6) are multi pairs, (1, 2) a single one.
t.set_all_from_slices(&[0, 0, 1, 5, 5, 5], &[1, 1, 2, 6, 6, 6], &[10, 11, 12, 20, 21, 22]);
t.flush();
t.resize(4, 4);
```

| | `main` | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `iter_edges()` | `(0,1,10) (0,1,11) (1,2,12) (5,6,20) (5,6,21) (5,6,22)` | `(0,1,10) (0,1,11) (1,2,12)` |
| `edge_count()` | 5 | 3 |
| `multi_pairs()` | 2 | 1 |

No C comparison: C has no equivalent shrink path on its tensors.

### Mechanism

The shrink branch of `Tensor::resize` (`graph/src/graph/graphblas/tensor.rs:814-828`) resizes `m`, `dp`, `dm` and `mt`, but not `me`. `me` is keyed by `compound_key(src, dst)` and is `ME_DIM` rows wide whatever the node count, so a shrink never touches it.

Why it is latent: the only caller that can shrink is `Graph::rebuild_derived_matrices` after an RDB load (`graph.rs:978` → `resize_node_matrices`), and it resizes to `node_cap`, which covers every node id in the graph, so no pair is ever cut off.

### Expected

After a shrink, `me` holds no ids of pairs outside the new dimensions, so `iter_edges`, `edge_count` and `multi_pairs` agree with the forward matrix.

### Suggested fix

In the shrink branch, remove the `me` entries whose `compound_key_inverse` falls outside `nrows x ncols`. It costs one pass over `me`, only on a shrink.

issues.title: [Rust] GRAPH.EFFECT CREATE_NODE with a repeated id is silently de-duplicated instead of refused
issues.body:
### Summary

A client-sent `GRAPH.EFFECT` whose `CREATE_NODE` record names the same node id twice (e.g. ids `[0, 0]`, count 2) is applied as one node and replies `OK`. The same mistake in a `CREATE_EDGE` record has been refused since #2846. A record that says it creates two nodes and creates one is a malformed buffer and should be refused like the edge case.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

v3 payloads (`u8 3 · u8 0` header, then the record), built as in `tests/flow/test_effects_wire.py`:

```
# empty graph; CREATE_NODE count 2, no labels/attrs, IdList [0, 0]
GRAPH.EFFECT dupn "\x03\x00" + CREATE_NODE(0, 0)
GRAPH.QUERY dupn "MATCH (n) RETURN count(n)"

# graph (:A)-[:R]->(:A); CREATE_EDGE count 2, type 0, ids [1, 1], src [0, 0], dst [1, 1]
GRAPH.EFFECT dupe "\x03\x00" + CREATE_EDGE([1, 1], 0, [0, 0], [1, 1])
```

| Record | Rust | 
|---|---|
| `CREATE_NODE` ids `[0, 0]` | `OK`, 1 node created |
| `CREATE_EDGE` ids `[1, 1]` | `effect apply failed: bulk relationship create got 2 ids of which only 1 are distinct; an id names one edge` |

No C comparison: the C module only reads effects up to v2 (`GRAPH.EFFECT version mismatch expected version <= 2 got: 3`).

### Mechanism

`apply_record` for `CreateNode` (`graph/src/effects/v3/apply.rs:207-218`) turns the `IdList` into a `RoaringTreemap` (`ids.to_roaring()`) and passes that set to `Graph::create_nodes`, so a repeated id is merged before anything can see it. `Graph::create_relationships_bulk` (`graph/src/graph/graph.rs:2601-2609`) compares the set size with the list length and refuses on a mismatch; nothing does that for nodes.

### Expected

The buffer is refused with an error naming the duplicate, the graph is unchanged, as for `CREATE_EDGE`.

### Suggested fix

In `CreateNode`, compare `nodes.len()` with the number of ids in the record and return the same kind of error as the edge path.

issues.title: [Rust] Range index on an attribute that also has a fulltext index returns no rows
issues.body:
### Summary

A range index on an attribute that already has a fulltext index never answers correctly. Every range-index lookup on that attribute (equality, range, inline property map, `IN`) returns no rows, on nodes and on relationships. C returns the matching rows.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (:L {s:'foo'}), (:L {s:'bar'}), (:L {s:'dog'})"
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX FOR (n:L) ON (n.s)"
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE INDEX FOR (n:L) ON (n.s)"
```

| Query | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| `MATCH (n:L) WHERE n.s = 'foo' RETURN n.s` | `[]` | `foo` |
| `MATCH (n:L) WHERE n.s > 'c' RETURN n.s` | `[]` | `dog`, `foo` |
| `MATCH (n:L {s:'bar'}) RETURN n.s` | `[]` | `bar` |
| `MATCH (n:L) WHERE n.s IN ['foo','dog'] RETURN n.s` | `[]` | `dog`, `foo` |

Both engines plan `Node By Index Scan`. Numeric attributes (`n.v = 2`, `n.v >= 2`) and relationship indexes (`Edge By Index Scan`) fail the same way. Creating the range index first, then the fulltext one, works.

### Mechanism

An attribute keeps one `Field` per index type in `Index::fields: HashMap<Arc<String>, Vec<Arc<Field>>>`, in creation order. Every query-node builder in `graph/src/index/mod.rs` takes the attribute's first field whatever its type: `build_numeric_range_node` (:1397), `build_string_range_node` (:1426), and `build_query_node` for numeric equality (:1484), string equality (:1496), point (:1554) and array-contains (:1615), all via `self.fields.get(key).and_then(|f| f.first())`. With the fulltext index created first, the numeric/tag/geo node targets the fulltext field's name, which holds no numeric/tag/geo data, so RediSearch returns nothing.

### Expected

The range lookup reads the range field and returns the rows, as in C.

### Suggested fix

Select the attribute's field whose type is `IndexType::Range` (one helper, used at all six sites) instead of the first one.

issues.title: [Rust] Graphs loaded from RDB ignore CACHE_SIZE (always 25)
issues.body:
### Summary

A graph loaded from an RDB gets a query-plan cache of 25 entries whatever `CACHE_SIZE` the module was loaded with. Graphs created at run-time honour it. So after a restart (or `DEBUG RELOAD`, or a replica's full sync) the cache size silently reverts to the default; with `CACHE_SIZE 0` caching comes back on.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

```
redis-server --enable-debug-command yes --loadmodule libfalkordb.dylib CACHE_SIZE 1
redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (:L)"
redis-cli DEBUG RELOAD
redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g "RETURN 1" | grep Cached
redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g "RETURN 2" | grep Cached
redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY g "RETURN 1" | grep Cached
```

Rust: `Cached execution: 0`, `0`, `1` (the cache holds two plans, so a 1-entry cache is not in effect).

C (`bin/macos-arm64v8-release/falkordb.so`, same arguments): `0`, `0`, `0`.

### Mechanism

`src/redis_type.rs:66` hard-codes `DEFAULT_CACHE_SIZE = 25` ("no Redis context available") and passes it to `rdb_load_graph` in `graph_rdb_load` (`:97`), to the multi-key placeholder (`:141`) and in `graphmeta_rdb_load` (`:856`). Every other construction site (`GRAPH.QUERY`, `GRAPH.RESTORE`, `GRAPH.COPY`, `GRAPH.BULK`, ...) reads `CONFIGURATION_CACHE_SIZE`.

### Expected

RDB-loaded graphs use the configured `CACHE_SIZE`, as C does.

### Suggested fix

The load callbacks run on the main thread, so the configured value can be read there: take a `Context` from the IO handle (`RedisModule_GetContextFromIO`) and lock `CONFIGURATION_CACHE_SIZE` with it, replacing the constant.

issues.title: [Rust] UDF node.getNeighbors() with no argument throws "Error converting from js 'undefined'"
issues.body:
### Summary

`node.getNeighbors()` called with no argument throws instead of returning the outgoing neighbours. The config argument is documented as optional, and C accepts the call.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

```
GRAPH.UDF LOAD n "falkor.register('ids', function(n){ return n.getNeighbors().map(x => x.id); });"
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (a {id:0})-[:R]->(a), (a)-[:R]->(:B {id:1})"
GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (a {id:0}) RETURN n.ids(a)"
```

| | result |
|---|---|
| Rust | `UDF Exception: Error converting from js 'undefined' into type 'object'` |
| C | `[0, 1]` |

`n.getNeighbors({})` works on both.

### Mechanism

The shared JS method is `function(config) { return h(this.__falkor_node_id, config); }` (`graph/src/udf/js_classes.rs:195`). It always passes two arguments, so an omitted config reaches the native `js_get_neighbors_entry` (`js_classes.rs:350-353`) as an explicit `undefined`. Its parameter is `Opt<Object>`, which handles a *missing* argument but fails to convert a present `undefined` to `Object`.

### Expected

`[0, 1]`: no config means the defaults.

### Suggested fix

Take the config as `Opt<Option<Object>>` (rquickjs maps `undefined` / `null` to `None`), in `js_get_neighbors_entry` and, for `graph.traverse([n], undefined)`, `js_traverse_entry`.

issues.title: [Rust] Unknown vector similarityFunction accepted at dimension 0; GRAPH.MEMORY error texts differ from C
issues.body:

Two leftovers after #3094 where Rust still answers differently from C:

1. `CREATE VECTOR INDEX … OPTIONS {dimension:0, similarityFunction:'bogus'}` creates the index (and `db.indexes()` reports `similarityFunction: bogus`). C refuses it. With a non-zero dimension Rust refuses, but with a different message than C's.
2. `GRAPH.MEMORY` error replies differ from C: the `SAMPLES` error carries an `ERR ` prefix C does not send, and the wrong-keyword errors have different text.

issues.title: [Rust] GRAPH.UDF LOAD accepts an empty library name (functions uncallable) and an empty script
issues.body:
### Summary

`GRAPH.UDF LOAD "" <script>` is accepted, but the library's functions can never be called. C rejects it with `empty lib name`. Likewise an empty script is accepted (a library with no functions), where C replies `empty script`.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

```
GRAPH.UDF LOAD "" "falkor.register('f', function(){ return 1; });"
GRAPH.QUERY g "RETURN .f()"
GRAPH.UDF LIST
GRAPH.UDF LOAD x ""
```

| | `LOAD ""` | `RETURN .f()` | `UDF LIST` | `LOAD x ""` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rust | `OK` | parse error | lists a library named `""` with function `f` | `OK` |
| C | `empty lib name` | parse error | — | `empty script` |

### Mechanism

`udf_load` (`src/commands/udf.rs:117`) only checks the name's maximum length (`validate_identifier_len`), never that it is non-empty. The repository registers the function as `.f`, which no Cypher function name can spell. No check on the script either.

### Expected

Reject both, with C's messages: `empty lib name`, `empty script` (C `cmd_udf_load.c` checks the name first).

### Suggested fix

In `udf_load`, before the length check: `if lib_name.is_empty() { return Err("empty lib name") }`, `if script.is_empty() { return Err("empty script") }`.

issues.title: [Rust] A list or map subscript is rejected as a WHERE predicate (Expected boolean predicate)
issues.body:
### Summary

A list or map subscript (`l[0]`, `m['k']`) is never accepted as a predicate. `WHERE n.flags[0]` fails with `Expected boolean predicate` before the query runs, even when the element is a boolean. C runs the query and checks the element's type at runtime.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (:N {flags: [true, false]})"
GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (n:N) WHERE n.flags[0] RETURN count(n)"
GRAPH.QUERY g "WITH [true] AS l WHERE true AND l[0] RETURN 1"
GRAPH.QUERY g "WITH {a: true} AS m WHERE m['a'] RETURN 1"
GRAPH.QUERY g "WITH [null] AS l WHERE l[0] RETURN 1"
GRAPH.QUERY g "WITH [1] AS l WHERE l[0] RETURN 1"
```

| query | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| `WHERE n.flags[0]` | `Expected boolean predicate` | 1 |
| `WHERE true AND l[0]` | `Expected boolean predicate` | 1 row |
| `WHERE m['a']` | `Expected boolean predicate` | 1 row |
| `WHERE l[0]` with `l = [null]` | `Expected boolean predicate` | 0 rows |
| `WHERE l[0]` with `l = [1]` | `Expected boolean predicate` | `Type mismatch: expected Boolean but was Integer` |

A slice (`l[0..1]`) and a negation (`-null`) are rejected by both engines, so those already agree.

### Mechanism

`Binder::expr_may_return_boolean` (`graph/src/planner/binder.rs:2329-2339`) lists `ExprIR::GetElement` with the node kinds that can never be boolean. A subscript returns whatever the element is, so it belongs with `Property`, `Variable` and `Parameter`, which are left to the runtime type check.

### Expected

As in C: the query runs, a boolean element filters, `null` drops the row, and any other type is a runtime type error.

### Suggested fix

Move `ExprIR::GetElement` to the "may be boolean" arm. `GetElements` (slice) always returns a list and stays where it is.

### Found by

Lean 4 model of the binder (`proofs/`, ledger entry W4-plan-2).

issues.title: [Rust] db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes/queryRelationships with a non-string label or query error; C returns no rows
issues.body:
### Summary

`db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes` / `queryRelationships` with a non-string label or query fail the whole query. C returns no rows for them.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

```
GRAPH.QUERY ft "CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX FOR (n:W) ON (n.name)"
GRAPH.QUERY ft "CREATE (:W {name:'1'})"
GRAPH.QUERY ft "CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes(1, 2)"
GRAPH.QUERY ft "CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes(null, 'x')"
GRAPH.QUERY ft "CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes('W', 1)"
GRAPH.QUERY ft "CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryRelationships(1, 2)"
```

| | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| `queryNodes(1, 2)` | `fulltext query expects a string label` | empty result |
| `queryNodes(null, 'x')` | `fulltext query expects a string label` | empty result |
| `queryNodes('W', 1)` | `fulltext query expects a string query` | empty result |
| `queryRelationships(1, 2)` | `fulltext query expects a string relationship type` | empty result |

### Mechanism

The planner rewrites these calls to `NodeByFulltextScan` / `EdgeByFulltextScan`. The ops return `Err` when the evaluated label or query is not a `Value::String` (`graph/src/runtime/ops/node_by_fulltext_scan.rs:87,96`, `edge_by_fulltext_scan.rs:92,101`).

### Expected

No rows, as C, the same as querying a label that has no fulltext index (which Rust already answers with no rows).

### Suggested fix

In both ops, return `Ok(None)` (no rows for this input row) instead of `Err` when the label or query is not a string.

Re-checked against C while filing: `db.idx.fulltext.drop` on a label with no fulltext index errors on **both** engines (`Unable to drop index on :Nope: no such index.`), so that one is not a divergence, only a message-text difference (Rust prints `:Nope()`); it is listed with the other output differences in a separate issue.

issues.title: [Rust] Nested lists in a client GRAPH.EFFECT payload reserve memory quadratic in its size (1 MB -> 2.3 GB RSS)
issues.body:
### Summary

A nested-list `SIValue` in a `GRAPH.EFFECT` payload can make the v3 decoder reserve memory that grows with the square of the payload size before it fails. Every client can send `GRAPH.EFFECT`, and the payload is decoded before it is rejected. A 1 MB payload pushes the server to a 2.3 GB peak RSS. The reserved address space grows quadratically, to about 16·(bytes/8)² bytes, which is roughly 260 GB for 1 MB.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

The payload is one `CREATE_NODE` record with one attribute. Its value is `levels` nested `T_ARRAY` headers. Level *k* claims `2·(levels−k−1)` children, which is the most that the bytes after it could hold, so every level passes the width check:

```python
import struct, redis
T_ARRAY = 1 << 3
def payload(levels):
    value = b''.join(struct.pack('<II', T_ARRAY, 2 * (levels - k - 1)) for k in range(levels))
    rec = struct.pack('<IIHHHI', 3, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1) + bytes([0, 0, 1])  # CREATE_NODE, 1 id, attr 0
    return bytes([3, 0]) + rec + value
redis.Redis(port=PORT).execute_command('GRAPH.EFFECT', 'h', payload(LEVELS))
# -> ERR effect apply failed: truncated effects buffer: want 4 bytes, have 0
```

Peak RSS of `redis-server` (`/usr/bin/time -l`, fresh server per row, macOS arm64):

| payload | levels | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|
| none (idle) | 0 | 23.6 MB |
| 128 KB | 16,000 | 291 MB |
| 256 KB | 32,000 | 566 MB |
| 512 KB | 64,000 | 1.13 GB |
| 1 MB | 128,000 | 2.31 GB |

RSS grows by about one touched page per level. The reservations behind those pages add up to the square of the payload. On a host with strict overcommit (`vm.overcommit_memory=2`), an allocation failure aborts the process.

C has no v3 decoder (C `master` is at `EFFECTS_VERSION 2`), so there is nothing to compare against.

stack.push(Frame::List { items: ThinVec::with_capacity(n), left:

issues.title: [Rust] A query may end with WITH and returns its projection (C: Query cannot conclude with WITH)
issues.body:
### Summary

A query whose last clause is `WITH` is accepted and returns the `WITH` projection as its result set. C rejects it, and so does openCypher: a query must end with `RETURN`, an update clause, a procedure call or a non-returning subquery. The same holds inside a `CALL { … }` body.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

| query | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| `MATCH (n) WITH n` | returns every node | `Query cannot conclude with WITH (must be a RETURN clause, an update clause, a procedure call or a non-returning subquery)` |
| `UNWIND [1] AS x WITH x` | `[[1]]` | same error |
| `WITH 1 AS x` | `[[1]]` | same error |
| `CREATE (a) WITH a` | creates the node and returns it | same error, nothing created |
| `MATCH (n) CALL { WITH n MATCH (m) WITH m } RETURN 1` | runs | same error |
| `MATCH (n) CALL { WITH n } RETURN 1` | runs | same error |
| `RETURN 1 AS x UNION WITH 2 AS x` | `All sub queries in a UNION must have the same column names.` | same `cannot conclude with WITH` error |

### Mechanism

`QueryIR::inner_validate` (`graph/src/parser/ast.rs:1271-1274`) handles `With` and `Return` in one arm and accepts both as the last clause. `Match` and `Unwind` in the same function already return the "Query cannot conclude with …" error when nothing follows them.

### Expected

`Query cannot conclude with WITH (must be a RETURN clause, an update clause, a procedure call or a non-returning subquery)`, as in C.

### Suggested fix

Split the `With` arm from `Return`, and return that error when `iter.next()` is `None`, the same way the `Match` and `Unwind` arms do. Validation runs after binding, and the binder's synthetic import `WITH` at the start of a `CALL` body is always followed by the body's own clauses, unless the body is only an import `WITH`, which C rejects too.

### Found by

Lean 4 model of the AST validator (`proofs/`, ledger entry W4-plan-5).

issues.title: [Rust] Failed fulltext CREATE INDEX leaks the RediSearch options block (unsupported language, NUL in a stopword)
issues.body:
### Summary

`Index::create_rs_index` leaks the RediSearch index-options block (~56 bytes, plus any stopword copies) every time it returns an error. A fulltext `CREATE` with an unsupported language or a stopword containing a NUL byte reaches that path, so each failing statement leaks.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

10 000-20 000 failing statements each, then `INFO memory` `used_memory` growth:

| Statement (repeated) | Error | Rust `main` | Control: `OPTIONS {weight:'x'}` (fails earlier) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX FOR (n:L) ON (n.s) OPTIONS {language:'klingon'}` | `Language is not supported: klingon` | +56.0 B/stmt | ~0 B/stmt |
| `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX FOR (n:L) ON (n.s) OPTIONS {stopwords:['a\u0000b']}` | `nul byte found in provided data at position: 1` | +54.2 B/stmt | ~0 B/stmt |

C has no equivalent leak: the `klingon` statement crashes C (#2448), and C accepts the NUL stopword (`Indices created: 1`).

### Mechanism

`graph/src/index/mod.rs:1112` calls `RediSearch_CreateIndexOptions()` (an `rm_calloc`), then three early returns skip `RediSearch_FreeIndexOptions`: the stopword `CString::new(...)?` (:1122), the language `CString::new(...)?` and the `Language is not supported` return (:1141-1143), and the label `CString::new(...)?` (:1151). After `RediSearch_IndexOptionsSetStopwords`, the deep-copied stopwords are lost along with the block.

### Expected

A refused statement leaves memory where it was.

### Suggested fix

Run the fallible `CString` conversions before allocating the options, and free the options on the `SetLanguage` failure path.

issues.title: [Rust] Compressed effects payloads of 4 GiB or more declare a truncated length and never apply on the replica
issues.body:
### Summary

When `EFFECTS_COMPRESSION` is on, a v3 effects payload whose plaintext is 4 GiB or larger is written with its decompressed length truncated to `u32`. The replica uses the declared length as the ceiling for `zstd::bulk::decompress`, so it rejects the frame. The write never applies on the replica, and the divergence guard forces a resync that fails again in the same way. The same truncation affects `comp_len` when the compressed frame is 4 GiB or larger.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

This was not run live, because it needs a 4 GiB payload. It is confirmed by code reading and by a unit test that builds the frame prefix from the lengths alone. `graph/src/effects/v3/records.rs`, `maybe_compress`:

```rust
let plain_len = (buf.len() - HEADER) as u32;   // 4 GiB + 5 -> 5
let comp_len = frame.len() as u32;
```

With that logic extracted unchanged into a helper, the prefix it produces for `plain_len = 2^32 + 5, comp_len = 10` is:

```
left: Some([5, 0, 0, 0, 10, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0])   // declares 5 bytes of plaintext
```

On the reading side, `open_payload` calls `zstd::bulk::decompress(frame, 5)`, which fails with `BadCompression`. `GRAPH.EFFECT` then returns `effect apply failed`, and `divergence_guard::on_failure` forces a resync.

C has no v3 or compression (C `master` is at `EFFECTS_VERSION 2`), so there is no C behaviour to compare against.

### Mechanism

`graph/src/effects/v3/records.rs:1376-1377`. Both lengths are narrowed to `u32` with `as`, with no check.

### Expected

A payload that the `u32` length fields cannot describe is not compressed. It ships uncompressed, which has no length field and applies normally.

### Suggested fix

Narrow with `u32::try_from` and fall back to the uncompressed payload (`maybe_compress` returns `false`) when either length does not fit. Also check the plaintext length before compressing, so that a 4 GiB payload is not compressed only to be thrown away.

issues.title: [Rust] CREATE with a named path as the last clause fails: "Variable _anon_0 not found" (regression from #2829)
issues.body:
### Summary

When a named-path `CREATE` is the last clause and follows another clause, the query fails with `Variable _anon_0 not found` and creates nothing. C creates the pattern. This is a regression from #2829 (eab2722c4), which wraps `CREATE p=…` in a `PathBuilder`. It is the same mechanism as #2993 (MERGE), which now also applies to CREATE.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (:A), (:A)"
```

| query | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| `MATCH (a:A) CREATE p=(a)-[:R]->(:B)` | `Variable _anon_0 not found` | Nodes created: 2, Relationships created: 2 |
| `UNWIND [1,2] AS x CREATE p=(:N {x:x})` | `Variable _anon_0 not found` | Nodes created: 2, Properties set: 2 |
| `MATCH (a:A) CALL { WITH a CREATE p=(a)-[:R]->(:B) } RETURN count(*)` | `Variable _anon_0 not found` | 2; Nodes created: 2, Relationships created: 2 |
| `MATCH (a:A) CREATE p=(a)-[:R]->(:B) RETURN count(*)` (not last) | works | works |
| `CREATE p=(:N)` (only clause) | works | works |

### Mechanism

Since #2829, `plan_clause` plans `CREATE p=…` as `PathBuilder(Create)` (`graph/src/planner/mod.rs:3147-3152`). `plan_query`'s first walk, which finds where the previous clause goes for the last clause, does not step over a `PathBuilder`, while the stitching loop does. So the preceding clause becomes a sibling of the `Create` (`PathBuilder(prev, Create)`) instead of its input, and the `Create` runs without its input rows. This is the planner gap #2993 describes for MERGE.

### Expected

The pattern is created once per input row, as in C, and as when the CREATE is not the last clause.

### Suggested fix

Open PR #3101 (for #2993) adds `IR::PathBuilder(_)` to the first walk in `plan_query` and steps over a PathBuilder in the FOREACH body stitching. That covers CREATE too. Add the CREATE cases above to its tests.

issues.title: [Rust] Virtual-key names can collide (t ^ seq), dropping a graph slice from the RDB save
issues.body:
### Summary

`uuid_v4`, which names the virtual keys a large graph is split into during an RDB save, combines the clock and a per-process counter as `t ^ seq`. Two calls get the same name whenever the clock and the counter changed in the same bits. For example, `t = 4, seq = 2` and `t = 5, seq = 3` both give `a = 6`, and every field of the name derives from `a`. If two virtual keys of one graph collide, the second `vkey_map.insert` replaces the first, and that key's slice of the graph is missing from the save.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

This depends on timing, so it was not reproduced live. On macOS the clock has microsecond resolution, so `t` is always a multiple of 1000. The XOR of two consecutive calls' `t` values is then even, while the XOR of consecutive counter values is odd, so back-to-back calls cannot collide there. On Linux (nanosecond clock), two calls exactly 1 ns apart with an even `t` and an even `seq` collide, and so does any pair where `t1 ^ t2 == seq1 ^ seq2`.

The collision is confirmed on the function itself. With `uuid_v4`'s mixing extracted unchanged into a `const fn uuid_fields(t, seq)`, a compile-time check that `uuid_fields(4, 2) != uuid_fields(5, 3)` fails:

```
error[E0080]: evaluation panicked: virtual key names collide for (t=4, seq=2) and (t=5, seq=3)
```

C names virtual keys with a random UUID (`UUID_New`), so this cannot happen in C.

### Mechanism

`src/redis_type.rs:783-806`: `let a = (t as u64) ^ seq;`. The printed fields are `a >> 32`, `(a >> 16) & 0xFFFF`, `a & 0xFFF`, and two fields of `b = a * K + C`. Everything is a function of `a`, and `a` is not injective in `(t, seq)`.

### Expected

Every call in a process returns a distinct name.

### Suggested fix

Keep the clock and the counter in separate fields: take `a` from `t`, and take the last 48 bits from `seq * K + C` with `K` odd. That is a bijection modulo 2^48, so the names differ for any two distinct `seq` values regardless of the clock.

issues.title: [Rust] A relationship variable repeated in a named-path CREATE or any MERGE pattern is silently dropped (C: already declared)

When an `AND`/`OR`/`XOR` operand is not a boolean at runtime, the error message prints the value in Rust's `Debug` form (`Int(3)`, `String("a")`) and not its type. C, and Rust's own `NOT`, name the type.

issues.title: [Rust] AND/OR short-circuit in projections where C evaluates every operand (false AND (1+2) -> false; C: type error) — needs decision
issues.body:
### Summary

Rust short-circuits `AND`/`OR` everywhere. C short-circuits only in `WHERE` filters. In a projection, C evaluates every operand, so a non-boolean operand or an error on the side that is not needed still fails the query. As a result, the same expression is a type error, or `Division by zero`, on C and a value on Rust. **This needs a decision.**

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

| query | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| `RETURN false AND (1+2)` | `false` | `Type mismatch: expected Boolean or Null but was Integer` |
| `UNWIND [3] AS x RETURN false AND x` | `false` | `Type mismatch: … but was Integer` |
| `UNWIND [3] AS x RETURN true OR x` | `true` | `Type mismatch: … but was Integer` |
| `UNWIND [0] AS x RETURN x <> 0 AND 10/x > 1` | `false` | `Division by zero` |
| `UNWIND [0] AS x WITH x WHERE x <> 0 AND 10/x > 1 RETURN 1` | no rows | no rows (C short-circuits in `WHERE`) |
| `UNWIND [3] AS x WITH x WHERE false AND x RETURN 1` | no rows | no rows |
| `RETURN false AND 1` (literal) | bind-time `Type mismatch: expected Boolean` | type error |

`(x AND false)` with a non-boolean `x` on the left fails on both engines.

### Mechanism

### Summary

The map forms of `date`, `localtime`, `localdatetime` and `duration` do not validate their components. A component that is `null` or a string is treated as absent, a float is truncated, and an unknown key is ignored. C rejects every one of these. A key the user wrote with a bad value therefore quietly becomes a default: `date({year:2020, month:null})` returns `2020-01-01`. **This needs a design decision**, because the fast path cannot currently tell an absent key from a null one (see Mechanism).

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

|---|---|---|
| `RETURN date({year:2020, month:null})` | `2020-01-01` | `month must be an integer value` |
| `WITH {year:2020, month:null} AS m RETURN date(m)` | `2020-01-01` | `month must be an integer value` |
| `RETURN date({year:'2020'})` | `1970-01-01` | `year must be an integer value` |
| `RETURN date({year:2020, month:1.5})` | `2020-01-01` | `month must be an integer value` |
| `RETURN date({year:2020, month:2.0})` | `2020-02-01` | `month must be an integer value` |
| `RETURN localtime({hour:null})` | `00:00:00` | `hour must be an integer value` |
| `RETURN localtime({hour:1.5})` | `01:00:00` | `hour must be an integer value` |
| `RETURN localdatetime({year:2020, hour:null})` | `2020-01-01T00:00:00` | `hour must be an integer value` |
| `RETURN date({year:2020, foo:5})` | `2020-01-01` | `datetime components map contains an unknown key` |
| `RETURN duration({days:null})` | `PT0S` | `days must be a numerical value` |
| `RETURN duration({days:'1'})` | `PT0S` | `days must be a numerical value` |

issues.title: [Rust] Property filter on a var-length relationship after WITH r is a type error; C pushes it into the traversal and returns rows — needs decision
issues.body:
### Summary

A property filter on a variable-length relationship works directly after `MATCH` on both engines, because the optimizer moves it into the traversal as a per-edge filter. After a pass-through `WITH r`, C still moves it there and returns rows. Rust evaluates `r.w` on the bound value, which is a `Path`, and fails with a type error. **This needs a decision**, because C's answer comes from an optimizer rewrite rather than from the expression's meaning: openCypher, and both engines' own `RETURN r.w`, treat `r.w` on a var-length `r` as a type error.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (:A)-[:R {w:1}]->(:B)-[:R {w:2}]->(:C)"
```

| query | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| `MATCH ()-[r*1..2]->() WHERE r.w = 1 RETURN count(*)` | `1` | `1` |
| `MATCH ()-[r*1..2]->() WITH r WHERE r.w = 1 RETURN count(*)` | `Type mismatch: expected Map, Node, Edge, … but was Path` | `1` |
| `MATCH ()-[r*1..2]->() WITH r, 1 AS k WHERE r.w = 1 RETURN count(*)` | type error | `1` |
| `MATCH ()-[r*1..2]->() WITH r ORDER BY size(r) WHERE r.w = 1 RETURN count(*)` | type error | type error (`size` of a Path) |
| `MATCH ()-[r*1..2]->() WITH r RETURN r.w` | type error | type error |
| `MATCH ()-[r*1..2]->() WHERE all(e IN r WHERE e.w = 1) RETURN count(*)` | `Type mismatch: expected List but was Path` | `Type mismatch: expected List or Null but was Edge` |

C's `1` is the path whose every edge has `w = 1`, which is the per-edge filter semantics, and the same answer both engines give without the `WITH`.

### Mechanism

`absorb_edge_filters_into_vlt` (`graph/src/planner/optimizer/absorb_edge_filters_into_vlt.rs`) absorbs a conjunct that reads only the edge alias into `CondVarLenTraverse.edge_filter`, but only when the `Filter` sits directly above the traversal. A `WITH r` (a `Project`) in between stops the absorption, so the filter evaluates `r.w` on the `Path` value. C's filter placement sees through a projection that only passes `r` along.

issues.body:
### Summary

The parser accepts two things that are syntax errors in C and in openCypher, and runs them:

1. A parenthesized `SET`/`REMOVE` target that is not followed by a property lookup: `SET (n.x) = 5` sets `n.x`, `SET (n) = {..}` replaces the property map, `SET (n):L` adds a label and `REMOVE (n):L` removes it.

GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (n) SET (n):L"                    -> Labels added: 1

issues.title: [Rust] A variable named _anon_N collides with an unnamed pattern entity: MATCH (_anon_0:A), (:B) counts 0 (C: 1)
issues.body:
### Summary

The parser names every unnamed node and relationship `_anon_<n>`. That is a plain identifier, so a query can write it too. A user variable spelled that way merges with an unnamed pattern entity: `MATCH (_anon_0:A), (:B)` becomes one node labelled `A` and `B`. Separately, the binder, planner, optimizer and runtime treat any variable whose name starts with `_anon` as anonymous, whatever the rest of the name is. C names unnamed entities `@anon_<n>`, which an unquoted identifier cannot spell.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (:A), (:B)"
GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (_anon_0:A), (:B) RETURN count(*)"        -> 0
GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (x:A), (:B) RETURN count(*)"              -> 1
GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (_anonymous:A) RETURN count(_anonymous)"  -> 0
GRAPH.EXPLAIN g "MATCH (n)-->() RETURN n"                      -> Conditional Traverse | (n)->(_anon_1)
```

C (`bin/macos-arm64v8-release/falkordb.so`):

```
MATCH (_anon_0:A), (:B) RETURN count(*)        -> 1
MATCH (_anonymous:A) RETURN count(_anonymous)  -> 1
GRAPH.EXPLAIN ... (n)-->()                     -> Conditional Traverse | (n)->(@anon_0)

For example, binder 2150 gives every `_anon...` occurrence a fresh variable, so `count(_anonymous)` reads a different variable from the one `MATCH` bound.

### Expected

C's results above.
