Use C's `@anon_` prefix, behind one `AN

issues.title: [Rust] A long clause chain (2000 UNWINDs, ~300 OPTIONAL MATCH ... WHERE) overflows a worker stack and crashes the server (C: runs)
issues.body:
### Summary

A long chain of clauses crashes the server with a stack overflow (raw SIGSEGV, every client disconnected). Every clause puts its operator on top of the previous clause's, so the plan is as tall as the query is long. The optimizer passes, the runtime operator build and every `next()` pull all recurse once per plan level, on a worker thread with Rust's default 2 MiB stack. Parsing, binding and planning are fine: they handle 100 000 chained `UNWIND`s. C runs every shape below.

### Reproduction (release build, `main` @ b033aecc6)

```python
q = " ".join(f"UNWIND [1] AS x{i}" for i in range(2000)) + " RETURN count(*)"
GRAPH.QUERY g q    # -> Connection refused (server gone)
```

Clauses at which `main` dies (bisected; 1 KB-7 KB of stack per plan level):

| Shape (per clause) | Rust `main` crashes at | C |
|---|---|---|
| `UNWIND [1] AS xN` | ~1600 | 5000 runs (33 s) |
| `WITH xN AS xN+1, count(*) AS cN` | ~800 | 2000 runs |
| `OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-->(bN)` | ~460 | 1000 runs (80 s) |
| `OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-->(bN) WHERE bN.v > 0` | ~285 | - |
| `CALL { WITH xN RETURN xN + 1 AS xN+1 }` | ~285 | - |
| `MERGE (aN:M {k: ..})` | ~370 | - |
| `FOREACH (x IN [1] \| SET a.fN = x)` | ~400 | - |
| `GRAPH.EXPLAIN` of 8000 `UNWIND`s | crash in `rebuild_with_hash_joins` (optimizer) | - |

lldb on the 2000-UNWIND crash: `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` in `<UnwindOp as Iterator>::next`, nested once per `UNWIND`, on a pool worker thread.

### Mechanism

- Runtime: each operator holds `child: Box<BatchOp>` and pulls it in `next()` (`graph/src/runtime/ops/unwind.rs` and the rest), so a pull recurses through the whole plan.
- Optimizer: passes such as `replace_cartesian_with_hash_join::rebuild_with_hash_joins` recurse over the plan tree.
- Worker threads come from `thread::spawn` (`graph/src/threadpool.rs:62`), with a 2 MiB stack.
- No check on plan height. The parser's guards (`MAX_NESTING`, `MAX_TREE_DEPTH`) only bound expression and subquery nesting, not how many clauses follow one another.

issues.title: Native index: update the index once per unit of work, not once per write call
issues.body:
Every graph write call that touches an indexed attribute updates the native index on its own: `graph_writes` reads the old values, stages the change and merges it into the column immediately. One Cypher write step makes several such calls (labels, new and existing attributes, deletes), and a replicated effects buffer makes one per record.

Collect a unit of work's native-index changes and apply them once, where its RediSearch documents are published: a Cypher query at the end of each `Commit` segment, a replicated effects buffer at the end of the buffer, `GRAPH.BULK` after each token. The functions in `graph_writes` should only read the graph and record into a buffer owned by the unit of work, carried in its `IndexDocs`. Applying keeps only the last change to each entry, since one write step can add an entry and then remove it (`SET n.v = 5 DELETE n`).

issues.title: [Rust] Support diskless replica loading (repl-diskless-load on-empty-db / swapdb)
issues.body:
## Problem

A replica configured with `repl-diskless-load on-empty-db` or `swapdb` never loads the primary's RDB from the socket when the Rust module is loaded. Redis falls back to writing the payload to disk first, and logs:

```
Skipping diskless-load because there are modules that don't handle read errors.
```

Redis only loads from the socket when every module declares `REDISMODULE_OPTIONS_HANDLE_IO_ERRORS`. `swapdb` additionally requires `REDISMODULE_OPTIONS_HANDLE_REPL_ASYNC_LOAD`. The Rust module declares neither. C declares `HANDLE_IO_ERRORS` since #3141, which closed #3140.

Turning the flags on alone is not enough. It exposes these problems:

1. **`on-empty-db`: an interrupted load corrupts the next one.** When the link drops partway through a graph stored across several keys, `on_loading(LOADING_FAILED)` finalizes only the graphs whose keys all arrived. The half-decoded ones stay in `DECODE_STATE`. On the replica's automatic retry, the first key of the same graph merges into those leftovers. The sync then reports `Finished with success`, but the graph is wrong. Reproduced: property sum `1812450` instead of `2001000`, and 1610 of 2000 edges.
2. **`swapdb`: the load overwrites live state before the swap.** Redis loads into a temporary database and keeps the live one in service until the swap. The module registers loaded graphs in the global `GRAPH_REGISTRY` and installs the snapshot's UDFs during the load. So:
   - an **aborted** load leaves the live graphs unregistered, and once the replica is promoted every write to them aborts with `graph was deleted or replaced while the query was running, aborting`;
   - the aborted load's UDFs replace the live ones;
   - during an **async** load, queries already see the new snapshot's UDFs.
3. **Async loading answers no queries.** During an async load Redis sets `REDISMODULE_CTX_FLAGS_ASYNC_LOADING` *instead of* `LOADING`. `must_run_inline` doesn't route it inline, so queries are blocked and handed to the thread pool.

issues.title: Server crash (SIGSEGV in OpBase_CloneRecord) when a Value Hash Join compares maps whose values have different types
issues.body:
## Summary

A `WHERE` equality between two maps built from independent patterns crashes the server when a value in one map has a different type than the value under the same key in the other map (for example a float against a string). The planner turns the predicate into a `Value Hash Join`. Without a fix, the join confirms a match its own binary search cannot find, ends up with zero intersecting records, and clones a NULL record.

issues.title: `STARTS WITH` / `ENDS WITH` / `CONTAINS` raise on non-string operands instead of returning `null`
issues.body:
**Versions tested** (Docker images, fresh containers, 2026-10-12):

- C engine: **v4.14.8, v4.20.6, v4.20.7, v4.22.0 — all raise** `Type mismatch: expected String or Null but was Integer`
- Rust engine: **v6.0.2 — returns `null`** (correct per the openCypher TCK)
- Neo4j 2026.05.0-community: returns `null`

**Repro — the TCK [8] query verbatim** (the scenario's operand set is all non-string/null — the case the TCK directly specifies), executed live:

```cypher
WITH [1, 3.14, true, [], {}, null] AS operands
UNWIND operands AS op1
UNWIND operands AS op2
WITH op1 STARTS WITH op2 AS v
RETURN v, count(*)
// TCK expectation: single row `null | 36`
// C 4.14.8 / 4.20.7 / 4.22.0: raises `Type mismatch: expected String or Null but was Integer` for the whole query
// Rust 6.0.2: [null, 36]
// (the ENDS WITH / CONTAINS variants of this query: C raises the same error; Rust 6.0.2 returns [null, 36])
```

**Additional observations** (string ↔ non-string mixed operands — *not* covered by Scenario [8]'s all-non-string operand set, so these are supplementary evidence rather than direct TCK coverage; Neo4j and Rust 6.0.2 return `null`, the C engine raises):

```cypher
RETURN 'abc' STARTS WITH 1 AS x    // C: raises  |  Rust 6.0.2, Neo4j: null
RETURN 1 STARTS WITH 'abc' AS x    // C: raises  |  Rust 6.0.2, Neo4j: null
RETURN 'abc' ENDS WITH 1 AS x      // C: raises  |  Rust 6.0.2, Neo4j: null
RETURN 'abc' CONTAINS 1 AS x       // C: raises  |  Rust 6.0.2, Neo4j: null
```

`STARTS WITH null` returns `null` on every version, so only the non-string, non-null operand case diverges.

**Context**

- The affected scenarios are marked `@skip` in this repository's TCK copy (`tests/tck/features/expressions/string/String{8,9,10}.feature`, checked at v4.14.8 / v4.20.7 / master), indicating that these tests are excluded. I could not establish from the skip annotations alone whether the C-engine behavior is intentionally retained or scheduled for remediation.
- This is **not** the #3105 precedence

issues.title: ALL over path nodes traverses branches behind a failed node
issues.body:
# ALL over path nodes traverses branches behind a failed node

### Describe the situation

Hi, FalkorDB developers,

Please consider these two queries:

```cypher
// q1
MATCH p = (s:GspLow {id: 1})-[:GSP_PATH_MANY*1..3]-(t:GspHigh)
WHERE all(n IN nodes(p) WHERE n.keep = true)
RETURN t.uid, length(p);

// q2
MATCH p = (s:GspLow {id: 1})-[:GSP_PATH_FEW*1..3]-(t:GspHigh)
WHERE all(n IN nodes(p) WHERE n.keep = true)
RETURN t.uid, length(p);
```

Both relationship types contain the same valid three-hop path. They differ only in the number of branches behind a node with `keep=false`: 300,000 for `GSP_PATH_MANY`, and one for `GSP_PATH_FEW`. These branches cannot pass either query's node condition. Both queries return the same row on this graph, but q1 takes about 231 times as long as q2. The relationship types are interchangeable for these projected results on the constructed graph, not on arbitrary graphs.

### Which FalkorDB versions are affected?

I ran this case on FalkorDB 4.18.11, which reports module version `41811`, with Redis 8.6.3 in Docker on macOS ARM64. The dedicated container has 4 CPUs and 4 GiB of memory. I used the FalkorDB Python driver 1.7.1 and disabled the result-size cap in this dedicated instance.

### How to reproduce

Create the following graph in an empty dedicated graph. The measured loader creates the 300,000 leaves in consecutive batches of 10,000; the complete native statements are in the accompanying `setup.cypher`.

```cypher
CREATE INDEX FOR (n:GspLow) ON (n.id);

CREATE (s:GspLow {uid:1, id:1, keep:true}),
       (a:GspMiddle {uid:2, keep:true}),
       (b:GspMiddle {uid:3, keep:true}),
       (t:GspHigh {uid:4, keep:true}),
       (c:GspBad {uid:5, keep:false})
CREATE (s)-[:GSP_PATH_MANY]->(a)-[:GSP_PATH_MANY]->(b)-[:GSP_PATH_MANY]->(t)
CREATE (a)-[:GSP_PATH_MANY]->(c)
CREATE (s)-[:GSP_PATH_FEW]->(a)-[:GSP_PATH_FEW]->(b)-[:GSP_PATH_FEW]->(t)
CREATE (a)-[:GSP_PATH_FEW]->(c);

MATCH (c:GspBad {uid:5})
UNWIND range(1, 300000) AS i
CREATE (c)

issues.title: Null-bound variable in a disconnected OPTIONAL MATCH incorrectly expands a Cartesian component
issues.body:
## Summary

When a node variable is bound to `NULL` by an earlier `OPTIONAL MATCH`, using
that variable as a bare node component in a later disconnected
`OPTIONAL MATCH` incorrectly allows the other component to be scanned.

The complete optional pattern cannot match while the already-bound variable is
`NULL`, so it should preserve the input row once. FalkorDB instead emits one
row for every node matched by the disconnected component.

## Environment

- FalkorDB module version: 4.18.1
- Image used at verification time: `falkordb/falkordb-server:latest`

## Minimal Reproduction

```cypher
CREATE (:A {id: 1}), (:A {id: 2}), (:A {id: 3});

OPTIONAL MATCH (n:Missing)
OPTIONAL MATCH (n), (d:A)
RETURN count(*) AS rows;
```

Expected result:

```text
rows
1
```

Actual FalkorDB result:

```text
rows
3
```

Projecting the bindings shows that `n` remains `NULL`, while FalkorDB still
scans all three `d:A` nodes:

```cypher
OPTIONAL MATCH (n:Missing)
OPTIONAL MATCH (n), (d:A)
RETURN n, d.id ORDER BY d.id;
```

```text
n     d.id
NULL  1
NULL  2
NULL  3
```

issues.title: Clarify imported-variable scope across UNION arms inside CALL subqueries
issues.body:
## Documentation gap

The `CALL {}` documentation explains the opening `WITH` import channel, and it
contains `UNION` examples whose arms are self-contained. It does not state
whether variables imported by the opening `WITH` are visible in every later
`UNION`/`UNION ALL` arm, or whether each arm declares a fresh scope.

For example, the documented semantics are not sufficient to predict the scope
of `n` in the second arm here:

```cypher
MATCH (n:Person)
CALL {
  WITH n
  RETURN n.name AS value
  UNION ALL
  RETURN n.id AS value
}
RETURN value;
```

## Requested documentation

Please state explicitly whether an opening import is shared by all union arms
or belongs only to the first arm.

issues.title: [C engine] CASE raises division-by-zero from an unselected branch (4.22.0; Rust 6.0.2 unaffected)
issues.body:
## Description

FalkorDB's C engine raises `Division by zero` from an unselected `CASE` branch, even when the selected branch returns a valid value.

The issue reproduces on C engine 4.22.0 with both constant and row-dependent conditions. Both queries execute successfully on FalkorDB Rust 6.0.2.

This report concerns the C engine only. It does not claim that the current Rust engine is affected.

## Environment

| Engine | Docker image | Graph module | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| C engine | `falkordb/falkordb:v4.22.0` | `42200` | Fails |
| Rust engine | `falkordb/falkordb:6.0.2` | `60002` | Passes |

The graph module versions were confirmed by runtime probes.

## Steps to reproduce

No graph data is required. Execute each query independently.

### Reproducer 1: Constant selected branch

```cypher
RETURN CASE WHEN true THEN 42 ELSE 1 / 0 END AS x;
```

**Expected:**

```text
x = 42
```

**Actual on C 4.22.0:**

```text
Division by zero
```

Rust 6.0.2 correctly returns `42`.

### Reproducer 2: Row-dependent branch selection

```cypher
UNWIND [0, 2] AS d
RETURN d,
       CASE WHEN d = 0 THEN null ELSE 4 / d END AS x
ORDER BY d;
```

**Expected:**

| d | x |
|---|---|
| 0 | `null` |
| 2 | `2` |

**Actual on C 4.22.0:**

```text
Division by zero
```

**Actual on Rust 6.0.2:**

| d | x |
|---|---|

issues.title: `WITH c WHERE r IS NOT NULL` fails with an internal alias lookup error after `OPTIONAL MATCH`
issues.body:
## Description

FalkorDB's C-based engine fails to execute a valid Cypher query when a `WITH`-associated `WHERE` clause references a relationship variable that is not included in the `WITH` projection.

The query is taken from the openCypher TCK `TriadicSelection1` scenario. It fails on **FalkorDB 4.20.1 and 4.22.0**, while FalkorDB 6.0.2 and Neo4j 2026.09 execute it successfully.

This report describes a distinct, reproducible query form. It does not claim that the underlying root cause is independent of previously reported filtered-alias issues.

## Versions

- FalkorDB 4.20.1 (C engine): affected; reproduced once.
- FalkorDB 4.22.0 (C engine): affected; reproduced in three consecutive runs.
- FalkorDB 6.0.2 (Rust engine): not reproduced.
- Neo4j 2026.09: executes successfully as a reference.

## Steps to reproduce

Run the following statements on a fresh graph.

**1. Create the graph**

```cypher
CREATE (a:A {name:'a'})-[:KNOWS]->(b:X {name:'b'}),
       (b)-[:NEXT]->(c:Y {name:'c'});
```

**2. Run the query**

```cypher
MATCH (a:A)-[:KNOWS]->(b:X)-->(c:Y)
OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-[r:KNOWS]->(c)
WITH c WHERE r IS NOT NULL
RETURN c.name;
```

## Expected behavior

The query should execute successfully and return **zero rows**.

The graph contains the two-hop path `a → b → c`, but no direct `KNOWS` relationship from `a` to `c`. Therefore, the `OPTIONAL MATCH` binds `r` to `null`, and the `WHERE r IS NOT NULL` filter eliminates the row.

According to Cypher's `WITH` semantics, its associated `WHERE` may reference a variable from the incoming scope even when that variable is not retained for subsequent clauses.

Reference: https://neo4j.com/docs/cypher-manual/current/clauses/with/

## Actual behavior

FalkorDB 4.20.1 and 4.22.0 return:

```text
_AR_EXP_UpdateEntityIdx: Unable to locate a value with alias r within the record
```

The same query returns zero rows on FalkorDB 6.0.2 and Neo4j 2026.09.

## Additional controls

**Control A — Retain `r` in the projection**

issues.title: 6.0.0 regression: node inserts under a unique constraint are 35-120x slower than 4.20.7 and scale quadratically
issues.body:
Creating nodes of a label that has a unique constraint is far slower on 6.0.0 than on 4.20.7, and the cost per node grows with the number of nodes already in the label.

### Repro

Fresh container, `redis-cli`:

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE INDEX FOR (n:A) ON (n.id)"
GRAPH.CONSTRAINT CREATE g UNIQUE NODE A PROPERTIES 1 id
# wait for db.constraints() to report OPERATIONAL
GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(1,5000) AS i CREATE (:A {id: i})"
GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(5001,10000) AS i CREATE (:A {id: i})"
GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(10001,20000) AS i CREATE (:A {id: i})"
```

### Timings

Wall clock, same machine, Docker on an Apple M2 Max:

| statement | `falkordb/falkordb:v4.20.7` | `falkordb/falkordb:6.0.0` |
|---|---:|---:|
| nodes 1 to 5,000 | 118 ms | 4,300 ms |
| nodes 5,001 to 10,000 | 155 ms | 8,878 ms |
| nodes 10,001 to 20,000 | 307 ms | 36,280 ms |
| 20,000 nodes, same label, no constraint | 11 ms | 26 ms |

On 6.0.0 the second 5,000 take twice as long as the first, and the next 10,000 take four times as long again, so each insert appears to cost time proportional to the nodes already in the label. On 4.20.7 the cost per node stays roughly flat.

The constraint is `OPERATIONAL` before the inserts on both versions, and both reject a duplicate afterwards (`unique constraint violation on node of type A`). String ids behave the same way as integers.

### Impact

A bulk load into a constrained label is impractical. Loading 750,000 nodes this way did not get past the first few tens of thousands; with a plain range index in place of the constraint, the same 1.1M-node load takes about 10 seconds.

### Versions

Graph module 60000 (`falkordb/falkordb:6.0.0`, also `latest`) against 42007 (`falkordb/falkordb:v4.20.7`).

issues.title: 6.0.0 regression: a parenthesised WHERE is answered by a label scan where the index was used
issues.body:
On 6.0.0, a `WHERE` whose conditions are wrapped in parentheses is answered by a label scan, where the same conditions without the parentheses use the index. 4.20.7 uses the index either way.

### Repro

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE INDEX FOR (n:A) ON (n.k)"
GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(1,100000) AS i CREATE (:A {k: i % 1000, s: i % 3})"

GRAPH.PROFILE g "MATCH (n:A) WHERE n.k = 7 AND n.s = 1 RETURN count(n)"
GRAPH.PROFILE g "MATCH (n:A) WHERE (n.k = 7 AND n.s = 1) RETURN count(n)"
GRAPH.PROFILE g "MATCH (n:A) WHERE (n.k = 7) AND n.s = 1 RETURN count(n)"
```

### 6.0.0

```
-- WHERE n.k = 7 AND n.s = 1
Aggregate | Records produced: 1
    Filter | Records produced: 34
        Node By Index Scan | (n:A) | Records produced: 100

-- WHERE (n.k = 7 AND n.s = 1)
Aggregate | Records produced: 1
    Filter | Records produced: 34
        Node By Label Scan | (n:A) | Records produced: 100000

-- WHERE (n.k = 7) AND n.s = 1
Aggregate | Records produced: 1
    Filter | Records produced: 34
        Node By Label Scan | (n:A) | Records produced: 100000
```

### 4.20.7

All three forms give `Node By Index Scan | (n:A) | Records produced: 100`.

The answers are right in every case; only the plan changes. Parameters in place of the literals behave the same way.

### Impact

Query builders commonly parenthesise a group of conditions, so a generated filter on an indexed property scans the label. On a label of 250,000 nodes that is about 24 ms for a lookup that takes 0.3 ms with the index.

### Versions

Graph module 60000 (`falkordb/falkordb:6.0.0`, also `latest`) against 42007 (`falkordb/falkordb:v4.20.7`).

issues.title: 6.0.0 regression: OPTIONAL MATCH of two hops from a bound node is planned from the labelled far end
issues.body:
On 6.0.0, an `OPTIONAL MATCH` of two hops that starts from a node already bound, and names a label on the node it ends at, is planned from the far end: it walks every relationship into nodes of that label and only then joins back to the bound node. 4.20.7 traverses outward from the bound node.

### Repro

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE INDEX FOR (p:P) ON (p.id)"
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE INDEX FOR (o:O) ON (o.id)"
GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(0,19999) AS i CREATE (:P {id: i})"
GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(0,199) AS i CREATE (:O {id: i})"
GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(0,19999) AS i MATCH (p:P {id: i}) MATCH (o:O {id: i % 200}) CREATE (p)-[:M]->(o)"
GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(0,19999) AS i MATCH (p:P {id: i}) MATCH (f:P {id: (i + 1) % 20000}) CREATE (p)-[:F]->(f)"

GRAPH.PROFILE g "MATCH (p:P {id: 7}) OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:F]->()-[:M]->(o:O) RETURN count(o)"
```

### 6.0.0

```
Node By Index Scan | (p:P) | Records produced: 1, Execution time: 0.04 ms
    Conditional Traverse | (_anon_1)<-(p:P) | Records produced: 1, Execution time: 2.35 ms
        Conditional Traverse | (o)<-(_anon_1) | Records produced: 20000, Execution time: 2.55 ms
```

All 20,000 `M` relationships are read to find one.

### 4.20.7

```
Optional Conditional Traverse | (p)->(o:O) | Records produced: 1, Execution time: 0.26 ms
    Node By Index Scan | (p:P) | Records produced: 1
```

### What does and does not trigger it on 6.0.0

| query | plan |
|---|---|
| `MATCH (p:P {id: 7}) OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:F]->()-[:M]->(o:O)` | from the far end, 20,000 records |
| `MATCH (p:P {id: 7}) OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:F]->()-[:M]->(o)` (no label on `o`) | from `p`, 1 record |
| `MATCH (p:P {id: 7}) MATCH (p)-[:F]->()-[:M]->(o:O)` (not optional) | from `p`, 1 record |
| `MATCH (p:P {id: 7})-[:F]->(:P)-[:M]->(o:O)` (one pattern) | from `p`, 1 record |
| `MATCH (p:P {id: 7}) OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:M]->(o:O)` (one hop) | from `p`, 1 record |

issues.title: UDF value conversion recurses without a depth limit
issues.body:
Converting values between the engine and a UDF (`js_to_value` / `value_to_js` in `graph/src/udf/type_convert.rs`) recursed once per nesting level with no limit. A UDF returning a deeply nested array or object, or an array that contains itself, exhausted the query thread's stack and crashed the server.

Expected: a value nested past a fixed depth is a query error, and the server keeps running.

Tracked as GHSA-frmf-ffvc-mxx5.

issues.title: GRAPH.RESTORE decodes nested values without a depth limit
issues.body:
`GRAPH.RESTORE` decodes nested array values recursively (`Value::decode` in `graph/src/runtime/value.rs`) with no depth limit. A payload with tens of thousands of nested arrays exhausts the stack and crashes the server. Property writes and `GRAPH.BULK INSERT` also accept list values of any depth, which the decoder must later load back.

Expected: a value nested past a fixed depth is refused with an error on restore, property write and bulk insert, and the server keeps running.

Tracked as GHSA-mwvh-8fq5-x2j8.

issues.title: UNWIND before MATCH ... WHERE ... MATCH is dropped from the plan, query silently returns 0 rows
issues.body:
### Summary

When an `UNWIND` variable is used in the `WHERE` of a node-only `MATCH`, and a second `MATCH` then expands from that node, the planner drops the `Unwind` operation. The filter is kept but reads a variable nothing produces, so the query returns 0 rows with no error.

Seen on `falkordb/falkordb:6.0.2` (`sha256:107455e8…`) and on today's `falkordb/falkordb:edge` (`sha256:a8f008dc…`).

### Steps to reproduce

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (:Fact {id: 'billing-v1'})<-[:PREMISE]-(:Link {id: 'l1'})"
```

| query | expected | got |
|---|---|---|
| `UNWIND ['billing-v1'] AS x MATCH (n:Fact) WHERE n.id = x MATCH (n)<-[:PREMISE]-(l) RETURN count(l)` | 1 | **0** |
| `UNWIND [0] AS nid MATCH (n) WHERE id(n) = nid MATCH (n)<-[:PREMISE]-(l) RETURN count(l)` | 1 | **0** |
| same as the first, with `WITH n` between the two matches | 1 | 1 |
| `UNWIND ['billing-v1'] AS x MATCH (n:Fact {id: x}) MATCH (n)<-[:PREMISE]-(l) RETURN count(l)` | 1 | 1 |
| `MATCH (n:Fact) WHERE n.id = 'billing-v1' MATCH (n)<-[:PREMISE]-(l) RETURN count(l)` | 1 | 1 |

The plan for the first query has no `Unwind` at all:

```
GRAPH.EXPLAIN g "UNWIND ['billing-v1'] AS x MATCH (n:Fact) WHERE n.id = x MATCH (n)<-[:PREMISE]-(l) RETURN count(l)"
Aggregate
    Filter
        Conditional Traverse | (n)<-(l)
            Node By Label Scan | (n:Fact)
```

issues.title: Segfault (NULL deref) in EnforceUniqueEntity when a UNIQUE-constrained string value is empty or whitespace-padded
issues.body:
Creating or updating a node/edge whose UNIQUE-constrained string property is empty, all-whitespace, or has leading/trailing whitespace crashes the server with a segmentation fault during write-commit constraint enforcement.

These values don't round-trip through the RediSearch TAG index (it trims surrounding whitespace and can't store an empty token), so the "find myself in the index" lookup in EnforceUniqueEntity returns NULL and the result is dereferenced.

The guarding ASSERT is compiled out in release builds, so production hits the raw NULL deref.

issues.title: Consecutive MATCH clauses are illegally fused into a single isomorphism scope, erroneously enforcing relationship uniqueness across separate MATCH clauses
issues.body:
**Version**
FalkorDB 6.0.2 Latest

**Environment**
Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS x86_64

**Bug Description**
According to the openCypher specification, relationship uniqueness (isomorphism) is scoped strictly per MATCH clause: while a single clause MATCH (a)-[r1:E]->(b), (a)-[r2:E]->(b) requires r1 <> r2, two separate clauses MATCH (a)-[r1:E]->(b) MATCH (a)-[r2:E]->(b) evaluate their relationship uniqueness independently and join on the bound nodes a and b. Consequently, separating two MATCH clauses with a pass-through WITH a, b, r1 is a pure relational identity transformation.

However, FalkorDB erroneously merges consecutive MATCH clauses into a single relationship uniqueness scope when no WITH clause separates them. On a graph with a single edge (1)-[:E]->(2), MATCH (a:V)-[r1:E]->(b:V) MATCH (a)-[r2:E]->(b) enforces r1 <> r2 across clauses and returns 0, whereas the semantically equivalent query with WITH a, b, r1 (as well as Neo4j and Memgraph on both queries) correctly returns 1.

**To Reproduce**

```
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g_fusion_mre "MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n"
1) 1) "Cached execution: 0"
   2) "Query internal execution time: 0.147782 milliseconds"
   3) "Graph version: 1"
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g_fusion_mre "CREATE (:V {id: 1})-[:E]->(:V {id: 2})"
1) 1) "Labels added: 1"
   2) "Nodes created: 2"
   3) "Properties set: 2"
   4) "Relationships created: 1"
   5) "Cached execution: 0"
   6) "Query internal execution time: 1.073790 milliseconds"
   7) "Graph version: 2"
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g_fusion_mre "MATCH (a:V)-[r1:E]->(b:V) WITH a, b, r1 MATCH (a)-[r2:E]->(b) RETURN count(r1) AS cnt_with_barrier"
1) 1) "cnt_with_barrier"
2) 1) 1) (integer) 1
3) 1) "Cached execution: 0"
   2) "Query internal execution time: 0.420409 milliseconds"
   3) "Graph version: 2"
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g_fusion_mre "MATCH (a:V)-[r1:E]->(b:V) MATCH (a)-[r2:E]->(b) RETURN count(r1) AS cnt_multi_match"

issues.body:
## Summary

A read-only query crashes the server (SIGSEGV, exit code 139) when an `IN` list on an indexed node property contains a string that is a stopword of the label's full-text index.

## Environment

- `falkordb/falkordb:latest`, image config digest `sha256:620a4bff89fe089f9218886696a523f5b4bf033e0603ffb534255c8d4bf66525` (FalkorDB 4.18.11, Redis 8.6.3)
- Seen in production through graphiti-core 0.28.2, which creates full-text indexes on `Episodic`/`Entity`/`Community` with a stopword list

```
GRAPH.QUERY t "CALL db.idx.fulltext.createNodeIndex({label:'L', stopwords:['a']}, 'x')"
GRAPH.QUERY t "CREATE INDEX FOR (n:L) ON (n.u)"
GRAPH.QUERY t "CREATE (:L {u:'a'}), (:L {u:'b'})"
GRAPH.RO_QUERY t "MATCH (n:L) WHERE n.u IN ['b'] RETURN n.u"   -- works
GRAPH.RO_QUERY t "MATCH (n:L) WHERE n.u IN ['a'] RETURN n.u"   -- server crashes
```

Reproduced on a fresh container on 2026-10-15: the last query ends the process with exit code 139 (not OOM).

QueryNode_AddChildren+0xf4
QueryNode_AddChild
Index_BuildQueryTree

issues.title: algo.WCC and algo.pageRank fail with `-1000` when the nodeLabels projection holds exactly one node (6.0.2)
issues.body:
### Summary

`algo.WCC({nodeLabels: [...]})` and `algo.pageRank('<label>', null)` return an error instead of a result when exactly one node matches the label. This happens however many other nodes the graph has. With zero labelled nodes see #3056 (`-6`). With two or more nodes, both procedures answer correctly.

### Steps to reproduce

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (:Node {id:'a'}), (:Other {id:'b'}), (:Other {id:'c'})"

GRAPH.RO_QUERY g "CALL algo.WCC({nodeLabels:['Node']}) YIELD node, componentId RETURN node.id, componentId"
(error) LAGr_ConnectedComponents failed: -1000

GRAPH.RO_QUERY g "CALL algo.pageRank('Node', null) YIELD node, score RETURN node.id, score"
(error) LAGr_PageRank failed: -1000
```

Controls on 6.0.2:

| query | result |
|---|---|
| same graph, `algo.labelPropagation({nodeLabels:['Node']})` | `a, 0` (correct) |
| same graph, `algo.WCC({relationshipTypes:['R']})` (no label filter) | `a 0`, `b 1`, `c 2` (correct) |
| graph with a single `(:Node {id:'a'})`, `algo.WCC(null)` or `algo.WCC({})` | `a, 0` (correct) |
| graph with a single `(:Node {id:'a'})`, `algo.WCC({nodeLabels:['Node']})` | `-1000` |
| two `:Node` nodes, no relationships, `algo.WCC({nodeLabels:['Node']})` | `a 0`, `b 1` (correct) |

### Expected

One row: `a` in its own component (WCC) and one row with its score (pageRank), as `labelPropagation` already returns.

### Notes

This looks like the 1x1 case of the compact matrix built for a `nodeLabels` projection. #3056 is the 0x0 case and #3029 covers ids under `nodeLabels`. Our case comes up naturally when the projected set is computed per request (for example, a time window that holds a single alert).

### Workaround

Add one isolated anchor node with the label, so the projection always holds at least two nodes, and drop it from the results.

### Environment

`falkordb/falkordb:6.0.2` @ `sha256:107455e862a824e45e8e9f5a7fbfdf5e00a08b14e13eae2577c72fd9e3f59ba6` (graph module 60002), default config, Docker on Linux x86_64.

```python
g.query("CREATE (:S {n:'a'})-[:D]->(:S {n:'b'})-[:D]->(:S {n:'c'})")

g.query("MATCH (x:S {n:'a'})-[:D*1..$d]->(y) RETURN y.n", {"d": 3})
# ResponseError: Encountered unhandled type in inlined properties.

g.query("MATCH (x:S {n:'a'})-[:D*1..3]->(y) RETURN y.n")   # [['b'], ['c']]
g.query("MATCH (x:S {n:$n}) RETURN x.n", {"n": "a"})       # [['a']], parameters work elsewhere
```

Expected: the bound accepts an integer parameter, or the error says that variable-length bounds must be literals.
Our workaround: validate the depth as an integer from 1 to 4 in code and format it into the pattern.
Related, but not the same: #1916 (same error text when a parameter is used as inlined pattern properties).

issues.title: 6.0.2: after `OPTIONAL MATCH ... WITH n, count(...) AS c WHERE ...`, a filter on a node bound by the next MATCH drops every row (4.22 returns it)
issues.body:
Found while writing a "decisions that only one person wrote" query for Graph Hacks; our two-engine test matrix caught it.

Graph: `CREATE (:P {name: 'ana'})-[:D {v: 5}]->(:Dec {id: 'd1'})`

```cypher
MATCH (d:Dec {id: 'd1'})
OPTIONAL MATCH (:Dec)-[s:S]->(d)
WITH d, count(s) AS c WHERE c = 0
MATCH (x)-[r:D]->(d) WHERE x.name = 'ana'
RETURN count(r)
```

| Variant | 6.0.2 | 4.22.0 |
|---|---|---|
| filter on the new node `x.name = 'ana'` (above) | 0 | 1 |
| `x.name IS NOT NULL` | 0 | 1 |
| filter on the new edge instead, `r.v > 0` | 1 | 1 |
| no `WHERE` after the `WITH` | 1 | 1 |
| `WITH d, count(*) AS c WHERE c = 1`, no `OPTIONAL MATCH` | 1 | 1 |
| filter moved to a later `WITH x, r WHERE x.name = 'ana'` | 1 | 1 |

Expected: 1 on both. It looks like `x` is seen as null by the `WHERE` that follows the next `MATCH`, only when the previous `WITH` has a `WHERE` and follows an `OPTIONAL MATCH` with an aggregate.
Script with all six variants: https://github.com/retailbox-automation/what-leaves-with-them/blob/main/spike/with_where_repro.py

issues.title: 6.0.2 regression: OPTIONAL MATCH with WHERE after an aggregating WITH returns null (works in 4.22.0)
issues.body:
## What happens

On FalkorDB 6.0.2, an `OPTIONAL MATCH ... WHERE` that comes right after an aggregating `WITH` returns null, even though a matching node exists. There's no error, just missing data.

The same query works on 4.22.0.

## Environment

- FalkorDB 6.0.2 (module version 60002), Docker image `falkordb/falkordb:latest` built 2026-10-08
- Reproduced with `redis-cli`, and also through the `falkordb` npm client 6.8.0
- Works on the Docker image `falkordb/falkordb:v4.22.0`

## Steps to reproduce

```cypher
CREATE (p:Person {email:'x'}),
       (r:Rule {status:'revoked', decided_at: 123})-[:SCOPED_TO]->(p)
```

```cypher
MATCH (p:Person)
OPTIONAL MATCH (r0:Rule)-[:SCOPED_TO]->(p)
WITH p, count(r0) AS n
OPTIONAL MATCH (r:Rule)-[:SCOPED_TO]->(p)
WHERE r.status = 'revoked'
RETURN n, r.decided_at AS e
```

**Expected:** `n = 1, e = 123`
**Actual on 6.0.2:** `n = 1, e = null`
**On 4.22.0:** `n = 1, e = 123`

## When it happens

All three of these have to be true:

1. There are two MATCH clauses before an aggregating `WITH`. The first one can be a plain `MATCH` or an `OPTIONAL MATCH`.
2. An `OPTIONAL MATCH` comes right after that `WITH`.
3. That `OPTIONAL MATCH` filters on its new variable, either with `WHERE r.status = ...` or an inline map like `{status:'revoked'}`.

Each of these changes makes the query return the right answer:

- removing the `WHERE`
- filtering on `p` instead of `r`
- having only one MATCH before the `WITH`
- using a `WITH` that doesn't aggregate
- adding an extra `WITH p, n` after the aggregation
- changing the second clause to a mandatory `MATCH`

## Query plan

The filter seems to run before `r` is bound, so it never matches.

6.0.2 (wrong):

```text
Project
    Apply
        Aggregate
            Apply
                Node By Label Scan | (p:Person)
                Optional
                    Conditional Traverse | (r0)->(p:Person)
                        Argument
        Optional
            Conditional Traverse | (r)->(p:Person)

issues.title: `MATCH (n) WHERE id(n) = 0` returns a node on an empty graph
issues.body:
## Summary

On a graph that has never had a node, looking up a node by id 0 returns a node that does not
exist. It has no labels and no properties. Trying to delete it fails with an internal error that
asks for the bug to be reported. Expected: no rows.

## Steps to Reproduce

```
GRAPH.QUERY g "RETURN 1"                                    // create an empty graph
GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (n) RETURN count(n)"                    // 0
GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (n) WHERE id(n) = 0 RETURN id(n), labels(n), properties(n)"
// 0, [], {}   <- one row is returned (expected: no rows)
```

- The plan is `Project <- NodeByIdSeek`. The seek does not seem to check whether id 0 was ever
  allocated.
- The range form of the seek has the same problem: `WHERE id(n) >= 0` and `WHERE id(n) < 3` also
  return id 0.
- Writing to that phantom node fails: `MATCH (n) WHERE id(n) = 0 DELETE n` answers
  `internal error in the node id space: 0 was never allocated here. No part of this write was
  applied. This is a bug in FalkorDB rather than a problem with the query  please report it`.
- These cases work correctly (no rows):
  - `id(n) = 5` on the empty graph
  - `id(n) IN [0, 1]` on the empty graph
  - `MATCH (n) RETURN id(n)` on the empty graph
  - a deleted id on a non-empty graph
  - id 0 after a node was created and then deleted
- So the problem only appears for id 0 in a graph that has never allocated a node.

## Environment

- FalkorDB 6.0.2 (`falkordb/falkordb:6.0.2` Docker image, module version 60002)
- Redis 8.10.2
- Reproduced with `redis-cli`, no client library involved

issues.title: Relationship isomorphism (edge uniqueness) is erroneously dropped in a single MATCH clause when relationship variables are anonymous
issues.body:
**Version**
FalkorDB 6.0.2 Latest

**Environment**
Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS x86_64

**Bug Description**
According to the openCypher specification's Relationship Isomorphism rule, a single MATCH pattern cannot traverse the exact same physical relationship twice. In a simple graph without parallel edges, a pattern that loops back via the same edge, such as MATCH (u)-[:INC]->(e)<-[:INC]-(u), must return 0.However, FalkorDB drops this isomorphism constraint when the relationship variables are omitted (anonymous). In such cases, the query planner appears to degrade the pattern into an unconstrained matrix multiplication (evaluating the trace of the incidence matrix product $B \cdot B^T$), incorrectly returning 6 instead of 0.This AST/Planner inconsistency is proven by the fact that simply naming the variables (-[r1:INC]-> ... <-[r2:INC]-) restores the expected isomorphism check and correctly returns 0.

**To Reproduce**
```
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n"
1) 1) "Cached execution: 0"
   2) "Query internal execution time: 0.132911 milliseconds"
   3) "Graph version: 1"

// 1. Create a simple bipartite incidence graph (6 physical edges total)
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (v1:V {id: 1}), (v2:V {id: 2}), (v3:V {id: 3}), (e1:Edge), (e2:Edge), (e3:Edge), (v1)-[:INC]->(e1)<-[:INC]-(v2), (v2)-[:INC]->(e2)<-[:INC]-(v3), (v3)-[:INC]->(e3)<-[:INC]-(v1)"

issues.title: The IN operator fails to perform value-based equality checks for nested lists (tuples), silently evaluating to false
issues.body:
**Version**
FalkorDB 6.0.2 Latest

**Environment**
Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS x86_64

**Bug Description**
According to the openCypher specification, equality and list inclusion checks (such as the IN operator) must perform value-based deep equality for complex types like lists/arrays.

When evaluating whether a dynamically constructed list exists within an aggregated list of lists (e.g., [a.id, b.id] IN [[1, 2], [2, 3]]), the evaluator should return true if the elements match. However, FalkorDB silently evaluates this to false and drops all rows. This strongly suggests that the scalar expression evaluator is incorrectly performing pointer/reference equality rather than deep value comparisons for nested lists.


**To Reproduce**
```
// 1. Setup a simple 3-node, 2-edge graph
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g_tuple_in "MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n"
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g_tuple_in "CREATE (v1:V {id: 1}), (v2:V {id: 2}), (v3:V {id: 3}), (v1)-[:E]->(v2), (v2)-[:E]->(v3)"

// 2. Direct pattern match (Returns 2 as expected)
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g_tuple_in "MATCH (a:V)-[:E]->(b:V) RETURN count(*) AS match_direct"
1) 1) "match_direct"
2) 1) 1) (integer) 2

// 3. Tuple filtering via IN operator (BUG: Returns 0)
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g_tuple_in "MATCH (x:V)-[:E]->(y:V) WITH collect([x.id, y.id]) AS valid_pairs MATCH (a:V), (b:V) WHERE [a.id, b.id] IN valid_pairs RETURN count(*) AS match_via_tuple_in"
1) 1) "match_via_tuple_in"
2) 1) 1) (integer) 0

```

**Expected Behavior**
The IN operator must evaluate nested lists by comparing their values, not their memory references. The second query is logically equivalent to the first and must return 2.

Verification on other openCypher engines:
Neo4j 5.x: Returns 2
Memgraph 3.x: Returns 2

**Actual Behavior**
FalkorDB returns 0. The IN operator fails to match identical lists when evaluating [a.id, b.id] IN [[1, 2], [2, 3]], breaking all queries that rely on composite key filtering or tuple-based subset assertions.

issues.title: Read-only graph ACLs from the docs (`%R~pattern`) refuse `GRAPH.RO_QUERY` on 6.0.2
issues.body:
### Summary

The ACL page (https://docs.falkordb.com/commands/acl) describes `%R~<pattern>` as read-only access to a graph, with two examples: `+@all ~app1:* %R~app2:*` and `ACL SETUSER reader on >pass +GRAPH.RO_QUERY %R~*`. On 6.0.2 both refuse a plain `GRAPH.RO_QUERY` with `NOPERM No permissions to access a key`. Graph commands seem to declare their key as read-write, so a read-only key pattern never matches.

### Reproduction

```
GRAPH.QUERY app2:users "CREATE (:U)"
ACL SETUSER reader_doc on >pass +GRAPH.RO_QUERY %R~*
AUTH reader_doc pass
GRAPH.RO_QUERY app2:users "MATCH (n) RETURN count(n)"
-> NOPERM No permissions to access a key
```

Same result for `ACL SETUSER rw_doc on >pass +@all ~app1:* %R~app2:*` reading `app2:users`.
`ACL LOG` shows `reason: key`, `object: app2:users`.

### Expected

`GRAPH.RO_QUERY` succeeds; `GRAPH.QUERY` with a write clause is refused.

### Workaround that works on 6.0.2

```
ACL SETUSER agent on >pass resetkeys -@all +@connection +INFO \
    ~app1:* +GRAPH.QUERY +GRAPH.RO_QUERY \
    (~app2:* +GRAPH.RO_QUERY)
```

Reads of `app2:*` succeed, `GRAPH.QUERY app2:users "CREATE ..."` is refused, and a write sent through
`GRAPH.RO_QUERY` is rejected by the engine. `+INFO` is needed because clients call `INFO` on connect.
`ACL DRYRUN <user> GRAPH.RO_QUERY app2:users ...` checks a rule set safely.

### Environment

`falkordb/falkordb:6.0.2` (module ver 60002), `redis_version:8.10.2`.

### Suggestion

Either declare a read-only key spec for `GRAPH.RO_QUERY` (and the other read commands) so `%R~` works as documented, or show the selector form on the ACL page. Happy to open a docs PR with the selector example.

### Evidence

Reproduced on a fresh `falkordb/falkordb:6.0.2` container with a self-contained script that starts a throwaway container, runs every step, prints the transcript below and removes the container: [`acl_readonly.sh`](https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/lineage/blob/main/docs/upstream/repro/acl_readonly.sh).

issues.body:
### Summary

While a library is being replaced with `GRAPH.UDF LOAD REPLACE`, queries that call its functions can fail with
`Unknown function '<lib>.<fn>'`, even when the new code defines the same functions.

### Reproduction

1. `GRAPH.UDF LOAD repro "function recency(d, a, h) { ... } falkor.register('recency', recency);"`
2. `GRAPH.QUERY g "UNWIND range(1, 2000) AS i CREATE (:N {dates: ['2025-01-01','2025-06-01']})"`
3. Client A loops on `GRAPH.UDF LOAD REPLACE repro "<same code>"`.
4. Clients B to G loop on `GRAPH.RO_QUERY g "MATCH (n:N) RETURN sum(repro.recency(n.dates, '2026-10-16', 180))"`.

Over 60 s on a fresh container: 28,168 replaces and 32,227 queries, 3 of which failed with
`Unknown function 'repro.recency'` (timestamps in the attached transcript). It is intermittent: across four runs we saw between 1 and 6 failures per minute. A self-contained script that reproduces it is attached (`udf_replace_race.py`: starts a throwaway container, runs the loops, prints a transcript, removes the container).

### Expected

A replace is atomic: a query sees either the old library or the new one.

### Environment

`falkordb/falkordb:6.0.2` (module ver 60002), `redis_version:8.10.2`.

### Evidence

Reproduced on a fresh `falkordb/falkordb:6.0.2` container with a self-contained script that starts a throwaway container, runs every step, prints the transcript below and removes the container: [`udf_replace_race.py`](https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/lineage/blob/main/docs/upstream/repro/udf_replace_race.py).

issues.title: MERGE after two aggregations returns a node of an earlier MERGE's label instead of its own (silent wrong write)
issues.body:
## Summary

A `MERGE` that follows two aggregations returns the node bound by an earlier `MERGE` (a different label) instead of matching or creating its own node. No error is raised; any `SET` after it writes to the wrong node.

## Environment

- `falkordb/falkordb:6.0.0` (digest `sha256:92fbda814970a648b1fd80835bff221766bccd0f0ce958bc58a62976fea06620`), Redis 8.10.2, `graph ver 60000`
- `docker run -d --rm --name falkor-repro falkordb/falkordb:6.0.0`, queries via `redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY`

## Repro (empty graph)

```
> GRAPH.QUERY g3 "UNWIND [{id:'a1'}] AS r0 MERGE (a:A {id: r0.id}) WITH count(*) AS c0 UNWIND [{id:'b1'}] AS r1 MERGE (b:B {id: r1.id}) WITH b, r1 WITH count(*) AS c1 UNWIND [{id:'c1'}] AS r2 MERGE (c:C {id: r2.id}) RETURN labels(c), c.id"
labels(c)
c.id
[B]
b1
Labels added: 3
Nodes created: 2
Properties set: 2

> GRAPH.QUERY g3 "MATCH (n) RETURN labels(n), n.id"
[A]  a1
[B]  b1

`[C], 'c1'` is returned, and three nodes exist: `A{a1}`, `B{b1}`, `C{c1}` (Neo4j / openCypher semantics).

issues.title: Carrying count(*) through later aggregations then UNWIND of a collected list: 'Type mismatch … but was Integer'
issues.body:
## Summary

Carrying a `count(*)` as a grouping key through later aggregations, then unwinding a collected list, fails with `Type mismatch: expected Map, Node, Edge, Datetime, Date, Time, Duration, Null, or Point but was Integer`.

## Environment

- `falkordb/falkordb:6.0.0` (digest `sha256:92fbda814970a648b1fd80835bff221766bccd0f0ce958bc58a62976fea06620`), Redis 8.10.2, `graph ver 60000`
- queries via `redis-cli GRAPH.QUERY`

## Repro (empty graph)

```
> GRAPH.QUERY g1 "CYPHER rows0=[{id:'a1'}] rows1=[{id:'b1'}] rows2=[{id:'c1'}] UNWIND $rows0 AS r0 MERGE (a:A {id: r0.id}) WITH count(*) AS c0 UNWIND $rows1 AS r1 MERGE (b:B {id: r1.id}) WITH c0, count(*) AS c1 UNWIND $rows2 AS r2 MERGE (c:C {id: r2.id}) WITH c0, c1, collect(c.id) AS ids UNWIND ids AS id RETURN id"
Type mismatch: expected Map, Node, Edge, Datetime, Date, Time, Duration, Null, or Point but was Integer
```

Nothing is written.

## Expected

One row, `id = 'c1'`, with nodes `A{a1}`, `B{b1}`, `C{c1}` created (Neo4j / openCypher semantics).

## Conditions observed while reducing it

The query succeeds if any one of these is changed:
- the earlier counts are not carried as grouping keys (`WITH count(*) AS c1`, then `WITH collect(c.id) AS ids`);
- the final `UNWIND ids AS id` is dropped and `ids` returned directly;
- the first segment is a plain `UNWIND` with no `MERGE`.

## Workaround

Do not carry the counts forward:

```
UNWIND $rows0 AS r0 MERGE (a:A {id: r0.id}) WITH count(*) AS c0 UNWIND $rows1 AS r1 MERGE (b:B {id: r1.id}) WITH count(*) AS c1 UNWIND $rows2 AS r2 MERGE (c:C {id: r2.id}) WITH collect(c.id) AS ids UNWIND ids AS id RETURN id
```

returns `c1` and creates the three nodes.

issues.title: Arithmetic expressions combining a forwarded variable and an aggregate function (e.g., c1 * count(*)) silently evaluate to null
issues.body:
**Version**
FalkorDB 6.0.2 Latest

**Environment**
Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS x86_64

**Bug Description**
In FalkorDB, when a query forwards a scalar variable from a WITH clause and uses it in a binary arithmetic expression alongside an aggregate function in the RETURN clause (e.g., RETURN c1 * count(*)), the engine fails to compute the mathematical result. Instead of calculating the product or throwing a syntax error (as strict parsers like Neo4j do), FalkorDB silently evaluates the expression to null (nil).


**To Reproduce**
```
// 1. Setup two disjoint components
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n"
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (v1:C1 {id: 1}), (v2:C1 {id: 2}), (v3:C1 {id: 3}), (v1)-[:E]->(v2), (v2)-[:E]->(v3), (v3)-[:E]->(v1)"
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g "CREATE (v4:C2 {id: 4}), (v5:C2 {id: 5}), (v6:C2 {id: 6}), (v4)-[:E]->(v5), (v5)-[:E]->(v6), (v6)-[:E]->(v4)"

// 2. Query mixing forwarded variable `c1` and aggregate `count(*)` (BUG: Returns nil)
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (a:C1)-[:E*2]->(b:C1) WITH count(*) AS c1 MATCH (x:C2)-[:E*2]->(y:C2) RETURN c1 * count(*) AS isolated_product"
1) 1) "isolated_product"
2) 1) 1) (nil)

// 3. Verifying normal aggregation works (Returns 9 as expected)
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (a:C1)-[:E*2]->(b:C1) WITH count(*) AS c1 MATCH (x:C2)-[:E*2]->(y:C2) RETURN sum(c1) AS isolated_product"
1) 1) "isolated_product"
2) 1) 1) "9"

```

**Expected Behavior**
If the parser accepts the syntax, the engine must correctly evaluate 3 * 3 and return 9 (which is what Memgraph does). Alternatively, it should throw a syntax violation error during parsing (which is what Neo4j does). Silently returning null (nil) for a valid numerical calculation constitutes an execution bug.

**Cross-engine comparison**

```
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUERY g "MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n"
1) 1) "Cached execution: 0"
   2) "Query internal execution time: 0.145559 milliseconds"
   3) "Graph version: 1"
127.0.0.1:6379> GRAPH.QUER

## 🕵️ Root Cause Analysis (RCA)
**Summary (tl;dr)**
FalkorDB keeps full copies of records **after** executing `DELETE`. The `Delete` execution operator forwards those stale records up the pipeline, and `GraphEntity_GetProperty` does **not** verify whether the underlying graph entity has been deleted. As a result, projections such as `RETURN n.k1` read the property from an in-memory `Node` struct that has already been removed from the graph store, instead of throwing an error.

### Root Cause
1. **Execution-plan behaviour** – In `src/execution_plan/ops/op_delete.c`, the `DeleteConsume` routine (≈ lines 220-255) first buffers its child records, invokes `_DeleteEntities` to physically remove nodes/edges, _then_ re-emits those same (pre-delete) records to its parent operator. 
2. **Missing guard in entity accessors** – `src/graph/entities/graph_entity.c` (`GraphEntity_GetProperty`) simply dereferences the attribute set; it never checks `GraphEntity_IsDeleted(e)`

#### 📋 Summary of Root Cause
`SET` (and similarly `REMOVE`) clauses in FalkorDB validate only that the left-hand side (LHS) is an *identifier*, but **do not verify that this identifier refers to a graph entity (node or relationship)**. Named path aliases are recorded in the validator with no type information, allowing them to pass unchanged through planning and execution. At runtime the engine resolves the alias to the first record slot of the path and silently performs the property update, so a query like:
```cypher

SET p.k1 = 1
RETURN n;

executes instead of failing, in contradiction to Cypher semantics where paths cannot hold properties.

### 🛠 Root-Cause Analysis (RCA) & Fix Proposal

**Issue:** Non-deterministic queries like
```cypher
WITH random() AS r WHERE r > 0.8 CREATE ()
```
are replicated by re-executing the original query text on replicas. Because `random()` is evaluated independently per host, primaries and replicas can diverge (some create a node, others don’t), leading to **data inconsistency**.

---
#### 1. Root Cause
1. **`random()` re-evaluated per replica**  
   • Implemented by `AR_RAND` (`src/arithmetic/numeric_funcs/numeric_funcs.c`, ~L102-110) calling C `rand()`; every process has its own RNG state.
2. **Replication path ignores determinism**  
   • After execution, `cmd_query.c::_should_replicate_effects` decides whether to ship a deterministic *effect log* or merely replicate the original `GRAPH.QUERY` text.  
   • Decision is based **only on execution time** vs. `EFFECTS_THRESHOLD` (300 µs, see `src/configuration/config.c`, ~L260).  
   • Fast queries therefore replica

[MAJOR]: `AR_AggFuncDescNew` now hardcodes `desc->deterministic` inside the constructor, but there is still no way for aggregates such as `COLLECT` (which are inherently non-deterministic) to flip the flag. If the planner/execution code starts trusting this field we will mislabel every aggregate as deterministic and enable unsafe rewrites. Please extend the constructor (and callers) with a deterministic parameter or provide a follow-up setter so that only the truly non-deterministic aggregates mark the flag false.

[MINOR]: The inline comment for the `reducible` argument still hints that reducibility implies determinism, even though a dedicated `deterministic` flag has just been added. This can easily lead future maintainers to conflate the two properties. Suggested fix: rephrase the `reducible` comment in terms of constant-foldability/static evaluation and reference determinism separately to avoid confusion.

[MAJOR]: `AR_DISTINCT` keeps a Set of previously seen values (see `DistinctCtx` and `Distinct_PrivateData`), so its result depends on the evaluation history, not only on its inputs. Marking the registration as deterministic allows the planner to cache or reorder it assuming stateless behavior, which can return incorrect results. Please set the deterministic flag for DISTINCT to `false` (as it was effectively treated before) so the engine knows it is stateful.

```bash
id=$(docker create --platform=linux/${{ matrix.platform.arch }} localhost:5000/falkordb/falkordb-compiler-${{ matrix.platform.suffix }})

```

2. `src/util/arr.h` lines 62-77 – `array_new_sz` allocates a header + buffer but only returns the buffer pointer; allocator APIs act on the header.
3. `src/util/arr.h` lines 238-244 – `array_free` converts `arr` to `array_hdr(arr)` before `rm_free`, confirming allocator contract.

**Impact**
Any attribute stored as array or map is subject to corruption when Redis’ act

[BLOCKER]: Defrag resets shared attribute flag
Converting the attribute to an `SIValue` and then calling `_AttrValueFromSIValue(attr, &v)` after `Map_Defrag`/`SIArray_Defrag` rewrites `attr->t` without re‑applying the shared bit that might have been set on the original attribute. Any attribute that was marked shared (e.g. copied between different attribute sets) will lose that flag, so both owners will now think they own the underlying map/array and attempt to free it, causing a double‑free after defrag relocates the buffer.

## 🛠 Root Cause Analysis & Fix Proposal

### 🐞 Root Cause
During Redis background persistence (`BGSAVE`, AOF rewrite, replication sync) the server `fork()`-s a child.  The FalkorDB module’s *child-side* `pthread_atfork` handler (`RG_AfterForkChild`) immediately:
1. Calls GraphBLAS (`GxB_set`) – guarded by OpenMP global locks (`GB_Global.lock[]`).
2. Iterates all registered graphs via `Globals` helpers – protected by FalkorDB’s own RW-lock (`_globals.lock`).

Both lock families are **inherited in the same state they had in the parent**.  If any parent thread was holding one of these locks when the fork happened, the child observes the lock as already *owned* and blocks forever.  The child therefore never reaches the RDB writing loop → `BGSAVE` hangs exactly as reported.

### 🔍 Evidence
* `src/module_event_handlers.c`  ‑ `RG_AfterForkChild` (≈ L560-590) – executed right after `fork`, before Redis background save code.
* `src/globals.c` ‑ `_globals.lock` decl

## 🕵️ Root Cause Analysis (RCA)

### Root Cause
FalkorDB’s `CREATE` execution path does **not** bound or validate the number of relationships it attempts to materialize. For a query like:
```cypher
MATCH (a:Victim), (b:Victim) CREATE (a)-[:AA]->(b)
```
the planner produces a Cartesian product of the matched node sets (|a| × |b|). The `Create` operator (`src/execution_plan/ops/op_create.c`) adds **every** of these pairs (10¹² in the PoC) to its pending-edge arrays. During `CommitNewEntities` (`src/execution_plan/ops/shared/create_functions.c`) it then unconditionally invokes `Graph_AllocateEdges`, which asks the storage layer to reserve space for all pending edges and to set Boolean entries in the adjacency matrices via GraphBLAS. Attempting to allocate trillions of edges immediately exhausts memory and crashes the Redis/FalkorDB process before any timeout or guard can intervene.

### 🕵️ Root Cause Analysis (RCA)
<!-- overcut:rca:done -->

**Summary**
`GRAPH.MEMORY USAGE` currently *over-estimates* the memory occupied by properties that hold **interned strings**.  The command samples node/edge attribute sets and, for every string-like property, adds the full `strlen()` of the payload.  Interned strings, however, are stored **once** in the global string-pool and each property keeps only a *pointer* to that shared buffer.  Because the estimator does not special–case the `ATTR_TYPE_INTERN_STRING` type, it counts the same bytes for every occurrence, so graphs that use `intern()` appear just as large as those that do not—even though the real allocator holds only one copy.

Importantly, list operations such as `list.dedup`, `list.reduce`, or concatenation **do not de-intern** their elements.  Interned `SIValue`s remain interned throughout these functions, so the issue is confined to the reporting logic, not to string pooling itself.

### 🐞 Root Cause Analysis (RCA)

**Root cause**
The `release-image.yml` and `release-ramp.yml` GitHub Action workflows set the environment variable `COMMIT_SHA` to `github.event.release.target_commitish` when they are triggered by a GitHub Release.  Unfortunately, `target_commitish` usually contains only a branch or tag *name* (e.g. `master` or `v1.7.0`) rather than the 40-character commit hash of the exact commit that produced the build artifacts.  

Every artifact-download step later passes this value to `dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v11`, which expects an exact commit SHA to locate the corresponding *Build* workflow run. Because the value is not a real SHA, the download action fails and the entire release pipeline aborts, preventing Docker images, shared libraries and RAMP bundles from being published.

#### 📝 Summary of Root Cause
FalkorDB 4.16.0 crashes when a query **deletes nodes/edges and then continues to reference the same aliases later in the pipeline** (e.g., via `WITH *`, `WHERE`, or `RETURN`).

1. `OpDelete` (`src/execution_plan/ops/op_delete.c`) collects incoming records, performs the physical delete (which frees the entities’ attribute sets) and then **returns those same, now-invalid records to its parent operator**.

3. The reporter’s note that the crash disappears when the query runs against an empty map aligns with this hypothesis – if no entities are matched, no deleted entity is dereferenced.

### 🛠 Root Cause Analysis (RCA)

#### Root Cause Summary
`SET n:Label` (and any other clause that adds/removes labels) is executed inside `CommitUpdates` (`src/execution_plan/ops/shared/update_functions.c`).  At the start of this routine the graph’s matrix policy is **always switched to `SYNC_POLICY_NOP`**, disabling automatic growth ("synchronisation") of matrices.  When a label that was created while the graph was small is later assigned to a **much higher node ID** (e.g., 49 152), the corresponding *per-label matrix* and the *node-label matrix* have not been resized.  The subsequent write therefore targets a position beyond the matrix bounds and GraphBLAS throws a dimension-mismatch error.

#### Evidence
1. **Policy forced to NOP in CommitUpdates**  
   `update_functions.c` (≈L55):
   ```c
   MATRIX_POLICY policy = Graph_GetMatrixPolicy(gc->g);
   Graph_SetMatrixPolicy(gc->g, SYNC_POLICY_NOP);   // <-- disables resizing
   ...
   GraphHub_UpdateNodeLabels

[MAJOR]: Both replication flows call `self.master.wait(1, 0)` before interrogating the replica. A WAIT timeout of 0 returns immediately, so these tests can hit the replica before `SET`/`REMOVE` updates have been propagated, meaning the assertions never actually verify that the label-matrix resize propagated. This undermines the purpose of the tests and can make them flaky.

Suggestion: Invoke WAIT with a real timeout (e.g., a few seconds) and assert the return value is ≥ 1 before issuing any replica reads (apply to both WAIT calls in these flows).

### 🛠 Root Cause Analysis (RCA)

**Root cause (summary)**
`startNode()` / `endNode()` arithmetic functions assume the source and destination nodes of an edge still exist. After a `DETACH DELETE`, the node is physically removed from the `DataBlock`. Subsequent calls to `Graph_GetNode` for that node ID fail and leave the returned `Node` object with `attributes == NULL`. ### 🛠 Root Cause Analysis (RCA)
**Root cause**  
The FalkorDB **Browser** automatically appends a default `LIMIT 300` clause when it believes a query has no explicit `LIMIT`.  Its current detection logic fails when a carriage-return / newline appears immediately after a comma in the `RETURN` list (e.g. `RETURN n0,\n    n1`).  Because of this failure the browser sends the engine the text `… LIMIT 3 LIMIT 300`, and the server-side parser rightfully raises a syntax error, which is what the user observed.

**Evidence**  
1. Parser grammar in `deps/libcypher-parser/lib/src/parser.leg` allows newlines after commas, so the query itself is valid Cypher.  
2. Error message includes `... LIMIT 3 LIMIT 300 ...`, proving two `LIMIT` tokens reached the server.  
3. FalkorDB core never injects textual `LIMIT`s – enforcement is procedural (`src/execution_plan/ops/op_results.c`).  Therefore the second `LIMIT` must originate in the browser UI.

**Impacted component**: Falkor

[MAJOR]: GraphEntity_GetAttributes now returns NULL but callers still dereference.

**Issue**: GraphEntity_GetAttributes previously always returned a valid AttributeSet pointer and many existing call sites immediately dereference it (e.g., `AttributeSet_Count(entity->attributes)` in serializers, reply builders, effects logging, etc.). Returning `NULL` when `e->attributes` is missing means those sites will now dereference a null pointer whenever a deleted or never-initialized entity is processed, crashing the engine.

**Suggested fix**: Either keep the prior behavior (return the dereferenced AttributeSet even when empty) or update all callers—EffectsBuffer_WriteAttributeSet, GraphHub commitments, serializers, memory accounting, Bolt/JSON reply builders, and any `AttributeSet_*` use sites—to tolerate NULL safely before merging this change.

[IMPORTANCE]: major — Compact clients rely on the protocol guarantee that each property is encoded as a triplet (type, attribute id, value). Replying with a zero-length array when `set == NULL` means the stream lacks those triplets, so clients misinterpret the next values and desynchronize or crash. Consider emitting a sentinel triplet (e.g. `VALUE_UNKNOWN, 0, NULL`) or preserving the previous structure so the property count and tuple boundaries stay consistent.

[MAJOR]: **Delta_Matrix_synchronize can return uninitialized info** — When the preliminary dimension/dirty checks short‑circuit, the function now returns before entering the locked section, but for the remaining flow it falls through to `return info` without guaranteeing `info` has been set to a success code; the variable is declared without initialization and the earlier success path never assigns it. Any successful execution that doesn’t hit a `GrB_RETURN_IF_FAIL` path could therefore return an indeterminate value. **Suggested fix:** Initialize `info` to `GrB_SUCCESS` when declared (or ensure every path assigns it) so the final return value is well defined.

[IMPORTANCE]: major  
**Matrix sync policy ignores failure**  
`_MatrixSynchronize` now returns `bool`, but the public accessors that call through `g->SynchronizeMatrix` (e.g. `Graph_GetRelationMatrix`, `Graph_GetLabelMatrix`, `Graph_GetNodeLabelMatrix`, `Graph_GetZeroMatrix`) still drop the return value. If `Delta_Matrix_synchronize` fails (OOM, resize failure, etc.) those helpers continue returning stale/undersized matrices, so the new error propagation contract is still bypassed.  
**Suggested fix:** Check the boolean return from `g->SynchronizeMatrix` in every accessor (or have them propagate an error) and abort/propagate when synchronization fails instead of ignoring it.

[MAJOR]: Fork prepare check compiled out in release

The new Graph_Synced verification in _ForkPrepare uses ASSERT, but ASSERT expands to a no-op in production builds, so the parent never actually halts or reports a dirty graph before forking. That means Redis can still spawn a child with unsynchronized matrices even though the change was meant to ensure the parent enforces a clean state.

**Suggested fix:** Replace the debug-only ASSERT with a runtime check that logs and aborts (or returns an error to Redis) when Graph_Synced fails so BGSAVE never starts from an inconsistent graph.

[MAJOR]: Fork child ignores sync failure

Both `Graph_Synced` checks in `_AfterForkChild` only log warnings when a graph is dirty and then let the save continue, so the child still emits an inconsistent RDB despite the parent failing to synchronize. The fork should abort once a graph fails `Graph_Synced` to avoid corrupt persistence.

**Suggested fix:** After logging the failure, terminate the child process (e.g. `_Exit(1)`/`RedisModule_KillForkChild`) so Redis cancels the BGSAVE when any graph isn’t synchronized.

## 🔍 Root Cause Summary
When `GRAPH.COPY src dest` runs, the forked **child process** (responsible for serialising the graph) *renames* the **live** `GraphContext` of the *source* graph to the destination name **inside the child** (`src/commands/cmd_copy.c`, lines ~181-188).

That `GraphContext` object is shared via the module-wide registry `_globals.graphs_in_keyspace`.  Renaming it alters the global bookkeeping (graph name → context mapping and telemetry key names) while the parent process – which still holds other graphs – remains active.  With >1 graph present, the registry becomes inconsistent and the child exits with status 1, propagating `copy failed` to the client.

After `_ReduceFilterToOp` returns, `ExecutionPlan_ReduceFilterToApply` frees the original filter, which frees `filter_root` as well. **Summary**
The intermittent hang in the `graph_copy` CI test is caused by a deadlock in `GRAPH.COPY`’s internal `_Graph_Copy` routine. When Redis temporarily refuses to fork (`RedisModule_Fork` returns `< 0`, common while another background save is running), the cron thread that initiated the copy:

3. **Never unlocks the GIL during the sleep**.

**Summary of Root Cause**
FalkorDB statically links RediSearch’s internal hash-table implementation (`src/util/dict.*`) into the module `falkordb.so`. `FALKORDB_VERSION_SCRIPT` is built from `CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR`, which points at the *top-level* source dir and can be wrong if this project is included via `add_subdirectory` (or if the top-level CMake changes). Since you already compute `root` from `CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR`, prefer using that (or `CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR`) for the path. Also, silently skipping the version script when the file isn’t found weakens the safety guarantee—consider failing the configure/build when the script is missing so we don’t accidentally ship a vulnerable binary.
```suggestion
    set(FALKORDB_VERSION_SCRIPT "${root}/src/falkordb.ver")
    if(NOT EXISTS "${FALKORDB_VERSION_SCRIPT}")
        message(FATAL_ERROR
            "FalkorDB version script not found at ${FALKORDB_VERSION_SCRIPT}. "
            "This script is required to hide internal dict* symbols and avoid Redis 8.x ABI issues.")
    endif()
    target_link_options(falkordb PRIVATE
        -Wl,--version-script=${FALKORDB_VERSION_SCRIPT})
```

The post-build verification can give false positives: if `nm -D` fails (tool missing, unsupported flag, or can’t read the binary), the pipeline produces no output and the script prints `OK` anyway. It also only matches `T/B/D` symbol types and won’t catch exported `W/V/R` or even an undefined `U dict*` (which would also bind to Redis at runtime). Consider using `${CMAKE_NM}` (or another CMake-detected tool) and making the command fail if the symbol listing step fails, and match any `dict` dynamic symbol regardless of type.
```suggestion
        COMMAND /bin/sh -c "tmp=\"$(mktemp)\"; if ! ${CMAKE_NM} -D \"$<TARGET_FILE:falkordb>\" >\"$tmp\" 2>/dev/null; then echo 'ERROR: Failed to list dynamic symbols for falkordb (nm -D via CMAKE_NM failed).' >&2; rm -f \"$tmp\"; exit 2; fi; if grep -q ' dict' \"$tmp\"; then echo 'ERROR: dict* symbols are dynamically exported — Redis 8.x ABI crash risk!' >&2; rm -f \"$tmp\"; exit 1; else echo 'OK: dict* symbols are hidden'; rm -f \"$tmp\"; fi"
```

Hi @splendorLee,
Let me try and explain why you're seeing this behavior,

FalkorDB recycles graph entity IDs, the query:
`CREATE (n {payload: 123}) WITH [n] AS list DETACH DELETE list[0] WITH list UNWIND range(1, 100) AS i CREATE (:Filler {val: 0xDEADBEEF}) RETURN list[0].val`

Creates a new node, let's assume its ID is 4, now that node is added to an array `list` so `list[0] == node with ID 4`
Next up the query deletes that node, putting node ID 4 in the recycle bin, the 100 iteration loop creates 100 new nodes, but the fist node created will be assign ID 4. **No client reply when the graph doesn't exist — blocked client can hang forever.**

When `gc == NULL`, both `_Constraint_Drop` and `_Constraint_Create` return `false` without ever calling `RedisModule_ReplyWith*`. This branch is easily reachable for `_Constraint_Drop` on the regular (non-force-retrieve) path: `GraphContext_Retrieve` is called with `create=false`, so dropping a constraint on a graph key that doesn't exist yields `gc == NULL`.

Since a regular client command runs through `Async_Constraint_Op`, which unconditionally calls `RedisModule_UnblockClient(bc, NULL)` after `Constraint_Op` returns, a `false` result with no reply ever sent means the client never receives a response and will hang. Note this doesn't affect the sync (AOF/replication) path since there's no client waiting there, and it's already flagged by the adjacent TODO — but the plain client-facing case still needs a reply.

`build/graphblas/PreJIT/*.c` is autogenerated — `gen_prejit.sh` harvests whatever SuiteSparse's runtime JIT emitted, and CLAUDE.md forbids hand-editing or locally patching these files precisely because a hand-written `defn[]` entry desynchronises the kernel from the `_query` hash GraphBLAS checks at load time. A mismatch there is not a crash: GraphBLAS silently rejects the PreJIT kernel and falls back to a generic one, i.e. hand-patching `defn[4]` would cost the speedup this PR is adding.

Whether the thunk's user definition belongs in `defn[4]` for a `GrB_IndexUnaryOp` whose y-type is a user type is a question for SuiteSparse's `GB_jitifyer`, not for the harvest. Every kernel here was produced by the same generator in the Linux toolchain image, and the harvest is evidenced as neutral: all 151 kernels common to the old and new sets are byte-identical.

## CodeQL: PreJIT kernels excluded, one manual step needed at merge

`main` was on CodeQL **default setup** (confirmed via API: `actions, c-cpp, python, rust`, `extended` suite, weekly). Default setup cannot exclude a path — `paths-ignore` is only read from a config file, and a config file is only read by advanced setup. So the generated kernels were being scanned as if hand-written.

`9d24d2d0` migrates this branch to advanced setup:

- `.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml` — `paths-ignore: build/graphblas/PreJIT/**`, plus `security-extended` to match the suite default setup was configured with.
- `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` — same four languages, same weekly cadence, all `build-mode: none`. Buildless matters beyond speed: `paths-ignore` only applies to codebases analysed without a build, so a build mode would silently drop the exclusion.

`master`'s own `codeql-analysis.yml` is branch-filtered to `master` and the release branches, so the two configurations never overlap.

### Require

`strip_empty` removes the wrong separator when dropping an empty middle child. `Branch` documents `seps[i] == min(children[i+1])`; removing `children[i]` should update separators so they remain the minima of the new right children. As written, removing `seps[i]` (for non-last) leaves `seps[i-1]` pointing at the removed child's min, which can break routing assumptions in later batch operations.

A robust fix is to drop all empty children first, then recompute `seps` from the remaining children minima.

`assert_first_doc_matches` uses `k + 1`, which will panic on overflow in debug builds if a test ever includes `u64::MAX` as a key (and it already explicitly probes `first_doc(u64::MAX)`). Use `wrapping_add(1)` to keep the neighbor-probe logic total over `u64`.

`heap_bytes()` is intended to approximate resident heap usage, but it uses `len()` for the `Vec` fields, which can substantially undercount when `capacity() > len()` (common after splits/merges). For heap allocation size, use `capacity()` (and consider including the `Branch` struct itself).

`from_sorted` currently only const-asserts `LEAF_MAX`/`BRANCH_MAX`. Because `DOC_BYTES` is a public const generic and is used as an AoS doc width, unsupported values (0, 3, >8) can lead to panics/mis-decodes later. Add a `DOC_BYTES` constraint to the const-assert in `from_sorted` so invalid monomorphizations fail to compile.

Fix opened in #2500.

**Root cause:** the `fuse_anonymous_traverse` optimizer pass collapses two stacked `CondTraverse` ops into one fused hop when the intermediate node is anonymous and unreferenced. The runtime executes a fused chain as a **boolean** matrix product, so the result records whether a destination is *reachable*, not how many distinct paths reach it — the two 2-hop paths across the diamond collapse into a single row.

**Fix:** restrict fusion to plans where row multiplicity is unobservable, i.e. under the existence branch (child 1) of a `SemiApply`/`AntiSemiApply`. Pattern predicates keep the optimization; a plain `MATCH` no longer fuses and now reports the correct cardinality.

## 1. The symbol collision was eliminated upstream by renaming, not by hiding

FalkorDB's RediSearch fork renamed **all 33 dict functions** to an `rs_` prefix (`rs_dictCreate`, `rs_dictAdd`, `rs_dictFind`, `rs_dictDelete`, …). This is present in the RediSearch submodule commit currently pinned on `master` (`311f901265edda45e4bf84c948d91dd34ed8ec11`, `src/util/dict.h`).

Verified empirically against the shipped `falkordb.so` from `falkordb/falkordb:latest` (module ver 42003 / v4.20.3):

```
# bare dict* function symbols dynamically exported (the #1642 root cause)
$ nm -D falkordb.so | grep -E '^[0-9a-f]+ [TBDWV] dict(Create|Add|Find|Delete|Replace|Release)'
(none)

# rs_dict* symbols exported (the upstream fix)
$ nm -D falkordb.so | grep -cE '^[0-9a-f]+ [TBDWV] rs_dict'
32

# undefined dict* references that Redis could interpose
$ nm -D falkordb

Fixed by #1670 (merged to `master` on 2026-03-08), which bumped the `deps/RediSearch` submodule to pull in FalkorDB/RediSearch#22 — *"add a rs_ prefix to dict functions"*.

## Root cause and fix

The fix was applied at the source rather than at the linker: RediSearch's internal dict API was **renamed**, so it no longer shares symbol names with Redis's dict API at all. With no name collision, there is nothing for the Redis 8.x dynamic linker to interpose, and the `dictType` layout mismatch (12+ fields vs 6) can no longer occur.

`accepted_expressions_stay_within_the_cap` silently skips expressions that fail to parse (`continue` on `Err`). That means the test won’t catch regressions where the depth guard becomes overly eager (rejecting valid expressions) or where these expressions start failing for reasons other than the depth cap. It’s safer to assert that any failure here is specifically a "too deep" error.

In `parse_expr_return!`, the branch that sets the frame’s initial height (`Some((_, expr, h))`) doesn’t call `check_depth`. Today most call sites check before invoking the macro, but having the macro enforce the invariant in both branches makes it harder to accidentally bypass the cap in future edits.

returns **1** once an index exists on `:N(v)`, and **0** without the index. Cypher's `true` and `1` are distinct values of distinct types, so the indexed answer is wrong and, worse, disagrees with the unindexed answer — creating an index changes query results.

This test assumes the `RENAME` happens before the flusher writes the queued entry, but nothing enforces that ordering. If the client round-trips take > FLUSH_LINGER (5ms), the flusher can write to telemetry{before} before the rename, and the rename will delete the stream—making the test flaky. Sending `GRAPH.QUERY` and `RENAME` back-to-back in a pipeline reduces client delay and makes the “in-flight rename” scenario deterministic.

`resolve_current_names` runs before the flusher acquires the GIL, so a concurrent `RENAME` can re-key `GRAPH_REGISTRY` between name resolution and the eventual write. In that interleaving, `key_holds_graph` will reject the old key and the entry will be dropped instead of following the renamed graph. Re-resolve names under the GIL right before sorting/writing to close this race window.

_🩺 Stability & Availability_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Remove the timing dependence between the query and the `RENAME`.**

The flusher wakes every 5ms and lingers 5ms (`FLUSH_INTERVAL` and `FLUSH_LINGER` in `src/telemetry.rs`). If the entry is flushed before the `RENAME` command arrives, it lands in `telemetry{before}`, the rename deletes that stream, and nothing remains in flight. `pollUntil` then fails after its 30s timeout.

Make the test deterministic. One option is to set `CMD_INFO no`, run the query, rename, then set `CMD_INFO yes`; that is not possible here because the entry must already be queued. A simpler option is to accept both outcomes: assert that exactly one entry exists under the current key, and that `telemetry{before}` is absent, without requiring the write to happen after the rename.

This rewrite prunes `child_idx` and reattaches its children, but `child_idx` is only guaranteed to *contain* a planner scan (via `planner_scan_alias`), not to *be* the `AllNodeScan`/`NodeByLabelScan` node. The planner can wrap the scan in `Filter` (inline attrs) (see `graph/src/planner/mod.rs:1803-1814`) or `IncludePending` (see `is_planner_scan_subtree` docs in this file). In those cases this block would prune the wrapper (dropping semantics like inline-attr filtering / IncludePending) and still leave the scan in place, so it can both change results and fail to remove the redundant scan.

A safe minimal fix is to only apply the “drop scan” splice when `child_idx` is directly the scan node; otherwise, leave the plan unchanged (or implement a deeper splice that removes the scan leaf while preserving wrappers).

The destination formula for non-probe pairs uses `s = i % ROWS` and `d = (i * 7 + 3) % ROWS`. Because `i` advances by multiples of `ROWS` for the same `s`, `(i * 7 + 3) % ROWS` is constant per row, so row length does *not* grow with `pairs` (and many inserts collapse into repeated `(src,dst)` pairs). This contradicts the fixture described in the doc comment/README and can invalidate the measured shape.

Make `d` depend on a per-row counter (e.g. `j = i / ROWS`) so each `src` gets more distinct `dst`s as `pairs` grows.

For the non-probe pairs, `a` is `ns[i%1000]` and `b` is `ns[(i*7+3)%1000]`. For any fixed source `i % 1000 == s`, `i` differs by multiples of 1000, so `(i*7+3) % 1000` is constant; this means each source repeatedly connects to the same destination and the number of *distinct* populated pairs does not grow as intended.

To make adjacency rows lengthen with `pairs`, incorporate a per-row counter such as `toInteger(i/1000)` into the destination expression.

When the multi-edge id matrix carries **any** pending entries, a multi-edge row read consults the delta layer instead of reading the committed base alone. That costs a flat **~1,200 instructions per read**, and flat is literal — one pending id costs what eight thousand do.

The `f64` coercion isn't a storage decision — it's what keeps the index agreeing with the evaluator.

`Value::compare_value` treats the two cases differently:

```rust
(Int(a), Int(b))   => a.cmp(b)                      // exact i64
(Int(i), Float(f)) => compare_floats(*i as f64, *f) // promotes
```

So in Cypher as this engine implements it, `Int(2^53+1) = Float(2^53)` is **true** — the language itself rounds the int for mixed comparison. The index has to reproduce that, and encoding through `f64` is how.

A false positive can be post-filtered; a row the index never returns cannot be recovered.

The new textual anchoring in `graph/src/runtime/functions/internal.rs` (`\\A(?:<pattern>)\\z`) can invalidate an otherwise valid regex. For example, in `(?x)a#comment`, verbose mode treats the remainder of the line as a comment, including the generated closing group and anchor.
